§ 4.2.2 Fundamental Properties of Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz

This paragraph details the fundamental properties of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} which will be used throughout this paper.

Theorem 4.2.2.1.

Let LL be a number field, let C/LC/L and X/LX/L be as above (§ 2.4) and an Initial Theta Data § 3.1, § 3.3 be fixed. Then the set Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} constructed above (4.2.3) has the following properties. Let 𝐆L′\mathbf{G}_{L^{\prime}} be the group defined in [Joshi, 2023a, § ] (for L′L^{\prime}). Let Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} be the set constructed above.

  1. (1)

    The set Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} is stable under the natural action of 𝐆L′\mathbf{G}_{L^{\prime}} on (𝐘𝐋′′)ℓ∗\left(\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}\right)^{\ell^{*}} which is given using the natural action of 𝐆L′\mathbf{G}_{L^{\prime}} on 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} (constructed in [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ]).

  2. (2)

    The set Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} is stable under the natural action of the (global) Frobenius 𝝋\boldsymbol{\varphi} on (𝐘𝐋′′)ℓ∗\left(\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}\right)^{\ell^{*}} given using the natural action of the (global) Frobenius 𝝋\boldsymbol{\varphi} on 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}.

  3. (3)

    Hence Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} is also stable under the natural action of (L′)∗(L^{\prime})^{*} on 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} constructed in [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ].

  4. (4)

    Let (𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)∈Σ~L′({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}, write, for j=1,2,…,ℓ∗j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}, 𝐲j′=(yj,w′)w∈𝕍L′{\bf y}_{j}^{\prime}=(y^{\prime}_{j,w})_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}. For each w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}. Let

    (yw,1′,yw,2′,…,yw,ℓ∗′)∈Yℂp♭,Lw′ℓ∗(y^{\prime}_{w,1},y^{\prime}_{w,2},\ldots,y^{\prime}_{w,{\ell^{*}}})\in{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}}

    be the ww-component of (𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)({\bf y}_{1}^{\prime},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime}). Let Kw,1′,Kw,2′,…,Kw,ℓ∗′K_{w,1}^{\prime},K_{w,2}^{\prime},\ldots,K_{w,{\ell^{*}}}^{\prime} be the residue fields of yw,1′,yw,2′,…,yw,ℓ∗′y^{\prime}_{w,1},y^{\prime}_{w,2},\ldots,y^{\prime}_{w,{\ell^{*}}} in Yℂp♭,Lw′{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}} respectively. Then one has the following relationship between their valuations

    (4.2.2.2) |−|Kyw,j′=|−|Kyw,1′j2 for j=1,2,…,ℓ∗.\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{w,j}^{\prime}}}=\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{w,1}^{\prime}}}^{j^{2}}\text{ for }j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}.
  5. (5)

    Moreover for each w∈𝕍L′−𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}-\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss} one has the following relationship between their valuations:

    (4.2.2.3) |−|Kyw,j′=|−|Kyw,1′ for j=1,2,…,ℓ∗.\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{w,j}^{\prime}}}=\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{w,1}^{\prime}}}\text{ for }j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}.

Proof.

The first assertion is a consequence of [Joshi, 2023b, Proposition ] and [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ]. The second assertion (2) is immediate from [Joshi, 2023b, Proposition ] and [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ].

Let me give a proof of (3). This can be proved along the lines of [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ], but let me deduce the present case as a consequence of [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ]. To see this, let w|pw|p. Then one has a quasi-finite morphism (4.2.1.2) Yℂp♭,Lw′→Yℂp♭,ℚp{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}. Let yp,j∈Yℂp♭,ℚpy_{p,j}\in{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} be the image of yw,j′y_{w,j}^{\prime} under this morphism and let (yp,1,yp,2,…,yp,ℓ∗)∈Σ~ℂp♭⊂Yℂp♭,ℚpℓ∗(y_{p,1},y_{p,2},\ldots,y_{p,{\ell^{*}}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}}\subset{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}^{\ell^{*}} be the corresponding point of Yℂp♭,ℚpℓ∗{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}^{\ell^{*}}.

In [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ], I have shown that (4.2.2.2) holds for the residue fields Kyp,1,Kyp,2,…,Kyp,ℓ∗K_{y_{p,1}},K_{y_{p,2}},\ldots,K_{y_{p,{\ell^{*}}}} of yp,1,yp,2,…,yp,ℓ∗y_{p,1},y_{p,2},\ldots,y_{p,{\ell^{*}}}. By [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Proposition 2.3.20(3)] one has an isomorphism of local rings of yp,jy_{p,j} and yw,j′y^{\prime}_{w,j} for each jj. Hence (4.2.2.2) also holds for the residue fields Kyw,1′,Kyw,2′,…,Kyw,ℓ∗′K_{y_{w,1}^{\prime}},K_{y_{w,2}^{\prime}},\ldots,K_{y_{w,{\ell^{*}}^{\prime}}} of yw,1′,yw,2′,…,yw,ℓ∗′y^{\prime}_{w,1},y^{\prime}_{w,2},\ldots,y^{\prime}_{w,{\ell^{*}}}.

The last assertion is immediate from the definition of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}.

This completes the proof.

The scaling relationship established in Theorem 4.2.2.1 (at the primes of semi-stable reduction) has fundamental consequences for global arithmetic. Mochizuki asserts the content of the next corollary as [Mochizuki, 2021a, Theorem A(ii)]:

Corollary 4.2.2.4.

Suppose that the notations and assumptions of Theorem 4.2.2.1 remain in force. Then the non-trivial scaling relationship established by Theorem 4.2.2.1(3) at primes w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, forces that suitable (re)normalization of valuations must be introduced at primes w∈𝕍L′−𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}-\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss} so that the product formula to continue to hold for each normalized arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j′n​o​r\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}^{\prime}_{j}}^{nor} given by (𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime}).

Proof.

This is clear from Theorem 4.2.2.1 and the global constraint placed by the requirement that the product formula holds.

§ 4.2.3 Mochizuki’s Ansatz is the set of Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]

Definition 4.2.3.1.

Let (𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)∈Σ~L′({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. Then the assignment

𝐲1′⟼(𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)∈Σ~L′{\bf y}_{1}^{\prime}\longmapsto({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}

will be called a Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Link. Sometimes I will write this as

Σ~L′∋(𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)⟼𝐲ℓ∗′∈𝐘𝐋′′.\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}\ni({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})\longmapsto{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}^{\prime}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}.

Thus Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} is the set of Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-links (more precisely Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links in 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} or 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}-Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links). One may also consider Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links using variants 𝐘𝐋′𝐦′​𝐚​𝐱\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{{}^{\prime}max} and 𝐘𝐋′ℝ′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{{}^{\prime}{\mathbb{R}}} of 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} considered in [Joshi, 2023a]. ∙\bullet

Remark 4.2.3.2.
  1. (1)

    Thus a Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Link is simply a point of Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} (Definition 4.2.2).

  2. (2)

    Mochizuki’s version of Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Link is introduced in [Mochizuki, 2021c] and Mochizuki asserts in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 4.1(iv), Page 344] that it has the valuation scaling property established here as Theorem 4.2.2.1(3). This property is central to [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] and [Mochizuki, 2021d]. [Mochizuki’s Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Link was first established rigorously in [Joshi, 2023b] and the global case is Theorem 4.2.2.1(3).]

  3. (3)

    By Proposition 4.3.1, one may think of Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz as a divisorial correspondence on the adelic Fargues-Fontaine curve 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} (see [Joshi, 2023a, § ]).

∙\bullet

The following is useful in the context of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]:

Corollary 4.2.3.3.

Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} is a metrisable space with the topology and the metric induced from 𝐘𝐋′ℓ∗\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}}.

Proof.

This is immediate from [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ] as 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} is a metrisable topological space.

Remark 4.2.3.4.

In particular, for a choice of a metric on 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}, it makes sense to talk about the distance between two distinct Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links. ∙\bullet

§ 4.3 Mochizuki’s Ansatz arises from a correspondence on 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}

The following proposition is based on the notion of correspondences on 𝐘𝐋\mathscrbf{Y}_{L} considered in [Joshi, 2023a, § ]. The assertion is the following:

Proposition 4.3.1.

Each point

𝐳∈Σ~L′=(𝐲1′,𝐲2′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}=({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1},{\bf y}_{2}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}

defines a divisorial correspondence

𝐲1′⟼∑j=1ℓ∗(𝐲j′)=(𝐲1′)+(𝐲2′)+⋯+(𝐲ℓ∗′){\bf y}_{1}^{\prime}\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}({\bf y}_{j}^{\prime})=({\bf y}^{\prime}_{1})+({\bf y}_{2}^{\prime})+\cdots+({\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})

on 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} of degree ℓ∗{\ell^{*}}

Proof.

This is clear from the construction of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} given above and [Joshi, 2023a, § ].

§ 4.4 The choice of a standard point of 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L}^{\prime}

I will choose a point 𝐲0∈𝐘𝐋′{\bf y}_{0}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} (resp. 𝐲0′∈𝐘𝐋′′{\bf y}_{0}^{\prime}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}), which will be referred to as the standard point, and whose construction is detailed, for the field LL, in [Joshi, 2023a, § ] but here I work with 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} and 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} respectively. To understand what this choice entails let me set out some notation.

Let w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}} be a prime of L′L^{\prime} with w|pw|p. Let Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} be the completion of L′L^{\prime} at ww. The choice of 𝐲0=(yw)∈𝕍L′{\bf y}_{0}=(y_{w})_{\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}} (resp. 𝐲0′=(yw′)∈𝕍L′∈𝐘𝐋′′{\bf y}_{0}^{\prime}=(y_{w}^{\prime})_{\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}), is such that each yw∈YL¯^w♭′,Lw′y_{w}\in{Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}} (resp. OPENyw′∈Yℂp♭,Lw′)y_{w}^{\prime}\in{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}) is a closed classical point in the fiber of the canonical quotient morphism

YL¯^w♭′,Lw′→XL¯^w♭′,Lw′​( resp. ​Yℂp♭,Lw′→Xℂp♭,Lw′){Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{X}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}}(\textit{ resp. }{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{X}_{{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}},L_{w}^{\prime}})

such that the image of this chosen point under the composite morphism

YL¯^w♭′,Lw′→XL¯^w♭′,Lw′→Xℂp♭,ℚp​( resp. ​Yℂp♭,Lw′→Xℂp♭,Lw′).{Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{X}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}(\textit{ resp. }{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}\to{X}_{{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}},L_{w}^{\prime}}).

is the canonical point of XL¯^w♭′,ℚp(resp.Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{\widehat{\overline{L}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}(resp.{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}). (this makes sense for all w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}} by [Joshi, 2023a]).

The residue field of the local ring of ywy_{w} (resp. yw′y_{w}^{\prime}) in YL¯^w♭′,Lw′{Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}}^{{}^{\prime}\flat}_{w},L_{w}^{\prime}} (resp. in Yℂp♭,Lw′{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{w}^{\prime}}) is an algebraically closed, perfectoid field which can be naturally identified with L¯^w\widehat{\overline{L}}_{w} (resp. naturally identified with ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p}) and equipped with a natural action of GLwG_{L_{w}}. The above discussion is summarized in following:

Proposition 4.4.1.

Let 𝐲0′=(yw′)∈𝕍L′{\bf y}_{0}^{\prime}=(y_{w}^{\prime})_{\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}} be a standard point of 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}. Then for each w∈𝕍L′n​o​nw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}^{non}, the image of yw′y_{w}^{\prime} under the canonical quotient morphism 𝐘𝐋′′→𝐗𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}\to\mathscrbf{X}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} is the canonical point of 𝐗𝐋′′\mathscrbf{X}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}.

Remark 4.4.2.

Let me remark that there are countably infinite possible choices for the standard point 𝐲0{\bf y}_{0} (resp. 𝐲0′{\bf y}_{0}^{\prime}). This is because the set of valuations 𝕍L\mathbb{V}_{L} of any number field LL is countable and for each v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}, the set of possible choices of closed classical points yvy_{v} (chosen as above) is countable hence the set of 𝐲0=(yv)v∈𝕍L{\bf y}_{0}=(y_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}} as above is countable. However it is important to recognize that the choice of any of the yvy_{v}’s, and hence of 𝐲0{\bf y}_{0}, is not unique. Any one of the countably many choices for 𝐲0{\bf y}_{0} are equally valid choices (for doing arithmetic and geometry). But, as has been established in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a, Joshi, 2022], each choice sees pp-adic arithmetic (and geometry) slightly differently relative to other possible choices and so one can average over such choices. ∙\bullet

§ 4.5 The choice of a standard point of Mochizuki’s Ansatz

Now I will choose a standard point of 𝐳Θ∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} which one may think of as a standard Θ\Theta-Link (for the purposes of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]). Let 𝐳Θ=(𝐲1,𝐲2,…,𝐲ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}=({\bf y}_{1},{\bf y}_{2},\ldots,{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} be chosen such that 𝐲ℓ∗=𝐲0′∈𝐘𝐋′′{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}={\bf y}_{0}^{\prime}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} is the point standard point of 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} chosen in § 4.4.

§ 4.6 Relationship with the global arithmetic period mapping of 𝐘𝐋\mathscrbf{Y}_{L}

I want to discuss the relationship between properties of Mochizuki’s Ansatz constructed above, especially Theorem 4.2.2.1, Corollary 4.2.2.4, and the global arithmetic period mapping of 𝐘𝐋′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} constructed in [Joshi, 2023a, § ]. This relationship (Theorem 4.2.2.1 and Theorem 4.6.1) is an important, but undemonstrated point in [Mochizuki, 2021c], and the absence of proof in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], led to the denial of its existence in [Scholze and Stix, 2018, Section 2.2].

Theorem 4.6.1.

Let LL be a number field, fixed as above. Let 𝐳=(𝐲1,𝐲2,…,𝐲ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}=({\bf y}_{1},{\bf y}_{2},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. Let (𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲1,…,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲ℓ∗)(\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{1}},\ldots,\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}}) be the tuple of arithmeticoids provided by 𝐳\mathbf{z}. Consider the ℝ{\mathbb{R}}-vector space considered in [Joshi, 2023a, § ]

𝒱L,j=⨁v∈𝕍Lℝv,j,\mathcal{V}_{L,j}=\bigoplus_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}{\mathbb{R}}_{v,j},

where each ℝv,j=ℝ{\mathbb{R}}_{v,j}={\mathbb{R}} is given its usual absolute value. Then

  1. (1)

    for j=1,2,…,ℓ∗j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}, each the ideloid ℐ​𝒹​ℯ​𝓁​ℴ​𝒾​𝒹𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j\mathcal{I\!d\!e\!l\!o\!i\!d}_{\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}} provides a homomorphism of groups

    log𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j:ℐ​𝒹​ℯ​𝓁​ℴ​𝒾​𝒹𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j→𝒱L,j\log_{\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}}:\mathcal{I\!d\!e\!l\!o\!i\!d}_{\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}}\to\mathcal{V}_{L,j}

    given by

    ℐ​𝒹​ℯ​𝓁​ℴ​𝒾​𝒹𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j∋(xv)v∈𝕍L⟼(log⁡|xv|Kyv)v∈𝕍L.\mathcal{I\!d\!e\!l\!o\!i\!d}_{\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}}\ni(x_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\longmapsto(\log\left|x_{v}\right|_{K_{y_{v}}})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}.
  2. (2)

    Each normalized arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{\bf y} provides a degree homomorphism

    ℐ​𝒹​ℯ​𝓁​ℴ​𝒾​𝒹𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j→𝒱L,j→ℝ\mathcal{I\!d\!e\!l\!o\!i\!d}_{\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}}\to\mathcal{V}_{L,j}\to{\mathbb{R}}

    given by

    (xv)v∈𝕍L⟼(log⁡|xv|Kyv)v∈𝕍L⟼∑v∈𝕍Llog⁡(|xv|Kyv)=deg𝐲𝐲j⁡((xv)v∈𝕍L).(x_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\longmapsto(\log\left|x_{v}\right|_{K_{y_{v}}})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\longmapsto\sum_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\log(\left|x_{v}\right|_{K_{y_{v}}})=\deg_{{\bf y}_{{\bf y}_{j}}}((x_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}).
  3. (3)

    As a consequence, each normalized 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲n​o​r\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}}^{nor} provides a hyperplane H𝐲j⊂𝒱L,jH_{{\bf y}_{j}}\subset\mathcal{V}_{L,j} given by the logarithm of product formula equation (2.1.1) for L↪𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲jn​o​rL\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}^{nor}:

    H𝐲j:deg𝐲j⁡((x)v∈𝕍L)=∑v∈𝕍Llog⁡|x|Kyj,v=0(for all ​x∈L∗).H_{{\bf y}_{j}}:\deg_{{\bf y}_{j}}((x)_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}})=\sum_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\log\left|x\right|_{K_{y_{j,v}}}=0\qquad(\text{for all }x\in L^{*}).
  4. (4)

    The scaling of valuations by the factor j2j^{2} at primes of semi-stable reduction which occurs via Theorem 4.2.2.1, together with the requirement that the global product formula holds for 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲jn​o​r\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}^{nor}, means that the local valuations (given by an arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲j\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}) at primes of non-semistable reduction must also be suitably (re)normalized so that the product formula holds (this is given to us by Corollary 4.2.2.4).

  5. (5)

    As the product formula (2.1.1) holds for each normalized arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲jn​o​r\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{{\bf y}_{j}}^{nor}, the hyperplane H𝐲jH_{{\bf y}_{j}} is stable under multiplication by elements of L∗L^{*}.

  6. (6)

    Let ℙ⁡(𝒱L){\mathbb{P}}(\mathcal{V}_{L}) be the projective space of hyperplanes in 𝒱L\mathcal{V}_{L}. Then one has a natural and non-constant function defined on Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz (§ 4.2):

    𝐘𝐋′ℓ∗⊇𝚺~𝐋′→∏𝐣=𝟏ℓ∗ℙ⁡(𝒱𝐋,𝐣)\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}}\supseteq\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}\to\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}{\mathbb{P}}(\mathcal{V}_{L,j})

    given by Σ~L′∋𝐳=(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)⟼(H𝐲1,…,H𝐲ℓ∗)\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}\ni\mathbf{z}=({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})\longmapsto(H_{{\bf y}_{1}},\ldots,H_{{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}}).

  7. (7)

    Let ℙ⁡(Σ~L′)⊂∏j=1ℓ∗ℙ⁡(𝒱L,j){\mathbb{P}}(\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}})\subset\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}{\mathbb{P}}(\mathcal{V}_{L,j}) be the image of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} under this function. Then ℙ⁡(Σ~L′){\mathbb{P}}(\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}) is equipped with a natural action of all the groups and symmetries given by Theorem 6.3.1 which act up on Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}.

Proof.

This is clear from [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ], and the properties of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} established so far and detailed in Theorem 4.2.2.1, Corollary 4.2.2.4.

Remark 4.6.2.
  1. (1)

    I expect that the above period mapping is continuous for a suitable topology on the codomain, but I hope to take this up in a separate paper.

  2. (2)

    Mochizuki’s discussion of the role of product formulas is in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.6], [Mochizuki, 2021a, Remark 5.2.1], [Mochizuki, 2020, Page 71].

  3. (3)

    It is worth noting that in the context of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] Mochizuki considers (without a transparent proof) a version of this construction by means of the theory of realified Frobenioid ℱ​𝓇​ℴ​𝒷​(L)ℝ\mathcal{F\!r\!o\!b}(L)^{\mathbb{R}} of LL (see my discussion of this Frobenioid is in § 10). Specifically Mochizuki works with the tuple of realified Frobenioids (ℱ​𝓇​ℴ​𝒷​(L)1ℝ,…,ℱ​𝓇​ℴ​𝒷​(L)ℓ∗ℝ)(\mathcal{F\!r\!o\!b}(L)_{1}^{\mathbb{R}},\ldots,\mathcal{F\!r\!o\!b}(L)_{\ell^{*}}^{\mathbb{R}}) which provides, by the same degree mapping, the hyperplanes considered here.

  4. (4)

    The existence of the phenomenon and properties established by Theorem 4.6.1 is vital to establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. But this type of proposition is claimed without proof in [Mochizuki, 2021c], [Tan, 2018], [Yamashita, 2019]. Notably, because of the scaling property Theorem 4.2.2.1, the hyperplane H𝐲jH_{{\bf y}_{j}} comes equipped with a scaling factor of j2j^{2} (for appropriate coordinate v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L} depending on the semi-stable elliptic curve as in [Joshi, 2024b]). The lack of proof of this property in [Mochizuki, 2021c] leads to the assertions of impossibility of this phenomenon in [Scholze and Stix, 2018, Section 2.2, Page 10].

∙\bullet

5 Some local preliminaries

I will recall a few local preliminaries and constructions which are not covered in [Joshi, 2023b] but which will be used in the remainder of this paper.

Let pp be a prime. Let ℚ¯p⊃ℚp{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}\supset{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} be an algebraic closure of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. Let ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} be the completion of ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}, and equip ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} with its canonical action of the absolute Galois group GℚpG_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} (computed using ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}). The following result will be used throughout the rest of the paper.

§ 5.1 Basic rings of pp-adic Hodge Theory

For any choice of an algebraic closure ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} one has the construction of pp-adic period rings of [Fontaine, 1994a]. Let Bd​R+B_{dR}^{+} be the ring of pp-adic periods constructed in [Fontaine, 1994a] for the (Galois group, field) pair (Gℚp,ℚp)(G_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}) and let Bd​RB_{dR} be its quotient field. By the results of several mathematicians, notably, Fontaine, Messing, Faltings and Tsuji, Bd​RB_{dR} is the ring of de Rham periods of varieties finite type, and defined over finite extensions of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} contained in ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}. The construction of Bd​RB_{dR} is functorial in the sense of [Fontaine, 1994a, 1.5.6].

§ 5.2 The ring Bp=Bℂp♭,ℚpB_{p}=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}

Let Bp=Bℂp♭,ℚpB_{p}=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} be the ring constructed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Chapitre 2]; if pp is clear from the context then, I will write B=BpB=B_{p}. By [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.5.2] and [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, 10.1.1]), there exists an element t∈Bt\in B which generates the maximal ideal of the canonical point of Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}. From the point of view of modern pp-adic Hodge Theory (as detailed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018]), the ring B⁡[1t]B[\frac{1}{t}] is also quite natural. Let Bp+=Bℂp♭,ℚp+B^{+}_{p}=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}^{+} be the ring constructed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, 1.10]; if pp is clear from the context then, I will write B+=Bp+B^{+}=B_{p}^{+}.

§ 5.2.1 The ring Bp+B_{p}^{+}

Let me also remark that for the ring Bp=B=Bℂp♭,ℚpB_{p}=B=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} one has B⊃B+⊃W⁡(Oℂp♭)​[1/p]B\supset B^{+}\supset W({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}})[1/p] and W⁡(Oℂp♭)​[1/p]⊃W⁡(𝔽¯p)​[1/p]=ℚpu​n​r​a​mW({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}})[1/p]\supset W({\overline{{\mathbb{F}}}_{p}})[1/p]={\mathbb{Q}}_{p}^{unram} (this is the maximal unramified extension of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}) and so BpB_{p} and Bp+B_{p}^{+} is naturally a module for ℚpu​n​r​a​m{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}^{unram}. Hence BB and B+B^{+} are E0E_{0}-algebras for any finite unramified extension E0/ℚpE_{0}/{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. This remark will be used in what follows.

§ 5.2.2 The rings Bd​R+,Bd​RB_{dR}^{+},B_{dR}

By [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.5.2], the ring Bd​R+B_{dR}^{+} is the completion of the local ring of Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} at the canonical point of Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} and hence the ring Bd​R+B_{dR}^{+} is a discrete valuation ring. Moreover the maximal ideal of this local ring is generated by the element tt and Bd​R=Bd​R+​[1t]B_{dR}=B_{dR}^{+}[\frac{1}{t}].

Remark 5.2.2.1.

On the other hand BB has uncountably many maximal ideals corresponding to closed classical points of Yℂp♭,ℚp{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} and my construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​i{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}} and Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} require using the fact that BB has infinitely many maximal ideals. ∙\bullet

§ 5.2.3 The ring BEB_{E}

Let EE be a pp-adic field and let E0⊂EE_{0}\subset E be its maximal unramified subfield. By [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Chap 1, 1.6.2 and Chap. 10], the ring BEB_{E} associated to the datum (F=ℂp♭,E)(F={\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E) is the ring BE=Bℂp♭,EB_{E}=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E}.

Lemma 5.2.3.1.

Let EE be a pp-adic field and let E0⊂EE_{0}\subset E be the maximal unramified subfield of EE. Then one has a natural isomorphism

(5.2.3.2) BE≃Bℂp♭,ℚp⊗E0E.B_{E}\simeq B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\otimes_{E_{0}}E.

Proof.

This is [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Proposition 1.6.9].

§ 5.2.4 The rings B,Bd​RB,B_{dR}

The ring B=Bℂp♭,ℚpB=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} is related to Bd​R,Bd​R+B_{dR},B_{dR}^{+} as follows. For a pp-adic field EE, let E0⊂EE_{0}\subset E denote the maximal unramified subfield of EE. Then by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Proposition 10.2.7] one has an injection (for each finite extension E/ℚpE/{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} contained in ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}).

(5.2.4.1) BE=B⊗E0E↪Bd​R.B_{E}=B\otimes_{E_{0}}E\hookrightarrow B_{dR}.

In particular

(5.2.4.2) B=Bp↪Bd​R.B=B_{p}\hookrightarrow B_{dR}.

§ 5.2.5 The ring B⊗ℚpEB\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E

It will be useful to consider a ring which is bigger than the ring BEB_{E} (Lemma 5.2.3.1) which is better suited for calculations. Consider

(5.2.5.1) B~=B⊗ℚpE\tilde{B}=B\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E

then by usual transitivity properties of tensor products with respect to the inclusions ℚp⊂E0⊂E{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}\subset E_{0}\subset E and so one can write this ring as

(5.2.5.2) B⊗ℚpE=(B⊗ℚpE0)⊗E0EB\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E=(B\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{0})\otimes_{E_{0}}E

and since BB is also an E0E_{0} algebra,

(5.2.5.3) B⊗ℚpE0=B⊕⋯⊕B⏞[E0:ℚp]factors.B\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{0}=\overbrace{B\oplus\cdots\oplus B}^{[E_{0}:{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}]factors}.

Hence

At any rate, B~E=B⊗ℚpE\tilde{B}_{E}=B\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E is naturally a finite and free B=Bℂp♭,ℚpB=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}-module through this identification.

One also has the natural diagonal embedding

§ 5.2.6 The ring BeB_{e}

Let me also introduce the ring [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.5.2]

(5.2.6.1) Be=B+​[1/t]φ=1=B​[1/t]φ=1=Bc​r​i​sφ=1.B_{e}=B^{+}[1/t]^{\varphi=1}=B[1/t]^{\varphi=1}=B_{cris}^{\varphi=1}.

By [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.5.2] BeB_{e} can be identified with the affine coordinate ring of the curve Xℂp♭,ℚp−{xc​a​n}{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}-\{x_{can}\} i.e. Xℂp♭,ℚp−{xc​a​n}=Spec⁡(Be){X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}-\{x_{can}\}={\rm Spec}(B_{e}). One also has, by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Theorem 6.5.2], the inclusions

(5.2.6.2)

These inclusions will allow one to view the theta-value locus as living in each of these period rings. Direct construction of the theta-value locus in Bc​r​i​sB_{cris} or Bd​RB_{dR} does not seem to be possible.

Remark 5.2.6.3.

By [Fontaine, 1994a, Fontaine, 1994b], the rings Bd​R⊃Bc​r​i​sB_{dR}\supset B_{cris} depend on the choice of a fixed algebraic closure ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. On the other hand, the rings B,Be,BEB,B_{e},B_{E} of [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018] do not depend on such a choice. ∙\bullet

§ 5.3 Enlarging subsets of BEℓ∗B_{E}^{\ell^{*}} using Aut⁡(GE){\rm Aut}(G_{E})-action, Frobenius action and convex closures

Let EE be a pp-adic field. Given a subset SS of the ring BEB_{E}, one can enlarge it in many natural ways. Let me review some of these enlargements which will be applied to obtain the final versions of the theta-values locii in various related rings.

Suppose S⊂BES\subset B_{E} (the considerations of this paragraph will be applied with E=Ew′E=E_{w}^{\prime} for each relevant w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}). I will enlarge this set further as follows:

§ 5.3.1 Aut⁡(GE){\rm Aut}(G_{E})-enlargements

Let S⊂BES\subset B_{E} or BEℓ∗B_{E}^{\ell^{*}} , consider the natural action of Aut⁡(GE){\rm Aut}(G_{E}) on the data GE​↷​BEG_{E}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}B_{E} by pre-composing the action of GEG_{E} on BEB_{E} with σ∈Aut⁡(GE)\sigma\in{\rm Aut}(G_{E}). More precisely, if σ∈Aut⁡(GE)\sigma\in{\rm Aut}(G_{E}) then consider the pre-composed or twisted action

and let SσS^{\sigma} be the image of SS under this new action of GEG_{E} on BEB_{E}. This consideration can be applied verbatim to the action GEG_{E}-action on BEℓ∗B_{E}^{\ell^{*}} and subsets in this context. So if S⊂BEℓ∗S\subset B_{E}^{\ell^{*}} is any subset then one simply takes the union

(5.3.1.2) ⋃σ∈Aut⁡(GE)Sσ⊂BEℓ∗.\bigcup_{\sigma\in{\rm Aut}(G_{E})}S^{\sigma}\subset B_{E}^{\ell^{*}}.

This provides a Galois enlargement of any subset S⊂BEℓ∗S\subset B_{E}^{\ell^{*}}.

Remark 5.3.1.3.
  1. (1)

    By [Joshi, 2020b], the Fargues-Fontaine curve XF,E{X}_{F,E} is not uniquely identified by its étale fundamental group–this group is isomorphic to the absolute Galois group GEG_{E} (this is the failure of the absolute Grothendieck conjecture for Fargues-Fontaine curves which is established in [Joshi, 2020b]).

  2. (2)

    In terminology of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d], taking unions over the images under automorphisms of Aut⁡(GE){\rm Aut}(G_{E}) is Mochizuki’s way of applying the indeterminacy Ind1 in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11] (my discussion of this is in § 8.11).

  3. (3)

    In this sense Mochizuki’s indeterminacy Ind1 arises from the failure of the absolute Grothendieck conjecture for Fargues-Fontaine curves established in [Joshi, 2020b].

∙\bullet

§ 5.3.2 Frobenius stablization enlargement

Another possible enlargement which can be applied is to replace S⊂BES\subset B_{E} by

(5.3.2.1) S⟼⋃n∈ℤφn​(S),S\longmapsto\bigcup_{n\in{\mathbb{Z}}}\varphi^{n}(S),

where φ\varphi is the Frobenius morphism of BEB_{E}. This obviously applies to subsets of BEℓ∗B_{E}^{\ell^{*}} and variants. This is the Frobenius enlargement of SS.

§ 5.3.3 Convex closure enlargement

Finally one can replace such a Galois and Frobenius enlarged set SS by the closure of its convex hull S¯\overline{S} in BEB_{E} with respect to the Frechet topology i.e. one can replace SS by the smallest, closed, convex subset containing SS. This set is closed and convex (see [Schneider, 2002, Chapter I] or [Schikhof, 1984] for basic properties of convex sets in pp-adic Banach spaces).

Remark 5.3.3.1.

My version of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] and Mochizuki’s version are both about lower bounds and it is important to recognize that enlargements (i.e. adding elements to the set SS) do not affect lower bounds on the supremum of norms of elements of SS. On the other hand, on a suitably enlarged set, an upper bound may be relatively easier to obtain. This is the rationale for establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. ∙\bullet

6 Construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?}

Let LL, C/LC/L and X/LX/L be as assumed in § 2.4 and § 3.1, § 3.3. In this section, subject to these assumptions, I provide the construction of the theta-values locii Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} (for suitable choice of decorations ??) and Mochizuki’s set Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (and its variant Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}). The sets Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} and Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} are needed for the statements of the fundamental estimate i.e the statements of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] in the respective theories. The construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} is the central assertion of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11].

One of the central difficulties which many readers have faced in ascertaining the veracity of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] has been the lack of a quantitative demonstration of the existence of distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures required for the construction of the set Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} which plays a fundamental role in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

This difficulty has been overcome through the present series of papers: my demonstration of the existence of arithmetic holomorphic structures is in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] and my construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} is in § 9. This section provides a construction of a simpler subset Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} which is adequate for establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

From my point of view the existence of these locii is a consequence of the existence of arithmetic Teichmuller spaces and its various properties established in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a, Joshi, 2023b] (and the present paper). Mochizuki’s approach to the construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (modulo the existence of arithmetic holomorphic structures and their properties) is detailed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11] and its proof.

The core idea of the construction of these sets is the same as that of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]–namely one collates, in a suitably chosen ambient set, some arithmetic information (Tate parameters or more generally theta-values) arising from many different holomorphoids of X/LX/L. Depending on the choice of ambient set used to collate the theta values, one obtains the version of the locus of that flavor. My construction of Mochizuki’s set Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} is detailed in § 9. It should be remarked that the verb to collate is not used in the context of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11, Corollary 3.12], but in my opinion it clarifies immensely what [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11] is all about. In fact, this verb is never used in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d], [Mochizuki, 2020] and [Mochizuki, 2022] at all.

The approach adopted here is based on [Joshi, 2023b] but, like [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], uses the (global) Initial Theta Data § 3.1, § 3.3 in a crucial way and is a more elaborate one than the local prototype of [Joshi, 2023b] which provides a natural demonstration of the structures claimed in [Mochizuki, 2021c]. A reading of that paper ([Joshi, 2023b]) is highly recommended along with this one.

§ 6.1 Descent of holomorphoid data to LmodL_{\rm mod}

    the bijection (see § 3.1, § 3.3)

§ 6.1.1 

From now on, and without further mention, 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(Lmod)𝐲¯\mathfrak{arith}(L_{\rm mod})_{\underline{{\bf y}}} will mean the arithmeticoid of LmodL_{\rm mod} constructed by Theorem 6.1.1 from the arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}} and in general underlined version of objects will refer to objects arising from arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(Lmod)𝐲¯\mathfrak{arith}(L_{\rm mod})_{\underline{{\bf y}}} constructed using Theorem 6.1.1.

§ 6.2 The definition of Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} and its variants

The construction of the set Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} is adelic and it will be constructed here by constructing subsets Θ~J​o​s​h​i,p?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},p}^{?}} for every prime pp and then taking product over all rational primes pp. The construction of the adelic set Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} (and of each Θ~J​o​s​h​i,p?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},p}^{?}}) requires fixing an Initial Theta Data § 3.1, § 3.3. This is also required in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] for the construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}.

§ 6.2.1 Local components of Θ~J​o​s​h​i,p{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},p}}

. The construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​i,p{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},p}} is based on the local construction of [Joshi, 2023b]. The important advantage of the method of [Joshi, 2023b] is that for any prime w|pw|p, it provides theta-values locii

Θ~J​o​s​h​iB?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{?}}

using a wide class of rings B?B_{?} used in pp-adic Hodge Theory, for example

B?=B,B⁡[1/t],BI​(I⊂[0,1]⊂ℝ),Bc​r​i​s​ and ​Bd​R,{B_{?}}=B,B[1/t],B_{I}\ (I\subset[0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}}),B_{cris}\text{ and }B_{dR},

(see Theorem 6.7.1.1). At the same time, by choosing a suitable Galois cohomology group (for each w|pw|p and for each rational prime pp) to serve as a receiver of theta-values, viewed as cohomology classes via [Mochizuki, 2009, Proposition 1.4], one establishes the construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} along the lines of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] using my canonical approach to arithmetic holomorphic structures.

On the other hand working with these rings of pp-adic Hodge Theory provides yet another distinct advantage: one can multiply (and add) together theta-values arising from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures for distinct primes ww lying over pp. This bundling of theta-values arising from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures and for distinct primes w|pw|p (for each fixed rational prime pp) also requires fixing an Initial theta-data § 3.1, § 3.3. In [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], Mochizuki works with a Galois cohomology group (for each prime w|pw|p and each prime pp) and so there is no natural ring structure to multiply theta-values at all. To circumvent this problem, Mochizuki forces multiplication of theta-values by means of his theory of tensor packets [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] (to achieve this bundling of theta-values).

In particular, my approach to the construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} also demonstrates that Mochizuki’s framework of tensor-packets, arises far more naturally from the theory of Arithmetic Teichmuller spaces as documented in the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper).

§ 6.3 Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz and arithmeticoids

Let LL, C/LC/L, and X/LX/L be as in § 2.4. Fix an Initial theta-data § 3.1, § 3.3. Let

𝐳=(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}=({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}

(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲1,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲2,…,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗)(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{1}},\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{2}},\ldots,\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}})

and hence one obtains an ℓ∗{\ell^{*}}-tuple of holomorphoids of

(X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲1,X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲2,…,X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗).(X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{1}},X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{2}},\ldots,X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}}).

of X/LX/L. The following is a fundamental consequence of [Joshi, 2023a]:

Theorem 6.3.1.

For any 𝐳=(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}=({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}, the holomorphoids

X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲1,X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲2,…,X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{1}},X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{2}},\ldots,X/\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}}

are all distinct and need not even provide isomorphic pairs of analytic spaces at any prime w∈𝕍L′n​o​nw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}^{non}.

Proof.

This is immediate from [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ].

§ 6.4 The collation of theta-values

Let 𝐳∈(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} (in Mochizuki’s parlance, each 𝐳\mathbf{z} is a Θ\Theta-Link). For the given X,L,L′X,L,L^{\prime} (as in § 3.1, § 3.3), Theorem 6.3.1 provides, for each 𝐳∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} and for each w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, the tuple of Tate parameters

(6.4.1) (qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲1),qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲2),…,qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲ℓ∗)).\left(q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{1})},q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{2})},\ldots,q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})}\right).

The basic idea behind the construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?} and Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i?{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{?} is that one wants to collate, for the given X,L,L′X,L,L^{\prime} (as in § 3.1, § 3.3), and for each 𝐳∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} and for each w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, the tuple of Tate parameters (6.4.1) in a suitable container set (here qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲j)q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{j})} is the Tate parameter of X/Lw′X/L_{w}^{\prime} computed in the arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲j)\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{j})).

The main problem here is that, even for any single w|pw|p, the individual elements qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲1)q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{1})}, qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲2)q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{2})}, …\ldots , qw,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲ℓ∗)q_{w,\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{\ell^{*}})} of the tuple given in eq. (6.4.1) do not live in a natural common set where these elements may be compared with each other. This is where the choice of a common set ?? (in the superscripts of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i?{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{?}, Θ~J​o​s​h​i?{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{?}) comes into picture. In [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2023b], I recognized that one may choose fundamental ring of pp-adic Hodge theory as a common location for comparing theta-values and there I introduced therein the theory of lifting of theta-values (this is recalled here briefly in § 6.4.2).

Mochizuki’s choice of his common set in [Mochizuki, 2021c] is based on his theory of Galois Theoretic Theta-evaluation [Mochizuki, 2009, Proposition 1.4] (applied to the arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(𝐲j)\mathfrak{arith}({\bf y}_{j})) and then observing that the relevant Galois cohomology group provided by any arithmeticoid is amphoric ([Joshi, 2023a, Proposition ]). The method of collation of cohomology classes (in the cohomology of a fixed arithmeticoid) is established here in § 9.7.5. Hence the methods developed in the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper) is better adapted for providing a uniform way at arriving at both the constructions.

§ 6.6 Admissible lifts and Tate parameters

The connection between admissible theta-values lifts and Tate parameters is given by the following:

Proposition 6.6.1.

Let X,L,L′X,L,L^{\prime} be as in § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3. Let 𝐳∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}, and let w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p} for some prime pp. Let 𝚵𝐳,w=(Ξλ,Ky1′,…,Ξλ,Kyℓ∗′)\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}=(\Xi_{\lambda,K_{y_{1}^{\prime}}},\ldots,\Xi_{\lambda,K_{y_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime}}}) be an admissible theta-values-lift at ww. For j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}} let

ψj:BE→Kyj\psi_{j}:B_{E}\to K_{y_{j}}

be the natural quotient homomorphism arising by taking quotient modulo the (principal) maximal ideal corresponding to the closed classical point yj′∈Yℂp♭,Ew′y_{j}^{\prime}\in{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E_{w}^{\prime}}. Then for j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}} one has

ψj​(Ξλ,Ky1′)=ψj​([zw,j])=ξ1,Kyj′=qX/Ew′,yj′∈Kyj′,\psi_{j}(\Xi_{\lambda,K_{y_{1}^{\prime}}})=\psi_{j}([z_{w,j}])=\xi_{1,K_{y_{j}^{\prime}}}=q_{X/E_{w}^{\prime},y_{j}^{\prime}}\in K_{y_{j}^{\prime}},

where is qX/Ew′,yj′q_{X/E_{w}^{\prime},y_{j}^{\prime}} the Tate parameter of X/Ew′X/E_{w}^{\prime} in the arithmetic holomorphic structure provided by yj′y_{j}^{\prime}.

Proof.

Let 𝔪j⊂BE\mathfrak{m}_{j}\subset B_{E} be the maximal ideal corresponding to the point yj′y_{j}^{\prime}. Then by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Chap. IV and Chap. VI] 𝔪j=(tKyj′)\mathfrak{m}_{j}=(t_{K_{y_{j}^{\prime}}}) is a principal ideal and this generator maps to zero under BE→BE/𝔪j=Kyj′B_{E}\to B_{E}/\mathfrak{m}_{j}=K_{y_{j}^{\prime}}. Hence

ψj​(Ξλ,Ky1′)=ψj​([zw,j]).\psi_{j}(\Xi_{\lambda,K_{y_{1}^{\prime}}})=\psi_{j}([z_{w,j}]).

The assertion now follows as [zw,j][z_{w,j}] is a Teichmuller lift of ξ1,Kyj′=qX/Ew′,yj′\xi_{1,K_{y_{j}^{\prime}}}=q_{X/E_{w}^{\prime},y_{j}^{\prime}}.

§ 6.6.1 The theta-values locus in Θ~J​o​s​h​iBE{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E}}

§ 6.9 Non-degeneracy of Θ~J​o​s​h​iBE{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E}}

The following lemma is useful in understanding Θ~J​o​s​h​iBE{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E}}:

Lemma 6.9.1.

Let 𝔪1,𝔪2,…,𝔪ℓ∗\mathfrak{m}_{1},\mathfrak{m}_{2},\ldots,\mathfrak{m}_{{\ell^{*}}} be closed maximal ideals of BEB_{E}. Let

τ:BEℓ∗→∏j=1ℓ∗BE/𝔪j\tau:B_{E}^{\ell^{*}}\to\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}B_{E}/\mathfrak{m}_{j}

be the homomorphism given using the natural surjection τj:BE→BE/𝔪j\tau_{j}:B_{E}\to B_{E}/\mathfrak{m}_{j} for each j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}. Then the image

τ⁡(Θ~J​o​s​h​iBE)≠(0,0,…,0).\tau({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E}})\neq(0,0,\ldots,0).

It suffices to note that Θ~J​o​s​h​iBE{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E}} contains elements of the form

𝚵0,𝐳,wz1,…,zℓ∗=([z1],[z2],…,[zℓ∗])\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{0,\mathbf{z},w}^{z_{1},\ldots,z_{\ell^{*}}}=([z_{1}],[z_{2}],\ldots,[z_{\ell^{*}}])

and by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Lemma 2.2.13], it follows that the image of any Teichmuller lift [z]∈W⁡(Oℂp♭)⊗ℤpOE⊂BE[z]\in W({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}{O}_{E}\subset B_{E} is non-zero in BE/𝔪jB_{E}/\mathfrak{m}_{j} for each j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}, hence

τ⁡([z1],…,[zℓ∗])≠(0,0,…,0)∈∏j=1ℓ∗BE/𝔪j.\tau([z_{1}],\ldots,[z_{\ell^{*}}])\neq(0,0,\ldots,0)\in\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}B_{E}/\mathfrak{m}_{j}.

This completes the proof.

§ 6.10.1 Elements 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}} as Mochizuki’s Θ\Theta-pilot objects

Let me remark that each admissible theta-values-lift 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}} is the additive analog of Mochizuki’s Θ\Theta-pilot object (see [Mochizuki, 2021c, Definition 3.8]). Especially, Mochizuki’s theta-values set Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}, according to [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12], is the “holomorphic hull” of the collection of all possible Θ\Theta-pilot objects- for the definition “holomorphic hulls” see [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5(ii)].

In § 9, I will demonstrate that each 𝚵𝐳∈Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\in{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} has a Galois cohomological manifestation and this cohomological object will be a Θ\Theta-Pilot in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2021c].

§ 6.10.2 Descending to LmodL_{\rm mod}

Assume L,C/L,X/L,ℓ,L′L,C/L,X/L,\ell,L^{\prime} are as in § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3. The curve X/LX/L is in fact definable over LmodL_{\rm mod}. Hence it will be convenient to provide a theta-values locus which does in fact live over LmodL_{\rm mod}. This is accomplished by means of the bijection 𝕍Lmod≃𝕍¯⊂𝕍L′\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}}\simeq\underline{\mathbb{V}}\subset\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}. By taking the image of the theta-values locii under the projection constructed in the proof of Theorem 6.1.1 and the trace morphism 𝔹L′→𝔹Lmod\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}\to\mathbb{B}_{L_{\rm mod}} given by taking, for each unique prime w∈𝕍¯w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}} of L′L^{\prime} lying over v∈𝕍Lmodv\in\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}} given by the bijection 𝕍¯≃𝕍Lmod\underline{\mathbb{V}}\simeq\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}}, the trace morphism BLw′→BLm​o​d,vB_{L_{w}^{\prime}}\to B_{L_{mod,v}}, one obtains the image of theta-values locii in 𝔹Lmodℓ∗\mathbb{B}_{L_{\rm mod}}^{\ell^{*}} which I will refer to as the descent of the theta-value locii to LmodL_{\rm mod}.

7 Proof of Mochizuki’s Corollary 3.12 for Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}

§ 7.1 

Now the stage is set for proving my version of the fundamental estimate known as of Mochizuki’s Corollary 3.12. A prototype version of which was established in [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ]. The version proved here works in the number field setting and exhibits all features of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] except for the fact that I work with the ring 𝔹L′\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}} defined above. Mochizuki’s version works with Galois cohomology groups and will be established in § 9.

Throughout this section, the assumptions and notational conventions of § 2.4 and § 3.1, § 3.3 will be in force.

§ 7.2 

The following definition will be used throughout.

Definition 7.2.1.

Let ρ∈(0,1]⊂ℝ\rho\in(0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}}. Let 𝐳∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}, let

𝚵=(𝚵𝐳,w)w∈𝕍L′∈Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′.\boldsymbol{\Xi}=(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w})_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}\in{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}.

For each w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}, 𝚵𝐳,w∈BLw′ℓ∗\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}\in B_{L_{w}^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}} is an ℓ∗{\ell^{*}}-tuple

𝚵𝐳,w=(Ξ1,Ξ2,…,Ξℓ∗)∈BLw′ℓ∗.\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}=(\Xi_{1},\Xi_{2},\ldots,\Xi_{\ell^{*}})\in B_{L_{w}^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}}.

Define the (BLw′,ρ)(B_{L^{\prime}_{w}},\rho)-size of 𝚵𝐳,w\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w} to be the product

(7.2.2) |𝚵𝐳,w|BLw′,ρ=|Ξ1|BLw′,ρ⋅|Ξ2|BLw′,ρ⋅⋯⋅|Ξℓ∗|BLw′,ρ∈ℝ.\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}=\left|\Xi_{1}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w},\rho}}\cdot\left|\Xi_{2}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w},\rho}}\cdots\cdot\left|\Xi_{\ell^{*}}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w},\rho}}\in{\mathbb{R}}.

be the product of absolute values with respect to the norm |−|BLw′,ρ\left|-\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w}},\rho} on BLw′B_{L^{\prime}_{w}} given by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Définition 1.10.2]. Define the (𝔹L′,ρ)(\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho)-size of 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}} to be the product

(7.2.3) |𝚵𝐳|𝔹L′,ρ=∏w∈𝕍L′|𝚵𝐳,w|BLw′,ρ.\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho}=\prod_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}.

∙\bullet

Lemma 7.2.4.

For all ρ∈(0,1]⊂ℝ\rho\in(0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}} and for all 𝐳∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}},

|𝚵𝐳|𝔹L′,ρ<∞.\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho}<\infty.

Proof.

By the definition of 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}, and by Lemma 6.5.2, for all w∈𝕍L′−𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}-\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, 𝚵𝐳,w\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w} has absolute value equal to one. Hence this product has a finite number of terms ≠1\neq 1 and so is finite.

Remark 7.2.5.

It will be often convenient to group the product definition |𝚵𝐳|𝔹L′,ρ\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho} as follows

(7.2.6) |𝚵𝐳|𝔹L′,ρ=∏p∈𝕍ℚ∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s|𝚵𝐳,w|BLw′,ρ.\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho}=\prod_{p\in\mathbb{V}_{{\mathbb{Q}}}}\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w}\right|_{B_{L^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}.

§ 7.3 The fundamental theta-values estimate

The following fundamental estimate is the global version of [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ] and is my version of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]:

Theorem 7.3.1.

Let C/LC/L be an elliptic curve and suppose ℓ\ell is an odd prime such that § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3 hold for C,L,ℓC,L,\ell. Let L′/LL^{\prime}/L be the finite extension of LL defined in § 3.1, § 3.3. For any w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, let pwp_{w} be the rational prime lying below ww. Choose a normalization of the pwp_{w}-adic valuation on, ℂpw{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}, a completed algebraic closure of ℚpw{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{w}} to be such that for any uniformizer πw∈OLw′\pi_{w}\in{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}} one has

|πw|ℂpw=pw−1.\left|\pi_{w}\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}}=p_{w}^{-1}.

Let Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} be the adelic theta-values locus for the ring 𝔹L′\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}} (defined in Definition 6.10.2). Then

|Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′|𝔹L′≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℂpwℓ∗\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{\ell^{*}}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}}

Proof.

The set of such rational primes pp is finite (by § 3.1, § 3.3, 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset if and only if pp is an odd rational prime such that for some w|pw|p the curve XX has split multiplicative reduction), hence the product in the assertion is finite.

Recall from § 4.4 and § 4.5 the construction of the standard point 𝐳Θ∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. I will write 𝐳=𝐳Θ\mathbf{z}=\mathbf{z}_{\Theta} for brevity of notation. By construction, the set Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} contains elements of the 𝚵𝐳Θ=𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}}=\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}. and

and especially it contains elements of the form

Hence it is sufficient to find a lower bound for |𝚵0,𝐳α|𝔹L′\left|\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{0,\mathbf{z}}^{\bbalpha}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} for some choice of α\bbalpha.

§ 7.4 Some corollaries of the fundamental estimates

Let me first make the following definition. A subset Φ=∏w∈𝕍L′Φw⊂𝔹L′ℓ∗\Phi=\prod_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}\Phi_{w}\subset\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}^{\ell^{*}} is said to be a special precompact subset if

  1. (1)

    Φ\Phi contains the lifts of theta values arising from special point 𝐳Θ\mathbf{z}_{\Theta} constructed in Theorem 7.3.1, i.e. 𝚵𝐳Θ∈Φ\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}}\in\Phi, and

  2. (2)

    for every w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, the factor Φw⊂BEw′ℓ∗\Phi_{w}\subset B_{E^{\prime}_{w}}^{\ell^{*}} is precompact i.e. the closure of Φw\Phi_{w} in BEw′ℓ∗B_{E^{\prime}_{w}}^{\ell^{*}} is compact (for the Fréchet-topology) and for all other primes w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}, Φw={1}\Phi_{w}=\{1\}.

Corollary 7.4.1.

With the hypothesis of the Theorem 7.3.1. Suppose Φ⊂Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′\Phi\subset{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} is a special precompact subset of Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} in the sense of § 7.4, then one has

∞>|Φ|𝔹L′>∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅|qw1/2​ℓ|ℂpwℓ∗.\infty>\left|\Phi\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}>\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{\ell^{*}}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}}.

Proof.

Let Φ⊂Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′\Phi\subset{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} be a special precompact subset. As any finite extension of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} is locally compact, special precompactness of Φ\Phi is equivalent to Φw\Phi_{w} being a bounded subset of BEw′ℓ∗B_{E^{\prime}_{w}}^{\ell^{*}} for all w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}} (for the Fréchet topology) and as the set of 𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss} is finite, so sup0<ρ<1|Φ|𝔹L′,ρ\sup_{0<\rho<1}\left|\Phi\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},\rho} is evidently bounded and hence the second assertion is established.

Corollary 7.4.2.

In the notation of Theorem 7.3.1, and with ρ=1\rho=1, one has

1≥|Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′|𝔹L′,1≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℂpw.1\geq\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}}\right|_{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},1}\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}}.

Proof.

The upper bound follows from the fact that for each w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, and ρ=1\rho=1, one can apply [Joshi, 2023b, Proposition ]. The lower bound is Theorem 7.3.1.

§ 7.5 Prime Bundling rings B˘L′,p{\breve{B}}_{L^{\prime},p} and 𝐁˘L′,p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{L^{\prime},p}

One important aspect of working with theta-value locii with values in a ring is that one can use the multiplicative structure of the ring to multiply theta-values arising from distinct arithmeticoids. For example in 𝔹L′\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}} it makes perfect sense to talk about

𝚵𝐳⋅𝚵𝐳′∈𝔹L′,\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}},

as well as

𝚵𝐳+𝚵𝐳′∈𝔹L′.\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}}+\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}.

Similarly one can also multiply the local components at two distinct primes w1,w2∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sw_{1},w_{2}\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p} lying over a fixed rational prime:

(𝚵𝐳,w1⊗1)⋅(1⊗𝚵𝐳,w2)∈BLw1′⊗ℚpBLw2′,(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w_{1}}\otimes 1)\cdot(1\otimes\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w_{2}})\in B_{L_{w_{1}}^{\prime}}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{L_{w_{2}}^{\prime}},

as well as

𝚵𝐳,w1⊗1+1⊗𝚵𝐳,w2∈BLw1′⊗ℚpBLw2′.\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w_{1}}\otimes 1+1\otimes\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z},w_{2}}\in B_{L_{w_{1}}^{\prime}}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{L_{w_{2}}^{\prime}}.

This observation allows me to demonstrate the tensor packet structure of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] which plays in the main theorem of [Mochizuki, 2021d]. I call this bundling of theta-values. The purpose of this bundling is to arrive at a minimal theta-values locus (this becomes important in providing tight bounds) and this together with the fact that 𝕍¯≃𝕍Lmod\underline{\mathbb{V}}\simeq\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}}, one can expect to descend these data back to LmodL_{\rm mod}.

In this section I will describe this bundling structure explicitly. One needs to work with several Fargues-Fontaine rings BEB_{E} (for varying EE) simultaneously and leads to some auxiliary rings which I call bundling rings. The definition of these bundling rings is the main content of this section.

The notations and assumptions of § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3 will strictly be in force. Following [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], I will work with all the primes w|pw|p in 𝕍¯\underline{\mathbb{V}} simultaneously.

§ 7.6 Norms on tensor product of Banach spaces

Familiarity with the archimedean theory of tensor products of Banach spaces is useful but not essential–for the archimedean theory see [Kaniuth, 2009] or [Diestel et al., 2008]. I will use the construction of tensor product of Banach spaces over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} for which [Schneider, 2002, Chap IV, § 17] is a convenient reference. To apply these results (of [Schneider, 2002]) one needs to remember that the Banach spaces BEB_{E} over EE and as the pp-adic field EE is discretely valued, EE is a spherically complete field.

§ 7.6.1 Basic examples

Let {Vα}\{V_{\alpha}\} be a finite multi-set of (1) finite dimensional ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} vector spaces or (2) ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-Banach spaces of infinite dimensions. Two collections of such will be important to us. The first is the collection of pp-adic fields which occur above

(7.6.1.1) {Vα}={Ew′:w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s,w|p}\{V_{\alpha}\}=\{E_{w}^{\prime}:w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss},w|p\}

viewed as a collection of finite dimensional ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} vector spaces which are complete with respect to their usual pp-adic norms |−|Ew′\left|-\right|_{E_{w}^{\prime}} and hence are Banach spaces with these norms. Second is the collection

(7.6.1.2) {Vα}={BEw′:w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s,w|p}\{V_{\alpha}\}=\{B_{E_{w}^{\prime}}:w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss},w|p\}

of infinite dimensional Fréchet algebras over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} equipped with Fréchet norms |−|ρ\left|-\right|_{\rho} for every ρ∈[0,1]⊂ℝ\rho\in[0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}} constructed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018] and hence can be treated as Banach spaces with respect to any of the Fréchet norms.

§ 7.6.2 Tensor products and the cross-norm property

Let EE be a pp-adic field for rational prime pp or let E=ℝE={\mathbb{R}} or ℂ{\mathbb{C}} i.e. the archimedean case is allowed in this discussion.

In general, there are many distinct tensor products of a pair of Banach spaces over EE. Let (V,|−|V),(W,|−|W)(V,\left|-\right|_{V}),(W,\left|-\right|_{W}) be Banach-spaces over EE. Suppose one has a tensor product (V⊗EW,|−|V⊗W)(V\otimes_{E}W,\left|-\right|_{V\otimes_{W}}) of (V,|−|V)(V,\left|-\right|_{V}) and (W,|−|W)(W,\left|-\right|_{W}). Then the following property, if true, of this tensor product will be called the cross-norm property (of this tensor product):

(7.6.2.1) |v⊗w|V⊗EW=|v|V⋅|w|W∀v∈V,w∈W.\left|v\otimes w\right|_{V\otimes_{E}W}=\left|v\right|_{V}\cdot\left|w\right|_{W}\qquad\forall v\in V,w\in W.

In the archimedean case, by [Grothendieck, 1953] or [Diestel et al., 2008], any tensor product of Banach spaces (over E=ℝ,ℂE={\mathbb{R}},{\mathbb{C}}) sandwiched between the injective tensor product and the projective tensor product has the cross-norm property (7.6.2.1). More precisely, in the archimedean case, by [Grothendieck, 1953] or [Diestel et al., 2008], the projective tensor product is the greatest cross-norm, while the injective tensor product is the smallest cross-norm.

Now assume EE is non-archimedean. I will not recall here the definition of the projective tensor product |−|V⊗EW\left|-\right|_{V\otimes_{E}W} given in [Bosch et al., 1984, Chapter 2, 2.1.7] or [Schneider, 2002, Chapter 4, § 17].

Then one has cross-norm property (7.6.2.1) for the projective tensor Banach spaces over the field EE ([Schneider, 2002, Proposition 17.4]). Note that since the pp-adic field EE is complete and discretely valued field, so it is spherically complete [Schneider, 2002, § 1, Lemma 1.6].

As a consequence of spherical completeness of EE, one has by [van der Put and van Tiel, 1967, Theorem 1] that the injective and projective tensor products coincide and so one may speak of the unique tensor product. [One of the difficulties of working with fields which are not spherically complete is that a Banach space may have no non-zero continuous linear forms on it; on the other hand, from the point of view of pp-adic integration (and measures), the existence of linear forms is desirable in any case.] Moreover under spherical completeness of EE, one has additionally the nice properties [Schneider, 2002, Proposition 17.8, 17.9] of the tensor product. This remark applies to all Banach spaces over pp-adic fields considered here and the following summarizes this discussion:

Theorem 7.6.2.2.

Let EE be a pp-adic field or let E=ℝ,ℂE={\mathbb{R}},{\mathbb{C}}.

  1. (1)

    If E=ℝ,ℂE={\mathbb{R}},{\mathbb{C}}, then the projective and the injective tensor products have the cross-norm property (7.6.2.1) (and so does any norm sandwiched between these two norms) ([Grothendieck, 1953] or [Diestel et al., 2008, Theorem 1.1.3 ]).

  2. (2)

    If EE is a pp-adic field, then projective tensor product and the injective tensor products coincide (and one can speak of the tensor product of Banach spaces over a pp-adic field EE) ([van der Put and van Tiel, 1967, Theorem 1]) and,

  3. (3)

    the cross-norm property (7.6.2.1) holds for any pair of Banach spaces over any pp-adic field EE .

  4. (4)

    Especially, for E=ℚpE={\mathbb{Q}}_{p}, one has

    |v⊗w|V⊗ℚpW=|v|V⋅|w|W.\left|v\otimes w\right|_{V\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}W}=\left|v\right|_{V}\cdot\left|w\right|_{W}.
  5. (5)

    In particular, for pp-adic fields E1,E2⊇EE_{1},E_{2}\supseteq E, the tensor product BE1⊗EBE2B_{E_{1}}{\otimes}_{E}B_{E_{2}} has the cross-norm property for any choice of norms on each of its factors.

§ 7.6.3 Passage to completed tensor products

While passage to completed tensor product is unnecessary for what I will do here, it is worth remarking that by [Schneider, 2002, Chapter 4, Proposition 17.6], if V,WV,W are Fréchet spaces over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} then completed tensor product V​⊗^ℚp​WV\widehat{\otimes}_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}W is a Fréchet space. In particular, for pp-adic fields E1,E2E_{1},E_{2}, the tensor product BE1​⊗^ℚp​BE2B_{E_{1}}\widehat{\otimes}_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{E_{2}} is a Fréchet space.

§ 7.6.4 Tensor products again

The discussion of this paragraph provides an analog of the above equality for the example of Banach algebras

{BE:E​ a p-adic field}\{B_{E}:E\text{ a p-adic field}\}

equipped with their multiplicative norms i.e. valuations

{|−|BE;ρ} for ρ∈[0,1]⊂ℝ\{\left|-\right|_{B_{E};\rho}\}\text{ for }\rho\in[0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}}

constructed in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Chapitre 2]. The following lemma is a standard consequence of valuation theory and is easily established:

Lemma 7.6.4.1.

Let E1,E2E_{1},E_{2} be two pp-adic fields, let ρ1,ρ2∈[0,1]⊂ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2}\in[0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}}. Write B1=BE1,B2=BE2B_{1}=B_{E_{1}},B_{2}=B_{E_{2}} and equip them with the multiplicative norms |−|Bi;ρi\left|-\right|_{B_{i};\rho_{i}} for i=1,2i=1,2. Then the algebra B1⊗ℚpB2B_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{2} is equipped with a valuation i.e. a multiplicative norm |−|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2\left|-\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}} such that for every b1∈B1b_{1}\in B_{1} and for every b2∈B2b_{2}\in B_{2} one has

|b1⊗b2|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|(b1⊗1)⋅(1⊗b2)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2==|(b1⊗1)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2⋅|(1⊗b2)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|b1|B1;ρ1​|b2|B2;ρ2.\left|b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|(b_{1}\otimes 1)\cdot(1\otimes b_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\\ \qquad\qquad=\left|(b_{1}\otimes 1)\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}\cdot\left|(1\otimes b_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|b_{1}\right|_{B_{1};\rho_{1}}\left|b_{2}\right|_{B_{2};\rho_{2}}.

especially

|b1⊗b2|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|b1|B1;ρ1​|b2|B2;ρ2.\left|b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|b_{1}\right|_{B_{1};\rho_{1}}\left|b_{2}\right|_{B_{2};\rho_{2}}.

I will refer to |−|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2\left|-\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}} as the tensor product norm of (B1,|−|B1;ρ1)(B_{1},\left|-\right|_{B_{1};\rho_{1}}) and (B2,|−|B2;ρ2)(B_{2},\left|-\right|_{B_{2};\rho_{2}}).

§ 7.6.5 Another variant

Here is a Banach theoretic version of the above lemma which I could not find in existing literature and of which I will provide a proof.

Lemma 7.6.5.1.

Let E1,E2E_{1},E_{2} be two pp-adic fields, let ρ1,ρ2∈[0,1]⊂ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2}\in[0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}}. Write B1=BE1,B2=BE2B_{1}=B_{E_{1}},B_{2}=B_{E_{2}} and equip them with the multiplicative norms |−|Bi;ρi\left|-\right|_{B_{i};\rho_{i}} for i=1,2i=1,2. Then the algebra B1⊗ℚpB2B_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{2} is equipped with a multiplicative norm |−|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2\left|-\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}} such that for every b1∈B1b_{1}\in B_{1} and for every b2∈B2b_{2}\in B_{2} one has

|b1⊗b2|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|(b1⊗1)⋅(1⊗b2)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2==|(b1⊗1)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2⋅|(1⊗b2)|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|b1|B1;ρ1​|b2|B2;ρ2.\left|b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|(b_{1}\otimes 1)\cdot(1\otimes b_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\\ \qquad\qquad=\left|(b_{1}\otimes 1)\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}\cdot\left|(1\otimes b_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|b_{1}\right|_{B_{1};\rho_{1}}\left|b_{2}\right|_{B_{2};\rho_{2}}.

especially

|b1⊗b2|B1⊗B2;ρ1,ρ2=|b1|B1;ρ1​|b2|B2;ρ2.\left|b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\right|_{B_{1}\otimes B_{2};\rho_{1},\rho_{2}}=\left|b_{1}\right|_{B_{1};\rho_{1}}\left|b_{2}\right|_{B_{2};\rho_{2}}.

Proof.

By [Lang, 2002], there is a natural way to define an algebra structure on the tensor product B1⊗ℚpB2B_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{2} compatible with the algebra structures of each of the factors, namely

(b1⊗b2)⋅(c1⊗c2)=(b1​c1)⊗(b2​c2).(b_{1}\otimes b_{2})\cdot(c_{1}\otimes c_{2})=(b_{1}c_{1})\otimes(b_{2}c_{2}).

Then

|(b1⊗b2)⋅(c1⊗c2)|B1⊗ℚpB2=|(b1​c1)⊗(b2​c2)|B1⊗ℚpB2\left|(b_{1}\otimes b_{2})\cdot(c_{1}\otimes c_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{2}}=\left|(b_{1}c_{1})\otimes(b_{2}c_{2})\right|_{B_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}B_{2}}

and by [Schneider, 2002, Chap 4, Proposition 17.4]

|(b1​c1)⊗(b2​c2)|=|b1​c1|B1​|b2​c2|B2\left|(b_{1}c_{1})\otimes(b_{2}c_{2})\right|=\left|b_{1}c_{1}\right|_{B_{1}}\left|b_{2}c_{2}\right|_{B_{2}}

and as the norms on B1,B2B_{1},B_{2} are multiplicative, one gets

|(b1​c1)⊗(b2​c2)|=|b1​c1|B1​|b2​c2|B2=|b1|​|c1|​|b2|​|c2|=|b1⊗c1|​|b2⊗c2|\left|(b_{1}c_{1})\otimes(b_{2}c_{2})\right|=\left|b_{1}c_{1}\right|_{B_{1}}\left|b_{2}c_{2}\right|_{B_{2}}=\left|b_{1}\right|\left|c_{1}\right|\left|b_{2}\right|\left|c_{2}\right|=\left|b_{1}\otimes c_{1}\right|\left|b_{2}\otimes c_{2}\right|

and therefore

|(b1​c1)⊗(b2​c2)|=|b1⊗c1|​|b2⊗c2|,\left|(b_{1}c_{1})\otimes(b_{2}c_{2})\right|=\left|b_{1}\otimes c_{1}\right|\left|b_{2}\otimes c_{2}\right|,

and the assertion of the lemma is immediate from this formula by considering the special case (b1⊗1)​(1⊗b2)=b1⊗b2(b_{1}\otimes 1)(1\otimes b_{2})=b_{1}\otimes b_{2}. This proves the assertion.

§ 7.6.6 The lower bound lemma

The proof of the following lemma is now self-evident:

Lemma 7.6.6.1.

Suppose one is given a finite collection of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-Banach spaces {Vα}α\{V_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha} and suppose that one is also given an element mα∈Vαm_{\alpha}\in V_{\alpha} for each VαV_{\alpha}. Then for the projective tensor product norm on ⨂αVα\bigotimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha}, one has

(7.6.6.2) |⨂αmα|⊗αVα=∏α|mα|Vα.\left|\bigotimes_{\alpha}m_{\alpha}\right|_{\otimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha}}=\prod_{\alpha}\left|m_{\alpha}\right|_{V_{\alpha}}.

In particular, if S⊂⨂αVαS\subset\bigotimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha} is a subset containing some pure tensor ⨂αmα\bigotimes_{\alpha}m_{\alpha} then one has

(7.6.6.3) sup{|s|⊗αVα:s∈S}≥∏α|mα|Vα.\sup\left\{\left|s\right|_{\otimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha}}:s\in S\right\}\geq\prod_{\alpha}\left|m_{\alpha}\right|_{V_{\alpha}}.

§ 7.6.7 Adelic considerations

The above consideration will now be adelized as follows. Suppose for every prime pp one has a finite collection of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-Banach spaces {Vα,p}\{V_{\alpha,p}\} (the indexing set for the α\alpha may depend on pp but I am suppressing the notation for the indexing set) and suppose Sp⊆⨂Vα,pS_{p}\subseteq\bigotimes V_{\alpha,p} is a subset. Then consider the product

S=∏pSp⊂∏p⨂αVα,p.S=\prod_{p}S_{p}\subset\prod_{p}\bigotimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha,p}.

Define

|Sp|=sup{|sp|⊗αVα,p:sp∈Sp},\left|S_{p}\right|=\sup\{\left|s_{p}\right|_{\otimes_{\alpha}V_{\alpha,p}}:{s_{p}\in S_{p}}\},

and define (with the convention that ∞⋅∞=∞,0⋅∞=∞\infty\cdot\infty=\infty,0\cdot\infty=\infty)

|S|=∏p|Sp|∈ℝ∪{∞}.\left|S\right|=\prod_{p}\left|S_{p}\right|\in{\mathbb{R}}\cup\{\infty\}.

§ 7.6.8 Basic examples

The principal cases of interest here are

Sp=Θ~J​o​s​h​i,pS_{p}={{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},p}}

and

Sp=Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,pS_{p}={\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},p}

for all rational primes pp lying below the primes in 𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss} and for the remaining primes Sp={1}S_{p}=\{1\} or SpS_{p} is the unit ball in the pp-component. In this case, the sets SpS_{p}, satisfy the additional condition that |Sp|=1\left|S_{p}\right|=1 for all but finitely many primes pp and for the remaining finitely many primes, one expects |Sp|<∞\left|S_{p}\right|<\infty. So |S|<∞\left|S\right|<\infty in the principal case of interest.

§ 7.6.9 Sets of adelic and bounded adelic types

The above example leads to the following definition.

  1. (1)

    I will say that SS as above is a set of adelic type if |Sp|=1\left|S_{p}\right|=1 for all but finitely many primes pp, and

  2. (2)

    I will say that SS is a set of bounded adelic type if SS is a set of adelic type and |Sp|<∞\left|S_{p}\right|<\infty for every prime pp.

The following lemma is a consequence of the construction of the theta-values sets:

Lemma 7.6.9.1.

The set Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝔹L′{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\mathbb{B}_{L^{\prime}}} and its variants for different choices of the BB-rings are of adelic type.

§ 7.7 The fundamental estimate for Θ~J​o​s​h​iB˘⊗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}} and Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘⊗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}}

§ 7.7.1 The tensor product rings B˘⊗{\breve{B}}^{\otimes} and 𝐁˘⊗{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}

Let me now provide a proof of the fundamental estimate using the above detailed theory of tensor products. To keep the discussion simple, I will work with tensor product of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-Fŕechet vectors spaces and, for any rational prime pp such that 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset, introduce the rings

(7.7.1.1) B˘L′,p⊗=⨂w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅BEw′,{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}_{L^{\prime},p}=\bigotimes_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}B_{E_{w}^{\prime}},

and the ring

(7.7.1.2) 𝐁˘⊗L′,p=⨂w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅(Bp⊗ℚpEw′).{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}_{L^{\prime},p}=\bigotimes_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}(B_{p}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}{E_{w}^{\prime}}).

Strictly speaking, I should work with completed tensor product ⊗^\hat{\otimes}, but I will avoid doing this for simplicity.

§ 7.7.2 The theta-values locii Θ~J​o​s​h​iB˘⊗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}} and Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘⊗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}}

∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sBEw′→B˘L′,p⊗\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}B_{E_{w}^{\prime}}\to{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}_{L^{\prime},p}

which maps an element (xw)w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s⟼⨂w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sxw(x_{w})_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}\longmapsto\bigotimes_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}x_{w} and

∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s(Bp⊗ℚpEw′)→𝐁˘⊗L′,p\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}(B_{p}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}{E_{w}^{\prime}})\to{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}_{L^{\prime},p}

which maps an element (xw)w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s⟼⨂w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sxw(x_{w})_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}\longmapsto\bigotimes_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}x_{w}. This can be applied to lifts of theta-values in ∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sBEw′\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}B_{E_{w}^{\prime}} and ∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s(Bp⊗ℚpEw′)\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}(B_{p}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}{E_{w}^{\prime}}) respectively. In particular one may take the image of the theta-values locii ∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sΘ~J​o​s​h​iBEw′\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}}{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{B_{E_{w}^{\prime}}} in (B˘L′,p⊗)ℓ∗\left({\breve{B}}^{\otimes}_{L^{\prime},p}\right)^{\ell^{*}} and similarly in (𝐁˘⊗L′,p)ℓ∗\left({\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}_{L^{\prime},p}\right)^{\ell^{*}}. This gives us theta-values locii

(7.7.2.1) Θ~J​o​s​h​iB˘⊗⊂∏p,𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅(B˘L′,p⊗)ℓ∗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}}\subset\prod_{p,\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\left({\breve{B}}^{\otimes}_{L^{\prime},p}\right)^{\ell^{*}}

and

(7.7.2.2) Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘⊗⊂∏p,𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅(𝐁˘⊗L′,p)ℓ∗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}}\subset\prod_{p,\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\left({\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}_{L^{\prime},p}\right)^{\ell^{*}}

§ 7.7.3 The fundamental estimate

Theorem 7.7.3.1.

Let C/LC/L be an elliptic curve and suppose ℓ\ell is an odd prime such that § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3 hold for C,L,ℓC,L,\ell. Let L′/LL^{\prime}/L be the finite extension of LL defined in § 3.1, § 3.3. For any w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}, let pwp_{w} be the rational prime lying below ww. Choose a normalization of the pwp_{w}-adic valuation on, ℂpw{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}, a completed algebraic closure of ℚpw{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{w}} to be such that for any uniformizer πw∈OLw′\pi_{w}\in{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}} one has

|πw|ℂpw=pw−1.\left|\pi_{w}\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}}=p_{w}^{-1}.

and a similar assertion for |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘⊗|𝐁˘⊗\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}}\right|_{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}}.

Proof.

By [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ], for each 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset, the set Θ~J​o​s​h​iB˘,p{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{B}}}{}_{,p} contains a pure tensor ⊗w|pZw\otimes_{w|p}Z_{w} such that

|Zw|BEw′,ρ≥|qw1/2​ℓ|ℂpw,\left|Z_{w}\right|_{B_{E^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}\geq\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{w}}},

with ZwZ_{w} a theta-Pilot object for X/Ew′X/E_{w}^{\prime} as defined earlier and by [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ] and its proof.

Now the properties of tensor products ⊗w|pBEw′\otimes_{w|p}B_{E^{\prime}_{w}} established in Lemma 7.6.4.1, Lemma 7.6.5.1 show that

(7.7.3.2) |⊗w|pZw|BEw′,ρ=∏w|p|Zw|BEw′,ρ.\left|\otimes_{w|p}Z_{w}\right|_{B_{E^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}=\prod_{w|p}\left|Z_{w}\right|_{B_{E^{\prime}_{w}},\rho}.

By [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ], for each 0<ρ<10<\rho<1 and each pp for which 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset and each w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p} one has the lower bound

Thus by taking products over all pp for which 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset and the extending the product (trivially) to all pp and all primes w|pw|p in L′L^{\prime} one gets:
