§ 7.8 The theta-values locii in 𝐁˘p⊗Bp𝐁˘p⊗Bp⋯⊗Bp𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}\otimes_{B_{p}}{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}\otimes_{B_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{B_{p}}{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} and in 𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}

One may further exploit multiplicative properties one has available in the situation at hand but which is not utilized in the construction of Θ~J​o​s​h​iB˘⊗⊂(𝐁˘⊗)ℓ∗{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{B}}^{\otimes}}\subset\left({\breve{\mathbf{B}}^{\otimes}}\right)^{\ell^{*}} given above. This construction does not explicitly demonstrate the tensor packet structure which is asserted in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3]. I will now demonstrate this as follows.

§ 7.8.1 Multiplication of lifts of theta-values

Since 𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} is a ring, one can also multiply elements in it. More precisely given a tuple of elements (b˘1,…,b˘ℓ∗)∈𝐁˘pℓ∗(\breve{b}_{1},\ldots,\breve{b}_{\ell^{*}})\in{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}^{\ell^{*}} one can also multiply them in 𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} i.e. consider the mapping

𝐁˘pℓ∗→𝐁˘p,{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}^{\ell^{*}}\to{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p},

given by

(b˘1,…,b˘ℓ∗)⟼b˘1⋅b˘2⋯b˘ℓ∗.(\breve{b}_{1},\ldots,\breve{b}_{\ell^{*}})\longmapsto\breve{b}_{1}\cdot\breve{b}_{2}\cdots\breve{b}_{\ell^{*}}.

This is multi-linear in each coordinate. This multi-linear mapping factors though the tensor product. In this case it is convenient to treat 𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} as a finite BpB_{p}-algebra and consider the natural factorization

(7.8.1.1)

where the first mapping is (b1,…,bℓ∗)⟼b1⊗b2⊗⋯⊗bℓ∗(b_{1},\ldots,b_{\ell^{*}})\longmapsto b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\otimes\cdots\otimes b_{\ell^{*}} and the second is the natural mapping b1⊗b2⊗⋯⊗bℓ∗⟼b1⋅b2⋅⋯⋅bℓ∗b_{1}\otimes b_{2}\otimes\cdots\otimes b_{\ell^{*}}\longmapsto b_{1}\cdot b_{2}\cdot\cdots\cdot b_{\ell^{*}}.

The advantage of these considerations becomes clear from the following elementary decomposition lemma:

Lemma 7.8.1.2.

One has the decomposition of the BpB_{p}-algebra:

𝐁˘p⊗Bp𝐁˘p⊗Bp⋯⊗Bp𝐁˘p=Bp⊗ℚp(⨁αEα′′){\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}\otimes_{B_{p}}{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}\otimes_{B_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{B_{p}}{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}=B_{p}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\left(\bigoplus_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}\right)

where the sum on the right runs over a finite multi-set of finite extensions Eα′′E_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} contained in ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p}.

Proof.

This is immediate from the definition of 𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} and properties of tensor products. Indeed, since

(7.8.1.3) 𝐁˘p=Bℂp♭,ℚp⊗ℚp(⨁w|p,w∈𝕍LmodEw){\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}=B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\left(\bigoplus_{w|p,w\in\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}}}E_{w}\right)

and as the tensor product 𝐁˘p⊗Bp𝐁˘p{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p}\otimes_{B_{p}}{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}_{p} reduces to computing tensor products of a finite collection of pp-adic fields, and so the assertion of the lemma follows.

Remark 7.8.1.4.

In [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3], especially [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.1.1, Remark 3.9.1], and [Mochizuki, 2021d], Mochizuki forces the tensor product structure and arrives essentially at the above lemma. Especially note that appearance of finite number of pp-adic fields Eα′′E_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime} in Lemma 7.8.1.2 and (hence also in Theorem 7.8.3.1 below) should be compared to [Mochizuki, 2021c, § 3, Remark 3.1.1] and [Mochizuki, 2021d]. ∙\bullet

§ 7.9 theta-values locii and compactly bounded subsets of M1,1​(ℚ¯){M}_{1,1}({\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}})

This paragraph is not needed in the main proofs. Let me remark that in the above constructions, and in Theorem 7.8.3.1, I have suppressed from the notation Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘{{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\breve{\mathbf{B}}} the dependence of this set on X/LX/L (and ℓ\ell). I will ignore ℓ\ell for the moment and write Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(X/L){{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}(X/L) to indicate dependence on X/LX/L. Let M1,1​(L){M}_{1,1}(L) be the LL-valued points of moduli stack M1,1{M}_{1,1} of 11-pointed elliptic curves.

Then it is tempting to expect that the following makes sense: let

(7.9.1) Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(M1,1​(L))=⋃X/L∈M1,1​(L)Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(X/L).{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}({M}_{1,1}(L))=\bigcup_{X/L\in{M}_{1,1}(L)}{{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}(X/L).

and expect that

(7.9.2) |Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(M1,1​(L))|𝐁˘<∞.\left|{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}({M}_{1,1}(L))\right|_{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}<\infty.

Especially if this is true then any upper bound for it can serve as a uniform upper bound for Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(X/L){{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}(X/L) for every X/L∈M1,1​(L)X/L\in{M}_{1,1}(L).

However eq. (7.9.2) is too optimistic. Fixing initial theta data as in § 3.1 means one is considering elliptic curves over LL which acquire semi-stable reduction over extensions of L′/LL^{\prime}/L, however the field L′L^{\prime} will vary as the curve varies in moduli in general (the degree L′/LL^{\prime}/L remains bounded by Lemma 3.4.2.1).

On the other hand such bounds may exist for arbitrary choice of compactly bounded subsets of M1,1​(ℚ¯){M}_{1,1}({\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}) (see [Mochizuki, 2010] for definition of compactly bounded subsets). Let ℚ¯≤d{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}^{\leq d} be the union of all finite extensions of ℚ{\mathbb{Q}} (all contained in ℚ¯{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}) of degrees bounded by the dd (specified by for example by Lemma 3.4.2.1).

For K⊂M1,1​(ℚ¯){K}\subset{M}_{1,1}({\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}) a compactly bounded subset supported at a finite set of rational primes Σ\Sigma one can expect to define

Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(K∩M1,1​(ℚ¯≤d)){\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}({K}\cap{M}_{1,1}({\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}^{\leq d}))

and one can expect to prove that

(7.9.3) |Θ^J​o​s​h​i𝐁˘​(K∩M1,1​(ℚ¯≤d))|𝐁˘<∞.\left|{\widehat{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}({K}\cap{M}_{1,1}({\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}^{\leq d}))\right|_{{\breve{\mathbf{B}}}}<\infty.

Very roughly this is the idea behind the computations of [Mochizuki, 2021d, Corollary 2.2]

8 A ‘Rosetta Stone’ for [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] and [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]

Let me now provide a fundamental ‘Rosetta Stone’ (Rosetta Stone Fragments 8.3.5, 8.3.6, 8.5, 8.7.1, 8.11.3) for the readers, so that they are able to translate objects and concepts between the theories of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] and [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

Once a reader has assimilated and understood the contents of the Rosetta Stone Fragments 8.3.5, 8.3.6, 8.5, 8.7.1, 8.11.3, hopefully, the readers will be persuaded that there exists corresponding objects in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] which allows one to establish the proofs of the relevant claims of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] with complete clarity.

§ 8.1 How to use the Rosetta Stone for reading [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]

The Rosetta Stone Fragments 8.3.5, 8.3.6, 8.5, 8.7.1, 8.11.3 must be read along with my discussion of other objects of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] such as Frobenioids and Hodge Theaters provided here in § 10. My work together with the (Rosetta Stone Fragments 8.3.5, 8.3.6, 8.5, 8.7.1, 8.11.3) provides an adequate toolkit for the reader to be able to navigate [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. [The existence of distinct such objects is asserted without proof in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].]

§ 8.1.1 Notation

Notations and assumptions of § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3 will strictly be in force for full compatibility with [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. This means LL is a number field with no real embeddings, C/LC/L is an elliptic curve and X=C−{O}/LX=C-\{O\}/L is the hyperbolic curve (of strict Belyi Type by Mochizuki’s definition) of topological type (1,1)(1,1). Notably, the isomorphism class [X/L][X/L] of X/LX/L defines a moduli point in the moduli stack M1,1{M}_{1,1} and the field of definition of this moduli point is LmodL_{\rm mod} by § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3.

This data, by the results of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper), provides the category 𝔍⁡(X/L)\mathfrak{J}(X/L) of the adelic arithmetic Teichmuller space associated to X/LX/L [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022]. Each object of this category, by means of [Joshi, 2023a, Proposition ], provides an arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)\mathfrak{arith}(L) of LL. As is demonstrated in [Joshi, 2023a], 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)\mathfrak{arith}(L) is a deformation of the arithmetic of number field LL. Working with holomorphoid (X,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L))(X,\mathfrak{arith}(L)) (Definition 2.1.2) allows us to view XX viewed as a scheme for the version of arithmetic of LL provided by the particular arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)\mathfrak{arith}(L). As a scheme X/𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)X/\mathfrak{arith}(L) is, of course isomorphic to X/LX/L. For the properties of arithmeticoids see [Joshi, 2023a, § ]. To be sure, a holomorphoid provides a global arithmetic structure and by Definition 2.1.5, it also provides local arithmetic holomorphic structures at all primes v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}. For the properties of arithmetic holomorphic structures and arithmetic teichmuller spaces see [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2023a, Joshi, 2022].

§ 8.2 Section 8.3.5: Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures

An idea central to both the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper) and especially [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], is the notion of arithmetic holomorphic structures.

§ 8.2.1 Arithmetic Holomorphic structures in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]

I will take the definition of arithmetic holomorphic structures as given in [Joshi, 2021a, Definition ], [Joshi, 2022, Definition 4.1] (which sets out the local theory at each prime of LL) and demonstrates that this provides all corresponding local data of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. [Existence of such structures is not demonstrated in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].] The global theory of arithmetic holomorphic structures is detailed in [Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a].

§ 8.2.2 The role of geometric base-points in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]

Mochizuki’s [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d], is founded upon Mochizuki’s Key Principle of Inter-Universality, which is stated in [Mochizuki, 2021a, § I3, Page 25]. According to this principle, Mochizuki’s [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] requires one to work with arbitrary geometric base-points. Furthermore, as Mochizuki reminds us [Mochizuki, 2021a, Page 26] (and in many other places in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] and [Mochizuki, 2020]), the domains and codomains of all the key operations of his theory, namely 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-links and Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-links, refer to distinct geometric base-points.

The reader may ask: why is it important to work with arbitrary geometric base-points? Working with arbitrary geometric base-points is the anabelian proxy for deformations of algebraic varieties. In [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] the idea is to use arbitrary geometric base-points (in the theory of tempered fundamental groups) as giving deformations of arithmetic. However, the exact mechanism by which one obtains such deformations was not established in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] but has been precisely quantified in [Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2023a]. Let me note that distinct geometric base-points also play an important role in the Chabauty-Kim Theory of [Kim, 2005] (i.e. usage of arbitrary geometric base-points is important in other Diophantine contexts).

My definition of arithmetic holomorphic structures [Joshi, 2021a, Definition ] (and also see Definition 2.1.5) includes geometric base-points and hence my approach is fully compatible with the approach taken in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d].

The following table compares the notion of geometric base-points in the theory of étale and tempered fundamental groups.

Remark 8.2.2.1.
  1. (1)

    While Mochizuki recognized the centrality of this principle for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d], Mochizuki’s approach to his theory is group theoretic and stays focused on utilizing the group theory surrounding the tempered fundamental group as the key tool in building his theory, however, his approach ignores the rich arithmetic, algebra and geometry which arbitrary geometric base-points for tempered fundamental groups provide (as can be seen in the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper)). This is an important difference in our respective viewpoints.

  2. (2)

    Let me remark that the anabelian reconstruction techniques of [Mochizuki, 2012, Mochizuki, 2013, Mochizuki, 2015] are of considerable importance in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]. However, [Mochizuki, 2015, Theorem 1.9] (which is the main theorem of that paper) does not determine the geometric base-point datum while, in accordance with Mochizuki’s Key Principle of Inter-Universality, this (undetermined) datum is of central importance in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d].

  3. (3)

    Let me also say that, as far as I am aware, though Mochizuki’s statement of this principle has appeared in all versions of [Mochizuki, 2021a] (for example it is included in the hard copy of RIMS-Preprint from 2012), neither this principle nor the centrality of the role of arbitrary geometric base-points (in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]) finds any mention in [Fesenko, 2015], [Tan, 2018], [Scholze and Stix, 2018], [Yamashita, 2019], [Dupuy and Hilado, 2020b, Dupuy and Hilado, 2020a], [Scholze, 2021], [Saïdi, 2022].

∙\bullet

§ 8.2.3 Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]

One notable problem with the claims of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] is that the existence of distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures is not established in it and my reading of [Mochizuki, 2022] is that this issue cannot be resolved by methods of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. My central observation is that arithmetic holomorphic structures provided here in § 8.2.1 also provide arithmetic holomorphic structures in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. My comparison of arithmetic holomorphic structures in the two theories is given in Section 8.3.5.

§ 8.2.4 Fundamental Dichotomy of an Arithmetic Holomorphic Structure

Arithmetic holomorphic structures in both the theories ([Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] and [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]) consists of two parts:

  1. (1)

    The first portion is tuned into arithmetic and topology of the field, and geometry of the variety while

  2. (2)

    the second portion tracks independent changes of valuations and hence requires recording the value group.

I call this the fundamental dichotomy of an Arithmetic Holomorphic Structure. Importantly, arithmetic holomorphic structures in both the theories exhibit such a dichotomy. The non-triviality of the theories rests on exhibiting the existence of plurality of such data. This is a central problem for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] which is not resolved by the artificial “resetting of logic” recommended in [Mochizuki, 2022]; on the other hand the theory of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper) provides a natural plurality of such data from the very beginning and these data can be applied to exhibit the corresponding data in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

§ 8.3 Mochizuki’s Dichotomy: Étale-pictures and Frobenius-pictures via [Joshi, 2021a]

Mochizuki has a similar dichotomy for arithmetic holomorphic structures. The two portions of Mochizuki’s dichotomy for arithmetic holomorphic structures are termed in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] as

  1. (1)

    an “étale-picture” (see [Mochizuki, 2021a, § 3, Corollary 3.9]) and,

  2. (2)

    a “Frobenius-pictures” (see [Mochizuki, 2021a, § 3, Corollary 3.8]).

The relationship between Dichotomy of Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures sss:fund-dichotomy and Mochizuki’s dichotomy of étale picture (or étale like data) and Frobenius-picture or (Frobenius-like data) is described for each prime v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L} separately. Hence fix a v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L} and let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}} be an arithmetic holomorphic structure on X/LvX/L_{v}. Let yv=(Kv,iKv:Kv♭≃Fv)y_{v}=(K_{v},i_{K_{v}}:K_{v}^{\flat}\simeq F_{v}) be point of YFv,Lv{Y}_{F_{v},L_{v}} provided by 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}}. Then I claim that Mochizuki’s Dichotomy of étale-picture and Frobenius-pictures arises from the Dichotomy of Arith Holomorphic Structure given by the datum of the local holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)y\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y} as by Proposition 8.3.1.1 and Proposition 8.3.2.1 and is summarized in Section 8.3.5:

§ 8.3.1 Mochizuki’s Étale Picture or étale-like data

Mochizuki’s étale-picture consists of the group theoretic data provided by the proposition below:

Proposition 8.3.1.1.

Each holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} of X/LX/L provides, for each v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}, Mochizuki’s étale-like picture, labeled by the geometric data of the (local) holomorphoid of 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}} from which it arises and consists of the following data:

  1. (1)

    the algebraically closed perfectoid field KvK_{v} which contains an isometrically embedded ℚpv{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{v}} and hence KvK_{v} provides an algebraic closure of any finite extension LvL_{v} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. Thus KvK_{v} provides a preferred algebraic closure Lv⊂L¯v;Kv⊂KvL_{v}\subset\overline{L}_{v;K_{v}}\subset K_{v} of LvL_{v} and hence provides a preferred isomorph GLv;Kv=Gal⁡(L¯v/Lv)≃GLvG_{L_{v};K_{v}}={\rm Gal}(\overline{L}_{v}/L_{v})\simeq G_{L_{v}} of absolute Galois group of LvL_{v};

  2. (2)

    the Galois category TempX/Lv;Kv\mathrm{Temp}_{X/L_{v};K_{v}} (as defined in [André, 2003a, Chap. III, 2.1.4]) of tempered coverings of XLva​nX^{an}_{L_{v}} which are defined over finite extensions of LvL_{v} contained in KvK_{v};

  3. (3)

    and a preferred isomorph ΠX/Lv;Kvt​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v};K_{v}} of the tempered fundamental group of X/LvX/L_{v} (see [Joshi, 2021a, Theorem ]).

  4. (4)

    Importantly, in my theory, this data appears with the distinguishable label given by the holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}} from which this “étale-picture” arises.

Proof.

The proof is clear.

Remark 8.3.1.2.

There are other étale like data in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], these may be also obtained in a similar manner as above. ∙\bullet

§ 8.3.2 Frobenius-picture or Frobenius-like data

Now I claim that 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}} also provides Mochizuki’s Frobenius-picture or Frobenius-like data.

Proposition 8.3.2.1.

Let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} be a holomorphoid of X/LX/L and let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/Lv​(Fv)yv\mathfrak{hol}_{X/L_{v}}(F_{v})_{y_{v}} be the local holomorphoid of X/LvX/L_{v} (for any v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}) given by 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}}. Then

  1. (1)

    the isometry iKv:Kv♭≃Fvi_{K_{v}}:K_{v}^{\flat}\simeq F_{v} identifies the value group of KvK_{v} with the value group of FvF_{v} [Scholze, 2012];

  2. (2)

    in particular for all anabelomorphic holomorphoids of X/LvX/L_{v} in the category 𝔍​(X/Lv)Fv\mathfrak{J}(X/L_{v})_{F_{v}}, one has a fixed value group–namely the value group of FvF_{v}, to compare valuations.

  3. (3)

    let L¯v⊂Kv\overline{L}_{v}\subset K_{v} be the algebraic closure of LvL_{v} in KvK_{v} and OL¯v⊳=OL¯v⊳−{0}⊂OKv⊳−{0}{O}_{\overline{L}_{v}}^{\triangleright}={O}_{\overline{L}_{v}}^{\triangleright}-\{0\}\subset{O}_{K_{v}}^{\triangleright}-\{0\} be the multiplicative monoid of the ring of integers OL¯v⊂L¯v⊂Kv{O}_{\overline{L}_{v}}\subset\overline{L}_{v}\subset K_{v}. Then OL¯v⊳{O}_{\overline{L}_{v}}^{\triangleright} is a Frobenius-like (monoidal) data of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c],[Mochizuki, 2020].

Proof.

This is clear.

The value group information provided by this proposition is Mochizuki’s Frobenius picture [Mochizuki, 2021a].

Remark 8.3.2.2.

Let me remark that the definition of K♭K^{\flat} [Scholze, 2012] shows how Frobenius i.e. pt​hp^{th}-powers play a central role in the construction of K♭K^{\flat}. So the term Frobenius-like or Frobenius-picture is quite reasonable in this context. One important point to be noted is that even if KK is fixed, there are many inequivalent untilts, (K,K♭≃F)(K,K^{\flat}\simeq F), of FF and hence there are many inequivalent Frobenius-like pictures. There are other types of Frobenius-like data in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]. These are also provided by the datum 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/E​(F)y\mathfrak{hol}_{X/E}(F)_{y}. ∙\bullet

§ 8.3.3 Existence of Étale and Frobenius Pictures

Since the geometric data of holomorphoids of X/LX/L provide étale-pictures and Frobenius-pictures of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] one has now established the following:

Theorem 8.3.3.1.

Each holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} of X/LX/L, provides, for each v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}, an arithmetic holomorphic structure in the sense of [Joshi, 2022] and also provides Mochizuki’s Dichotomy of an arithmetic holomorphic structure: namely an “Étale picture” and a “Frobenius picture” in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], which is indexed by the holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} which it arises from. In particular, there exist many inequivalent étale and Frobenius pictures in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

Remark 8.3.3.2.

I will not use the terminology of étale and Frobenius pictures, but the above results make it clear that my approach does indeed have all the properties claimed by Mochizuki in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] where he has asserted the existence of such inequivalent data without proofs. ∙\bullet

§ 8.3.4 L∗L^{*}-action on Étale and Frobenius pictures

There is natural action of L∗L^{*} on the set of pairs consisting of (étale,Frobenius)-pictures and the justification of the existence of this action is inadequate (in my opinion) in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], though Mochizuki asserts the principal the property of this action [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 1.2.3(ii)], namely that if α∈L∗\alpha\in L^{*} acts trivially, then α\alpha is a root of unity.

In [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ], I demonstrate the existence of the natural multiplicative action of L∗​↷​𝐘𝐋L^{*}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\mathscrbf{Y}_{L}. From the above description of (étale,Frobenius)-pictures, one sees at once, that L∗​↷​𝐘𝐋L^{*}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\mathscrbf{Y}_{L} provides the required action on the sets of such pairs (arising, as above, from arithmeticoids in 𝐘𝐋\mathscrbf{Y}_{L}). The fundamental property of this action alluded to in the above paragraph is proved in [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ].

§ 8.6 Primes-strips à la [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] from [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]

A prime-strip ([Mochizuki, 2021a, § I1, Page 9]) in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] consists of certain monoidal data equipped with the action of the local Galois group. While the notion of prime-strips of [Mochizuki, 2021a, § I1, Page 9] is not used in the theory of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a], prime-strips are certainly available in the theory of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] and there is a correspondence between prime-strips of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] and those of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]. This correspondence between prime-strips of the two theories may be transcribed using Section 8.5 (reading it from left to right) from the corresponding object in the rightmost column (which provides objects in the theory of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper)). For example:

to indicate the datum of the point of the Arithmetic Teichmuller Space giving rise to this particular prime-strip. So where Mochizuki [Mochizuki, 2021a, § I1, Page 9] writes

§ 8.6.1 Realified Prime-strips a la Mochizuki from [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]

Let v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L} and let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv=(X/Lv,X/Kyv)\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}}=(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}}) be a holomorphoid of X/LvX/L_{v}. Recall that by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018], the data of the point yv∈Yℂp♭,Lvy_{v}\in{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{v}} provides a valuation |−|Kyv\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{v}}} on the residue field KyvK_{y_{v}} and hence a valuation |−|L¯v\left|-\right|_{\overline{L}_{v}} on the algebraic closure L¯v⊂Kyv\overline{L}_{v}\subset K_{y_{v}} of LvL_{v} contained in KyvK_{y_{v}}.

For datum of this holomorphoid, and for each prime-strip

FJ​o​s​h​i?​(𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv){F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{?}(\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}})

given in Section 8.5 arising from this datum, one also has a realified prime-strip

(8.6.1.1) FJ​o​s​h​i|?(𝔥𝔬𝔩(X/Lv)yv){F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{|?}(\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}})

in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. My notation for realified prime-strips follows Mochizuki’s convention [Mochizuki, 2021a, Table I1.2 on page 9] which puts an extra vertical bar |?|? at the start of the decoration ?? to denote the corresponding realified version of that prime-strip.

Thus for example, the realified prime-strip corresponding to the prime-strip

FJ​o​s​h​i⊢▶×μ(X/Lv,X/Kyv)=GLv↷OL¯v×μ×q(X/Lv,X/Kyv)ℕ{F}^{\vdash\blacktriangleright\times\mu}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}})=G_{L_{v}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}{O}_{\overline{L}_{v}}^{\times\mu}\times q_{(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}})}^{\mathbb{N}}

will be denoted by

and consists of the data

(FJ​o​s​h​i⊢▶×μ(X/Lv,X/Kyv),|−|Kyv:Kyv→ℝ)({F}^{\vdash\blacktriangleright\times\mu}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}}),\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{v}}}:K_{y_{v}}\to{\mathbb{R}})

consisting of the prime-strip FJ​o​s​h​i⊩▶×μ(X/Lv,X/Kyv){F}^{\Vdash\blacktriangleright\times\mu}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}}) plus the valuation

given by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018] which allows us to compute absolute values of elements of L¯v⊂Kyv\overline{L}_{v}\subset K_{y_{v}} and in particular calculate the absolute value of the Tate parameter

q(X/Lv,X/Kyv)∈Kyv.q_{(X/L_{v},X/K_{y_{v}})}\in K_{y_{v}}.
Remark 8.6.1.2.

Mochizuki’s method of keeping track of valuations is through the notion of realified Frobenioids. By my discussion of Frobenioids in § 10.2, one can use the given valuation (Kyv,|−|Kyv→ℝ)(K_{y_{v}},\left|-\right|_{K_{y_{v}}}\to{\mathbb{R}}) to obtain the relevant realified frobenioid. ∙\bullet

These observations are summarized in the following proposition.

Proposition 8.6.1.3.

Each holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} with 𝐲={yv}v∈𝕍L{\bf y}=\{y_{v}\}_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}} provides (for each v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}) an isomorph,

FJ​o​s​h​i?​(X/Lv)yv,{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{?}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}},

of Mochizuki’s prime-strip

FM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,Lv?{F}_{Mochizuki,L_{v}}^{?}

(as in Section 8.5) and also an isomorph

FJ​o​s​h​i|?(X/Lv)yv{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{|?}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}}

of the corresponding realified prime-strip

FM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,Lv|?{F}_{Mochizuki,L_{v}}^{|?}

(as in Section 8.5). In particular, there are many geometrically and arithmetically distinguishable prime-strips in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

Remark 8.6.1.4.

In particular, Proposition 8.6.1.3 provides clearly distinguishable geometric labels for the prime-strips. This means that there exist many distinct (but abstractly isomorphic) prime-strips in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]– this is needed in the proofs of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11] and [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. ∙\bullet

§ 8.7 The fundamental Prime-Strips of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022]

In the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper), I do not use the notion of prime-strips but it is certainly possible to define prime-strips as indicated in Section 8.5. But Section 8.7.1 shows that there is however a more natural and even canonical object which serves this role and is given by

(8.7.1) GLv​↷​𝔾^m​(Oℂp♭)≃GLv​↷​Bφ=p.G_{L_{v}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{m}({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}})\simeq G_{L_{v}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}B^{\varphi=p}.

(the isomorphism is given by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Proposition 4.4.6]) which I shall call the canonical prime-strip at pp provided by the theory of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper). By Section 8.7.1, there are natural, and equally important, variants of (8.7.1):

(8.7.2) GLv​↷​|Yℂp♭,ℚp|,\displaystyle G_{L_{v}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\left|{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\right|,
and
(8.7.3) GLv​↷​|Xℂp♭,ℚp|.\displaystyle G_{L_{v}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\left|{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\right|.
Remark 8.7.4.

The fundamental prime-strip at pp (8.7.1) provides a number of advantages over Mochizuki’s definition of prime-strips (8.6.2). Notably, I demonstrate (in Theorem 8.8.3) that the set of prime-strips in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] is equipped with a natural action of GLvG_{L_{v}} which corresponds to the galois action on the set of arithmetic holomorphic structures via its action on Yℂp♭,Lv{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{v}} i.e. the natural operations of the theory permute the prime strips of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. This is an important point, even for the proofs of [Mochizuki, 2021c], however, it is not established in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. ∙\bullet

§ 8.7.1 Section 8.7.1

The next Section 8.7.1 provides a detailed comparison of prime-strips in the two theories.

§ 8.8 Gluing along prime-strips à la Mochizuki via [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a]

Now let me prove that the analog of Mochizuki’s gluing of prime-strips [Mochizuki, 2021a, Page 23] exists in the theory of present series of papers because of Theorem 8.8.3.

Let me describe Mochizuki’s gluing of two prime-strips of the type:

(8.8.1) FM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i⊢▶×μ=Gv↷O¯v×μ×qℕ{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\vdash\blacktriangleright\times\mu}=G_{v}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\overline{{O}}_{v}^{\times\mu}\times q^{\mathbb{N}}

the core idea of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], especially see [Mochizuki, 2021a, Page 23], is that group theoretic data of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] i.e. two isomorphs (Π1,Π¯1)(\Pi_{1},\overline{\Pi}_{1}) and (Π2,Π¯2)(\Pi_{2},\overline{\Pi}_{2}) of (Π,Π¯)(\Pi,\overline{\Pi}) are glued along an isomorphism of the copies of

FM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i⊢▶×μ=Gv↷O¯v×μ×qℕ.{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\vdash\blacktriangleright\times\mu}=G_{v}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\overline{{O}}_{v}^{\times\mu}\times q^{\mathbb{N}}.

provided by each of these pairs of fundamental groups.

Remark 8.8.2.

[Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] attempts to accomplish this gluing [Mochizuki, 2021a, Page 23] without explicitly exhibiting the existence of distinct primes-strips, i.e. prime-strips in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] do not have any arithmetically (or any natural or Teichmuller Theoretic) distinguishable labels. Mochizuki’s gluing claim [Mochizuki, 2021a, Page 23] is established here in Theorem 8.8.3 by means of the theory developed in the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper) and applies to context of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. ∙\bullet

In the parlance of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], [Mochizuki, 2020], the isomorphisms of prime-strips given by Theorem 8.8.3 can be stated as follows: one has two distinct copies of Mochizuki’s prime-strips F?M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i1{}^{1}{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{?} and F?M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i2{}^{2}{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{?} which are identified via an abstract isomorphism

However, let me caution the reader that the two sides of this diagram make separate contributions to the set whose construction is asserted in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. So this gluing does not really represent the creation of a new geometric object by gluing (as asserted in [Mochizuki, 2022, Example 2.4.7]). That is why I have disagreed with claims of [Mochizuki, 2022, § 3.4] and [Mochizuki, 2022, Example 2.4.7]. More precisely, for a workable Teichmuller Theory of the sort one wants to establish here, one must demonstrate that both sides of the above diagram exist for intrinsic reasons and hence the analogy with projective line [Mochizuki, 2022, Example 2.4.7] is highly misleading. ∙\bullet

§ 8.9 Mochizuki’s log-links

The local theory of Mochizuki’s 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-links is detailed in [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem 10.15.1] [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ]. Notably, it identifies the 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-link at a fixed prime v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L} explicitly. That assertion provides the following global definition of Mochizuki’s 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log} from the point of view of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper):

Definition 8.9.1.

Let X/LX/L be as defined in § 2.4 (or more generally, let XX be a geometrically connected, quasi-projective variety over a number field LL with no real embeddings). § 8.10 Mochizuki’s Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Links

My approach to Mochizuki’s theta-links (specifically the Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-links) is detailed in Definition 4.2.2, § 4.2.1, Theorem 4.2.2.1 and [Joshi, 2023b] and hence will not be repeated here. In [Joshi, 2023b, Appendix], I establish the existence of theta-links in the context of proofs of the Geometric Szpiro Inequality [Amorós et al., 2000], [Zhang, 2001].

§ 8.11 Mochizuki’s “Three Indeterminacies” [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11]

As I have pointed out in [Joshi, 2021b], from the point of view of classical Teichmuller spaces and Arithmetic Teichmuller spaces, if one holds the (tempered) fundamental group fixed, then the holomorphic structure (i.e. the holomorphoid) giving rise to the said group, is necessarily indeterminate i.e the mapping

𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv⟼ΠX/Lvt​e​m​p\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}}\longmapsto\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v}}

does not determine the holomorphoid i.e. the arithmetic holomorphic structure uniquely.

More precisely, if the topological isomorphism class of the fundamental group ΠX/Lvt​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v}} is held fixed, then a holomorphoid 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}} giving rise to this group is necessarily an indeterminate quantity as there are many distinct holomorphoids 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}} (in the classical case, there are many distinct complex structures) which provide the said group.

§ 8.11.1 

So in my view, Mochizuki’s Three Indeterminacies (see [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11]) which underlie his theory, are necessarily consequences of the existence of Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces. Let me illustrate how this remark allows one to arrive at Mochizuki’s three indeterminacies. I am listing them as they appear in the theory in the order they get applied in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11 and Corollary 3.12] (the perspective is my own, Mochizuki’s perspective is discussed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11]).

Ind3

In [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem A (aka Theorem 3.11), Page 425], this indeterminacy arises from the upper semi-compatibility of 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-Links. From my point of view, this indeterminacy arises by [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ] (reader may recall that in [Joshi, 2023b, § ], I have established that working with the Frobenius orbit of a point on YL¯^v♭,Lv{Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}} corresponds to working with a column of 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-links). To understand this, let 𝐲0{\bf y}_{0} be the standard point § 4.4. This choice is not canonical and one can also use 𝝋⁡(𝐲0)\boldsymbol{\varphi}({\bf y}_{0}) as a standard point. Write 𝐲0=(yv)v∈𝕍L′{\bf y}_{0}=(y_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}. One wants to understand how the choice of 𝐲0{\bf y}_{0} over 𝝋⁡(𝐲0)\boldsymbol{\varphi}({\bf y}_{0}) affects arithmetic holomorphic structures and related Galois cohomology calculations. The local aspect of this, at each vv, is explicated in [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ]. To recall what [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem ] provides, let pvp_{v} be the residue characteristic of vv. Then at each vv, the choice of yvy_{v} over φv​(yv)\varphi_{v}(y_{v}) means that the homomorphism

ℤpv​(1)→Bℂpv♭,ℚpv{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{v}}(1)\to B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{v}}}

which send a generator to the element t∈Bℂpv♭,ℚpvt\in B_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{v}}} is uniquely determined only up to a pp-multiple.

Ind2

This indeterminacy arises as a consequence of [Joshi, 2021a, Theorem ], [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ] and is the indeterminacy of the point 𝐲∈𝐘𝐋′{\bf y}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}} which provides the arithmetic holomorphic structure at each v∈𝕍L′v\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}. One can write this Mochizuki style as indeterminacy with respect to ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-linear isomorphisms σ:𝔾^m​(Oℂpv♭)→𝔾^m​(Oℂpv♭)\sigma:\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{m}({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat}})\to\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{m}({O}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat}}) ([Joshi, 2021a, Theorem ] and [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ] which demonstrate how such an isomorphism changes arithmetic holomorphic structures).

In other words, Mochizuki’s Ind2 is the indeterminacy with respect to the choice of a point of the space of arithmetic holomorphic structures provided by the relevant Fargues-Fontaine curve Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}. The precise demonstration of the existence of Ind2 is an important contribution of [Joshi, 2021a]. As remarked in [Joshi, 2021a, § ] and [Joshi, 2023a, Remark ], this indeterminacy is the arithmetic analog, at all primes, of the Virasoro action in the Geometric Langlands Program [Beilinson and Drinfel’d, 2000].

Ind1

This indeterminacy is what I have called anabelomorphy in [Joshi, 2020a]. Mochizuki’s contributed [Joshi, 2020a, § ] to clarify the role of anabelomorphy in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] and [Joshi, 2020a] provides other arithmetic consequences of anabelomorphy. The precise origins of Ind1 are quite arithmetic-geometric and not group theoretic as one might be led to believe because of the group theoretic methods of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. This indeterminacy Ind1 arises as follows. By [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a], one may view the Fargues-Fontaine curve Xℂpv♭,Lv{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}} (and especially Yℂp♭,Lv{Y}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},L_{v}}) as a sort of moduli for arithmetic holomorphic structures. By [Joshi, 2020b, Theorem 2.1], this moduli is not uniquely determined by the absolute Galois group

GLv=π1e​t​(Xℂpv♭,Lv).G_{L_{v}}=\pi_{1}^{et}({X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}}).

So one must consider all Fargues-Fontaine curves X{X} with π1e​t​(X)=GLv\pi_{1}^{et}({X})=G_{L_{v}} as providing arithmetic holomorphic structures which must be included to ensure the largest collection of arithmetic holomorphic structures over which one calculates averages in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. One way to understand this is that in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a], one may think of Xℂpv♭,Lv{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}} as a parameter space for arithmetic holomorphic structures up to an action of Frobenius, then Xℂpv♭,Lv{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}} is itself not uniquely identified by its étale fundamental group! [Also see [Joshi, 2023a, Remark ].] The following proposition is useful:

Proposition 8.11.1.1.

Let EE be a pp-adic field contained in an algebraic closure ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. Then there are only finitely many pp-adic fields E′⊂ℚ¯pE^{\prime}\subset{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} such that E′E^{\prime} is anabelomorphic to EE. In particular, for a fixed geometric point ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} (fixed for computing all the relevant fundamental groups), there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of Fargues-Fontaine curves Xℂp♭,E′{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E^{\prime}} which are anabelomorphic to Xℂp♭,E{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E} i.e such that

π1e​t​(Xℂp♭,E′)=GE.\pi_{1}^{et}({X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},E^{\prime}})=G_{E}.

Proof.

By [Joshi, 2020a], if EE is a pp-adic field, then its absolute degree [E:ℚp][E:{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}] is an amphoric quantity i.e. for any pp-adic field E′E^{\prime} which is anabelomorphic to EE, one has [E:ℚp]=[E′:ℚp][E:{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}]=[E^{\prime}:{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}]. By standard results–for example Krasner’s Lemma, there are only a finitely many subfields of ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} of a bounded degree over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. So the assertion follows from the main theorem of [Joshi, 2020b].

§ 8.11.2 Canonical Interpretation of Mochizuki’s Indeterminacies

One may describe these indeterminacies in the following canonical way:

Crystalline Indeterminacy or Mochizuki’s Ind3

The homomorphism ℤp​(1)→B→Bc​r​i​s{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1)\to B\to B_{cris} is determined uniquely only up to a pp-multiple. From my point of view, this indeterminacy corresponds to working with Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures arising from the Frobenius orbit of a point in the Fargues-Fontaine curve YL¯^v♭,Lv{Y}_{{\widehat{\overline{L}}_{v}}^{\flat},L_{v}} at all primes vv.

Inderminacy of Arith. Hol. Strs. or Mochizuki’s Ind2

For each v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}, the local holomorphoid of X/LvX/L_{v} is not uniquely determined by ΠX/Lvt​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v}}.

Anabelomorphy at all primes or Mochizuki’s Ind1

This arises from the fact that the isomorphism class of GLvG_{L_{v}} (for each prime vv) does not uniquely determine LvL_{v} in its isomorphism class. This was already clarified by Mochizuki who contributed [Joshi, 2020a, Paragraph 1.6]. My work provides a more canonical view of this: this indeterminacy arises from the fact [Joshi, 2020b] that the parameter space XF,E{X}_{F,E} for arithmetic holomorphic structures is not uniquely determined by it étale fundamental group.

§ 8.11.3 Section 8.11.3

Finally one has Section 8.11.3 which provides a translation between several objects central to [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

9 Construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i​I{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}{I} and Θ~J​o​s​h​i​I{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}{I} using Mochizuki’s tensor packets of log\log-shells

Mochizuki’s construction of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i​I{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}{I} requires constructing his codomain 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i⊂𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}\subset\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) for receiving theta-values. This codomain 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (resp. 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) is constructed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] using Galois cohomology (Mochizuki’s notation is some what more complicated than mine). It is also possible to work with somewhat simpler codomains 𝐈J​o​s​h​i⊂𝐈J​o​s​h​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}\subset\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} constructed in Mochizuki’s style. The locus theta-values locus Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} is somewhat simpler than Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} and is adequate for establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. The construction of 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (resp. 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ,𝐈J​o​s​h​i,𝐈J​o​s​h​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) is an adelic construction and carried out separately at each prime and requires some additional preparation. Once one has constructed the codomain 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (resp. 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ,𝐈J​o​s​h​i,𝐈J​o​s​h​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}), one may consider theta-values locii in 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (resp. 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ,𝐈J​o​s​h​i,𝐈J​o​s​h​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}},\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}).

§ 9.1 Bloch-Kato subspaces in Galois cohomology

Readers are advised to read [Joshi, 2023a, § ] before reading this section. As established there, Galois cohomology of a number field depends on the choice of an arithmeticoid. This point will be used throughout.

Mochizuki’s construction of the codomain

𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}

for constructing Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} is based on his notion of log-shells [Mochizuki, 2015, Definition 5.4(iii)]. Here I will provide a more intrinsic description of log-shells than is done in [Joshi, 2020a] and is based on Bloch-Kato subspaces in Galois cohomology. To do this I recall the definitions of Bloch-Kato subspaces in Galois cohomology.

§ 9.1.1 The non-archimedean case

Let E⊃ℚpE\supset{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} be a pp-adic field. Fix an algebraic closure E¯\overline{E} of EE, let GE=Gal⁡(E¯/E)G_{E}={\rm Gal}(\overline{E}/E) and let E¯^\widehat{\overline{E}} be its completion equipped with its canonical action of GEG_{E}. By well-known classical results the prime pp, and the topological groups OE∗⊂E∗{O}_{E}^{*}\subset E^{*} are amphoric (see [Joshi, 2020a, Theorem 3.3] or [Jarden and Ritter, 1979]).

My next point is important. By [Mochizuki, 2004, Proposition 1.2.1] or [Hoshi, 2019, Proposition 4.2] one sees that the triple GE​↷​μ​(E¯)G_{E}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\mu(\overline{E}) consisting of the absolute Galois group GEG_{E}, the subgroup μ⁡(E¯)⊂E¯∗\mu(\overline{E})\subset\overline{E}^{*} consisting of the roots of unity in E¯\overline{E} equipped with the natural action of GEG_{E}, is amphoric and any isomorphism of topological groups

GE1≃GE2G_{E_{1}}\simeq G_{E_{2}}

of local fields E1,E2E_{1},E_{2} (with chosen algebraic closures E¯1,E¯2\overline{E}_{1},\overline{E}_{2}) provides an isomorphism of the corresponding triples

(GE1​↷​μ​(E¯1))≃(GE2​↷​μ​(E¯2))\left(G_{E_{1}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\mu(\overline{E}_{1})\right)\simeq\left(G_{E_{2}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\mu(\overline{E}_{2})\right)

and hence an isomorphism

(GE1​↷​ℤ^​(1)E1)≃(GE2​↷​ℤ^​(1)E2).\left(G_{E_{1}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\hat{{\mathbb{Z}}}(1)_{E_{1}}\right)\simeq\left(G_{E_{2}}\overset{}{\curvearrowright}\hat{{\mathbb{Z}}}(1)_{E_{2}}\right).

This should help understanding how one approaches Galois cohomology from the point of Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces (for more details see [Joshi, 2023a]).

Now to my third point. One has an isomorphism of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector space ([Perrin-Riou, 1994]):

(9.1.1.1) ExtGE1​(ℚp​(0),ℚp​(1))=H1​(GE,ℚp​(1)).{\rm Ext}\,^{1}_{G_{E}}({\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(0),{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)).
Remark 9.1.1.2.

By [Mochizuki, 2009, Proposition 1.4], Mochizuki’s Galois theoretic theta classes live in ExtGE1​(ℚp​(0),ℚp​(1))=H1​(GE,ℚp​(1)){\rm Ext}\,^{1}_{G_{E}}({\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(0),{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)). The archimedean case is discussed below. ∙\bullet

Recall further that one has the decomposition of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector spaces (see [Perrin-Riou, 1994]):

(9.1.1.3) H1​(GE,ℚp​(1))≃Hf1​(GE,ℚp​(1))⊕ℚp≃E⊕ℚp.H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\simeq H^{1}_{f}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\oplus{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}\simeq E\oplus{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}.

This isomorphism is explicitly given as q⟼(logE⁡(q),vE​(q))q\longmapsto(\log_{E}(q),v_{E}(q)), so this isomorphism tracks the valuation of qq separately.

Following [Bloch and Kato, 1990, Nekovář, 1993, Perrin-Riou, 1994], write

Hf1​(GE,ℚp​(1))\displaystyle H_{f}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) =ker⁡(H1​(GE,ℚp​(1))→H1​(GE,Bc​r​i​s)),\displaystyle=\ker(H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\to H^{1}(G_{E},B_{cris})),
Hs​t1​(GE,ℚp​(1))\displaystyle H_{st}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) =ker⁡(H1​(GE,ℚp​(1))→H1​(GE,Bs​t)),\displaystyle=\ker(H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\to H^{1}(G_{E},B_{st})),
Hg1​(GE,ℚp​(1))\displaystyle H_{g}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) =ker⁡(H1​(GE,ℚp​(1))→H1​(GE,Bd​R)),\displaystyle=\ker(H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\to H^{1}(G_{E},B_{dR})),
He1​(GE,ℚp​(1))\displaystyle H_{e}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) =ker⁡(H1​(GE,ℚp​(1))→H1​(GE,Bc​r​i​sφ=1)),\displaystyle=\ker(H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\to H^{1}(G_{E},B_{cris}^{\varphi=1})),

and for ∗∈{e,f,s​t,g}*\in\{e,f,st,g\} define the integral versions as

H∗1​(GE,ℤp​(1))=H1​(GE,ℤp​(1))∩H∗1​(GE,ℚp​(1)).H_{*}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1))\cap H^{1}_{*}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)).

The first three subspaces are the subspaces corresponding respectively to subspaces consisting of crytalline, semi-stable and de Rham extensions of ℚp​(1){\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1) by ℚp​(0){\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(0) and He1​(GE,ℚp​(1))H_{e}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) consists of crystalline, Frobenius trivial extensions of ℚp​(1){\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1) by ℚp​(0){\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(0) contained in Hf1​(GE,ℚp​(1))H^{1}_{f}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)). From [Bloch and Kato, 1990, Nekovář, 1993, Perrin-Riou, 1994] one further has:

(9.1.1.4) He1​(GE,ℚp​(1))=Hf1​(GE,ℚp​(1))⫋Hs​t1​(GE,ℚp​(1))=Hg1​(GE,ℚp​(1))=H1​(GE,ℚp​(1)).H_{e}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H_{f}^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))\subsetneqq H^{1}_{st}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}_{g}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}(G_{E},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)).

The first equality will play an important role in what follows.

§ 9.1.2 The archimedean case

[It will be useful to read my discussion of Schottky uniformization in § 12. Mochizuki does not use the Schottky uniformization approach for his archimedean calculations, but my view is that working with Schottky uniformization at the archimedean primes sets the archimedean and the non-archimedean primes of split-multiplicative reduction on par because both have the same type of uniformization i.e. the Schottky uniformization at archimedean primes corresponds to Tate uniformization at non-archimedean primes of split multiplicative reduction.

Following § 12, for any archimedean prime v∈𝕍La​r​cv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}^{arc} of a number field LL (assuming as in § 3.1, § 3.3, that LL has no real embeddings), one has Lv≃ℂL_{v}\simeq{\mathbb{C}} and I will write:

(9.1.2.1) H1​(Lv,ℤ⁡(1)):=E​x​tℤ−M​H​S1​(ℤ⁡(0),ℤ⁡(1))≃Lv∗≃ℂ∗.H^{1}(L_{v},{\mathbb{Z}}(1)):=Ext^{1}_{{\mathbb{Z}}-MHS}({\mathbb{Z}}(0),{\mathbb{Z}}(1))\simeq L_{v}^{*}\simeq{\mathbb{C}}^{*}.

As explained in [Joshi, 2023a, § ] this is the archimedean analog of Galois cohomology (for v∈𝕍Ln​o​nv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}^{non}) H1​(GLv,ℚp​(1))H^{1}(G_{L_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) considered above.

To keep the theory at archimedean primes further aligned with the theory at non-archimedean primes, I define the archimedean Frobenius-invariant Bloch-Kato subspace to be the multiplicative submonoid of ℂ∗{\mathbb{C}}^{*} given by

(9.1.2.2) He1​(ℂ,ℤ⁡(1))={q∈E​x​tℤ−M​H​S1​(ℤ⁡(0),ℤ⁡(1)):0<|q|ℂ≤1}⊂H1​(ℂ,ℤ⁡(1)).H^{1}_{e}({\mathbb{C}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))=\left\{q\in Ext^{1}_{{\mathbb{Z}}-MHS}({\mathbb{Z}}(0),{\mathbb{Z}}(1)):0<\left|q\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}}\leq 1\right\}\subset H^{1}({\mathbb{C}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1)).

Notably, if qq is a Schottky parameter of an elliptic curve over ℂ{\mathbb{C}}, then

q∈He1​(ℂ,ℤ⁡(1))⊂H1​(ℂ,ℤ⁡(1))=E​x​tℤ−M​H​S1​(ℤ⁡(0),ℤ⁡(1)).q\in H^{1}_{e}({\mathbb{C}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))\subset H^{1}({\mathbb{C}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))=Ext^{1}_{{\mathbb{Z}}-MHS}({\mathbb{Z}}(0),{\mathbb{Z}}(1)).

§ 9.2 Mochizuki’s Log-shells from the point of view of [Joshi, 2021a]

§ 9.2.1 

Mochizuki’s log-shell used in [Mochizuki, 2021c] should be viewed as a rule on the arithmetic Teichmuller space 𝔍⁡(X,E)\mathfrak{J}(X,E):

Definition 9.2.1.1.

Suppose 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} is a holomorphoid of X/LX/L and v∈𝕍Ln​o​nv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}^{non} is a prime of LL with v|pv|p and 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lv)yv\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{v})_{y_{v}} is the local holomorphoid of X/LX/L at vv given by 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}}. Then the Mochizuki’s log-shell given by 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} at vv is the ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}-module given as follows

(9.2.1.2) I⁡((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv))={1p​log⁡(OLv∗)⊂1p​log⁡(OKv∗) if ​p≥3,14​log⁡(OLv∗)⊂14​log⁡(OKv∗) if ​p=2.{I}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})})=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{p}\log({O}_{L_{v}}^{*})\subset\frac{1}{p}\log({O}_{K_{v}}^{*})&\text{ if }p\geq 3,\\ \frac{1}{4}\log({O}_{L_{v}}^{*})\subset\frac{1}{4}\log({O}_{K_{v}}^{*})&\text{ if }p=2.\end{cases}

The Mochizuki’s ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-log-shell given by 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}} at vv is the ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector space

(9.2.1.3) Iℚp​((X/Lv,Ya​n/Kv))=I⁡((X/Lv,Ya​n/Kv))⊗ℤpℚp.{I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}({(X/L_{v},Y^{an}/K_{v})})={I}({(X/L_{v},Y^{an}/K_{v})})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}.

∙\bullet

To connect with [Mochizuki, 2021c], one uses the following:

Lemma 9.2.1.4.

The log-shell I⁡((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv)){I}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})}) (Definition 9.2.1.1) is the mono-analytic log-shell [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 1.2(vi)] given by the arithmetic holomorphic structure 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L)_{{\bf y}}.

Proof.

This is immediate from Mochizuki’s definition of mono-analytic log-shells (for example [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 1.2(vi)]) and the definition of arithmetic holomorphic structures in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022].

An important property of the ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-logshells is following identification with the Bloch-Kato subspaces:

Proposition 9.2.1.5.

For any v∈𝕍Ln​o​nv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}^{non} one has

  1. (1)

    I⁡((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv)){I}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})}) is a ΠX/Lv;Kvt​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v};K_{v}}-amphoric (and hence also GLv;KvG_{L_{v};K_{v}}-amphoric) ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}-module.

  2. (2)

    Iℚp​((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv)){I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})}) and He1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1))H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) are ΠX/Lv;Kvt​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{X/L_{v};K_{v}}-amphoric (and hence also GLv;KvG_{L_{v};K_{v}}-amphoric) ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} vector spaces.

  3. (3)

    One has

    I⁡((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv))=Hf1​(GLv;Kv,ℤp​(1))=He1​(GLv;Kv,ℤp​(1)),{I}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})})=H^{1}_{f}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1)),

    and

    Iℚp​((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv))=Hf1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1))=He1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1)).{I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})})=H^{1}_{f}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))=H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)).
  4. (4)

    In particular, I⁡((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv)){I}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})}) (resp. Iℚp​((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv)){I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})})) consists of integral (resp. rational) Frobenius-invariant Galois cohomology classes.

Proof.

The first and the second assertions are immediate from the amphoricity of OLv∗{O}_{L_{v}}^{*} and of the prime number pp (see [Joshi, 2020a, Theorem ], [Joshi, 2020a, Theorem ] and [Joshi, 2020a, Remark ]). The third is immediate from (9.1.1.4) which also yields the amphoricity of He1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1))H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)). The fourth assertion is a consequence of the third.

Remark 9.2.1.6.

These assertion are important in the context of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]: Thanks to the explicit identification of the Frobenius morphism 𝝋:𝐘𝐋′′→𝐘𝐋′′\boldsymbol{\varphi}:\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime}\to\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} of 𝐘𝐋′′\mathscrbf{Y}_{L^{\prime}}^{\prime} and 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-Links in § 8.9 one sees that He1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1))H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) which serves as a container for such cohomology classes of interest is stable under iterates of 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-Links. This stability property (9.2.1.5) underlies Mochizuki’s choice of Iℚp​((X/Lv,Xa​n/Kv))=He1​(GLv;Kv,ℚp​(1)){I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}({(X/L_{v},X^{an}/K_{v})})=H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{v};K_{v}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1)) as the foundation for constructing the codomain for defining the theta-values locus in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3]. [This proposition is not established in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].] This codomain is constructed in the next few paragraphs. ∙\bullet

§ 9.3 The Banach space 1t​Bφ=p\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p} as the log-shell for [Joshi, 2021a]

The theory developed in the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper) one has a more natural definition of a log-shell. This paragraph provides the detail of this assertion.

§ 9.3.1 The subspace Bφ=pB^{\varphi=p}

Let me begin by recalling from [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018]:

Theorem 9.3.1.1.
  1. (1)

    One has an isomorphism of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-Banach spaces

    given by 1+x⟼log⁡([1+x])1+x\longmapsto\log([1+x]).

  2. (2)

    The ring BB is generated as a ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-algebra by Bφ=pB^{\varphi=p}.

Proof.

These are established in [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Proposition 4.4.6] and [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.2.1] respectively.

§ 9.3.2 

It is precisely because of the Theorem 9.3.1.1 and Mochizuki’s definition of the log-shell that I have asserted in [Joshi, 2021b] that Bφ=pB^{\varphi=p} is the analog of Mochizuki’s log-shell in [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2021b]. Here is a more precise construction.

Definition 9.3.2.1.

For any prime p<∞p<\infty, let

(9.3.2.2) Ij​o​s​h​i,p=1t​Bφ=p.{I}_{joshi,p}=\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p}.

Then Ij​o​s​h​i,p{I}_{joshi,p} will be referred to as the log-shell for B⁡[1/t]B[1/t]. ∙\bullet

From § 5.2.6 recall the ring Be=B​[1/t]φ=1B_{e}=B[{1}/{t}]^{\varphi=1}, that is, BeB_{e} is the ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-algebra of Frobenius-invariant elements of B⁡[1/t]B[{1}/{t}] (generated by 1t​Bφ=p\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p}).

The geometric meaning of Ij​o​s​h​i,p{I}_{joshi,p} is explicated by the following.

Lemma 9.3.2.3.
  1. (1)
    Ij​o​s​h​i,p=log⁡(1+𝔪ℂp♭)t.{I}_{joshi,p}=\frac{\log(1+\mathfrak{m}_{{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}}})}{t}.
  2. (2)

    For all n∈ℤn\in{\mathbb{Z}} one has

    φn​(Ij​o​s​h​i,p)⊂Ij​o​s​h​i,p.\varphi^{n}({I}_{joshi,p})\subset{I}_{joshi,p}.
  3. (3)

    One has

    Ij​o​s​h​i,p=1t​Bφ=p=Bed​e​g≤1.{I}_{joshi,p}=\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p}=B_{e}^{deg\leq 1}.
  4. (4)

    Notably, the log-shell Ij​o​s​h​i,p{I}_{joshi,p} consists of functions on Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} of degree ≤1\leq 1 which are inariant under the Frobenius morphism of B⁡[1/t]B[1/t].

Proof.

The first assertion is immediate from Theorem 9.3.1.1 and the definition of Ij​o​s​h​i,p{I}_{joshi,p}. It is enough to prove the second assertion for n=1n=1. First note that if bt∈1t​Bφ=p\frac{b}{t}\in\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p} then

(9.3.2.4) φ⁡(bt)=φ⁡(b)φ⁡(t)=p⋅bp⋅t=bt\varphi(\frac{b}{t})=\frac{\varphi(b)}{\varphi(t)}=\frac{p\cdot b}{p\cdot t}=\frac{b}{t}

and so bt\frac{b}{t} is a φ\varphi invariant or Frobenius fixed element of BB (also see [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, Théorème 6.5.2]). Thirdly, by [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018], Xℂp♭,ℚp{X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} can be obtained as

Xℂp♭,ℚp=Proj⁡(Be){X}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}={\rm Proj}(B_{e})

and one has the equality

(9.3.2.5) Ij​o​s​h​i,p=1t​Bφ=p=Bed​e​g≤1.{I}_{joshi,p}=\frac{1}{t}B^{\varphi=p}=B_{e}^{deg\leq 1}.

Hence the assertion is clear.

Remark 9.3.2.6.

Stability of Ij​o​s​h​i,p{I}_{joshi,p} under iterates of the Frobenius morphism provided by Lemma 9.3.2.3 corresponds to the stability of Mochizuki’s log-shells under iterates of Mochizuki’s 𝔩​𝔬​𝔤\mathfrak{log}-links (see [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 1.1.1, Remark 1.2.2(iii)] and [Joshi, 2023b, Appendix]). ∙\bullet

§ 9.4 Construction of Mochizuki’s Tensor Packet codomain 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (resp. 𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) for Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i​I\widetilde{\Theta}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}{I}

Let me briefly describe Mochizuki’s choice of codomain or container for theta-values. Mochizuki’s formalism of tensor packets is discussed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, § 3]. Assumptions § 2.4, § 3.1 will now be strictly in force.

In [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], Mochizuki bundles theta-values arising primes w|pw|p by means of tensor products of log-shells. This is the analog in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] of the formalism of bundling rings considered earlier in § 7.5. The formalism of bundling rings allows us to use the ring structure to multiply the theta-values at primes w|pw|p in a common ring. The formalism of tensor products and tensor packets [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] provide this functionality in [Mochizuki, 2021c].

§ 9.4.3 

Mochizuki’s method in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] relies on anabelian reconstruction theory and the proof requires recovering a lot of information about X/LX/L purely from the tempered fundamental groups of X/LvX/L_{v} for v∈𝕍Lv\in\mathbb{V}_{L}. This necessitates tracking a lot more information than is needed for my methods above. This is not required in my approach. Instead of appealing to Mochizuki’s Anabelian Reconstruction [Mochizuki, 2012, Mochizuki, 2013, Mochizuki, 2015], one can use the Rosetta-Stone § 8.5 to translate the required objects from my theory and Mochizuki’s Reconstruction Theory is not needed. Nevertheless to be fully compatible with [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], I will work with Mochizuki’s setup for defining the codomain for his theta-values locus.

§ 9.4.4 

I will follow [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] closely for the most part. It will be convenient to work with the graph of the correspondence which gives rise to Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz § 4 instead of working with Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz. This means that instead of working with

𝐳=(𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}=(\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}

one works with the ℓ∗+1{\ell^{*}}+1-tuple

(𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)(\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}})

where

𝐳0⟼(𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)\mathbf{z}_{0}\longmapsto(\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}})

is the correspondence on 𝐘𝐋\mathscrbf{Y}_{L} giving rise to Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. Notably, if 𝐳Θ\mathbf{z}_{\Theta} is the standard point § 4.5 of Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}, then one has the ℓ∗+1{\ell^{*}}+1-tuple

𝐳Θ=(𝐲0′,𝐲1′,…,𝐲ℓ∗′)\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}=({\bf y}_{0}^{\prime},{\bf y}_{1}^{\prime},\ldots,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}^{\prime})

associated with this point.

§ 9.4.5 Mochizuki’s Procession of prime-strips

Following [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3], for 0≤j≤ℓ∗0\leq j\leq{\ell^{*}}, let 𝕊j+1={0,1,…,j}\mathbb{S}_{j+1}=\{0,1,\ldots,j\} so that each set 𝕊j+1\mathbb{S}_{j+1} has exactly j+1j+1 elements. Similarly define 𝕊j+1⋇={1,…,j}\mathbb{S}_{j+1}^{\divideontimes}=\{1,\ldots,j\} so that each set 𝕊j+1⋇={1,…,j}\mathbb{S}_{j+1}^{\divideontimes}=\{1,\ldots,j\} has exactly jj elements.

I will think of these sets as giving functions (with values in finite sets) on the set of ℓ∗+1{\ell^{*}}+1 tuples rising from Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. This is done as follows. For each ℓ∗+1{\ell^{*}}+1 tuple 𝐳=(𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)\mathbf{z}=(\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}}) of arithmeticoids as above, one has, for each j=0,1,…,ℓ∗j=0,1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}, the sets

𝕊j​(𝐳)={𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳j}\mathbb{S}_{j}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{j}\right\}

and

𝕊j⋇​(𝐳)={𝐳1,…,𝐳j}.\mathbb{S}_{j}^{\divideontimes}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{j}\right\}.

Notably

𝕊ℓ∗​(𝐳)={𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗}\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{{\ell^{*}}}\right\}

and

𝕊ℓ∗⋇​(𝐳)={𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗}.\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}}^{\divideontimes}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{{\ell^{*}}}\right\}.

The following is an elementary consequence of this observation

Lemma 9.4.5.1.

For each ℓ∗+1{\ell^{*}}+1-tuple 𝐳=(𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)\mathbf{z}=(\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}}) (as constructed above) and arising from 𝐳=(𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗)∈Σ~L′\mathbf{z}=(\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}})\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}}. Then one has the obvious chain of inclusions of sets of arithmeticoids

𝕊0​(𝐳)={𝐳0}⊂𝕊1​(𝐳)={𝐳0,𝐳1}⊂⋯⊂𝕊ℓ∗​(𝐳)={𝐳0,𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗},\mathbb{S}_{0}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{0}\right\}\subset\mathbb{S}_{1}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1}\right\}\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{0},\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}}\right\},

and

𝕊1⋇​(𝐳)={𝐳1}⊂𝕊2⋇​(𝐳)={𝐳1,𝐳2}⊂⋯⊂𝕊ℓ∗⋇​(𝐳)={𝐳1,…,𝐳ℓ∗}.\mathbb{S}_{1}^{\divideontimes}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{1}\right\}\subset\mathbb{S}_{2}^{\divideontimes}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{1},\mathbf{z}_{2}\right\}\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}}^{\divideontimes}(\mathbf{z})=\left\{\mathbf{z}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{\ell^{*}}\right\}.

Applying Mochizuki’s “prime-strip” constructions FM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i?{F}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{?} of § 8.6, Proposition 8.6.1.3 and Rosetta Stone Fragment 8.5, to these chains of subsets, one obtains a procession of prime-strips in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11(i)].

Remark 9.4.5.2.

Mochizuki’s choice of the sets A=𝕊j+1A=\mathbb{S}_{j+1} for j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}} is dictated by his reconstruction theoretic approach in which Mochizuki reconstructs a specific instance of X/Lw′X/L_{w}^{\prime} from anabelian data. Notably in [Mochizuki, 2021a], 𝕊ℓ∗\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}} is in bijection with the set of cusps of a certain tempered covering constructed from X/LvX/L_{v} at a prime v∈𝕍L′n​o​nv\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}^{non}. From the point of view of the present series of papers ([Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023b, Joshi, 2023a] and this paper), anabelian reconstruction arguments are unnecessary and all functionality which is needed in establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] is provided in my approach by working with distinct holomorphoids 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L′)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}}. ∙\bullet

and

§ 9.4.8 

It will be useful to work with simpler versions of 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} and 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} given as follows. Let 𝐳Θ=(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}=({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}) be the standard point of Mochizuki’s Ansatz constructed in 4.5. This point is a Θg​a​u\Theta_{gau}-Link in the terminology of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. Taking A={1,…,ℓ∗}A=\{1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}\} in Mochizuki’s construction:

(9.4.8.1) 𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢=∏𝐩(⨂𝐣=𝟏ℓ∗𝐈𝐩,𝐲𝐣)⊂∏𝐩(⨂𝐣=𝟏ℓ∗𝐈𝐩,𝐲𝐣ℚ)=𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢ℚ\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}=\prod_{p}\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}{I}_{p,{\bf y}_{j}}\right)\subset\prod_{p}\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}{I}_{p,{\bf y}_{j}}^{\mathbb{Q}}\right)=\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}
Remark 9.4.8.2.

By Proposition 9.2.1.5 the log-shells are amphoric. Hence one has abstract isomorphisms

Ip,𝐲j≃Ip,𝐲ℓ∗ for ​j=1,…,ℓ∗,{I}_{p,{\bf y}_{j}}\simeq{I}_{p,{\bf y}_{\ell^{*}}}\qquad\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}},

so one can write

(9.4.8.3) 𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢=∏𝐩(⨂𝐣=𝟏ℓ∗𝐈𝐩)\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}=\prod_{p}\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}{I}_{p}\right)

obtained by forgetting the 𝐲j{\bf y}_{j} (or any arithmeticoids giving rise to a specific log-shell) altogether (as [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] does). But keeping the 𝐳Θ\mathbf{z}_{\Theta} components in the above notation allows us to remember that the individual factors come equipped with the valuation scaling property given by Theorem 4.2.2.1. This property is crucial for establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] and also for the main theorem of [Mochizuki, 2021d]. ∙\bullet

or in Mochizuki’s style as:

and

obtained by projection onto the (j+1)t​h(j+1)^{th} factor of each 𝕊j+1\mathbb{S}_{j+1} for j=1,…,ℓ∗j=1,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}.

This discussion together with Proposition 9.4.2.4 and Theorem 10.11.3.1 leads to the following explicit description:

Proposition 9.4.9.3.

Let 𝐳Θ=(𝐲1,…,𝐲ℓ∗)\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}=({\bf y}_{1},\ldots,{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}) be the standard point of Mochizuki’s Ansatz constructed in 4.5. Using Proposition 9.4.2.4 one may identify 𝐈~J​o​s​h​i\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}} and 𝐈~J​o​s​h​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} as ℓ∗{\ell^{*}}-tuples of Galois cohomology classes of the ℓ∗{\ell^{*}}-tuple of arithmeticoids 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐳Θ=(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲1,…,𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗)\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}}=(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{1}},\ldots,\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}}) with respect to the bijection 𝕍¯≃𝕍Lmod\underline{\mathbb{V}}\simeq\mathbb{V}_{L_{\rm mod}} (obtained from § 3.1, § 3.3) explicitly as

(9.4.9.4) 𝐈~J​o​s​h​i\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}} =∏j=1ℓ∗H¯e1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲j,ℤ⁡(1))≃He1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗,ℤ⁡(1))ℓ∗,\displaystyle=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\underline{H}_{e}^{1}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{j}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))\simeq H_{e}^{1}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))^{\ell^{*}},
(9.4.9.5) 𝐈~J​o​s​h​iℚ\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} =∏j=1ℓ∗H¯e1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲j,ℚ⁡(1))ℓ∗≃He1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲ℓ∗,ℚ⁡(1))ℓ∗.\displaystyle=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\underline{H}_{e}^{1}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{j}},{\mathbb{Q}}(1))^{\ell^{*}}\simeq H_{e}^{1}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}_{{\ell^{*}}}},{\mathbb{Q}}(1))^{\ell^{*}}.

Remark 9.4.9.6.

In [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] Mochizuki only considers the tensor product version 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} and 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢ℚ\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} to define his theta-values locus. But the theta-values locus may also be defined in the product versions 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} and 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} (9.4.6.3) and (9.4.6.4). ∙\bullet

§ 9.4.10 

Notably, for j=ℓ∗j={\ell^{*}} expanding out the tensor product (9.4.6.2) for Ip𝕊j+1{}^{\mathbb{S}_{j+1}}{I}_{p} one gets

(9.4.10.1) Ip𝕊ℓ∗+1=⨂a∈𝕊ℓ∗+1Ipℚp=⨂a∈𝕊ℓ∗+1(⨁w|pLw′)=⨁αEα′′{}^{\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}+1}}{I}_{p}=\bigotimes_{a\in\mathbb{S}^{{\ell^{*}}+1}}{{I}}_{p}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}=\bigotimes_{a\in\mathbb{S}^{{\ell^{*}}+1}}\left(\bigoplus_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime}\right)=\bigoplus_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime}

where Eα′′E_{\alpha}^{\prime\prime} runs over a multi-set of pp-adic fields. This is similar to the multi-set of pp-adic fields which appear in Lemma 7.8.1.2. If one works with Ip𝕊ℓ∗+1⋇{}^{\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}+1}^{\divideontimes}}{I}_{p} (instead of Ip𝕊ℓ∗+1{}^{\mathbb{S}_{{\ell^{*}}+1}}{I}_{p}) then one obtains the multi-set of pp-adic fields which appear in Lemma 7.8.1.2.

Remark 9.4.10.2.

In particular, this remark proves my assertion that tensor packet structure in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Section 3] is to compensate for the missing ring structure (in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]) needed to take products of the theta-values at distinct primes w|pw|p. From my point of view this is directly available through the product structure of the period ring BpB_{p} of [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018]. ∙\bullet

§ 9.4.11 

These construction lead to the following definition

Definition 9.4.11.1.

Mochizuki’s adelic tensor product log-shells 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢​(𝐋′)\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}(L^{\prime}), given in (9.4.6.8) as a subgroup of 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢ℚ​(𝐋′)\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}(L^{\prime}) (resp. the group 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i​(L′)\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}(L^{\prime}), given in (9.4.7.1) as a subgroup of 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) equipped with the topology induced from adeles (topology on each factor is the obvious one), are Mochizuki’s tensor product codomains for the theta-values locus (resp. Mochizuki’s product codomains for the theta-values locus) (see [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] or for an explicit assertion see [Tan, 2018, Definition 7.16] of the tensor product log-shell). 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ→𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢ℚ.\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}\to\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}.

Remark 9.4.11.2.
  1. (1)

    This construction is carried out in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 3.1] and 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} is called the holomorphic log-shell.

  2. (2)

    One may also carry out these constructions for arbitrary 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}} and the 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(Lmod)𝐲¯\mathfrak{arith}(L_{\rm mod})_{\underline{{\bf y}}}. In this case, in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 3.2], this is called mono-analytic log-shell.

  3. (3)

    In both the instances, Mochizuki’s notation is a bit more complex and I will not use it here.

∙\bullet

§ 9.5 Mochizuki’s evaluation of theta-values in log-shells

The assumptions § 2.4 and § 3.1, § 3.3 will now be in force. Let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L′)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}} be a holomorphoid of X/L′X/L^{\prime}. Let w∈𝕍L′w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}. Let 𝐲=(yw)w∈𝕍L′{\bf y}=(y_{w})_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}} and let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/Lw′)yw\mathfrak{hol}(X/L_{w}^{\prime})_{y_{w}} be the local holomorphoid of X/LX/L at ww given by 𝐲{\bf y}.

§ 9.5.1 

By properties of L′/LL^{\prime}/L (available by § 2.4 and § 3.1, § 3.3) one sees that the entire 2​ℓ2\ell-torsion of C/L′C/L^{\prime} is defined over L′L^{\prime} and hence the 2​ℓ2\ell-torsion of C/Lw′C/L_{w}^{\prime} is defined over Lw′L_{w}^{\prime}. So one can apply Mochizuki’s Galois theoretic evaluation of theta-values ([Mochizuki, 2009, Proposition 1.4]) to deduce that these classes, say one of them is ξw\xi_{w}, lands in

ξw∈H1​(GLw′;Kw,ℤpw​(1)Kw)\xi_{w}\in H^{1}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{w}}(1)_{K_{w}})

where ℤpw​(1)Kw{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{w}}(1)_{K_{w}} is the GLw′;KwG_{L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w}}-module of pwp_{w}-power roots of unity contained in KwK_{w}. However it is more useful for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] to construct cohomology classes in He1​(GLw′;Kw,ℤpw​(1)Kw)H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{w}}(1)_{K_{w}}) (with Bc​r​i​sB_{cris} constructed using the completed algebraic closure of Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} provided by KwK_{w}).

§ 9.5.2 

Let me say that one cannot view the classes ξw\xi_{w} provided by the Tate parameter in He1H^{1}_{e}. So [Mochizuki, 2021c] resorts to another approach to this which consists of considering multiplicative action of ξw\xi_{w} on the log-shell see for instance [Mochizuki, 2021c, Figure 3.1] and [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11(b)]. This action emerges naturally in my approach in the proof of Theorem 9.9.1.

This is remedied (in § 9.6 below) by explicitly constructing Frobenius trivial, crystalline cohomology classes associated to any Tate parameter and hence also theta-values on any holomorphoid of any Tate elliptic curve. These classes do live in Mochizuki’s log-shells!

§ 9.6 Construction of crystalline, Frobenius invariant Galois cohomology class associated to a Tate elliptic curve

Here by crystalline and Frobenius invariant Galois cohomology classes, I mean elements of He1​(−,−)H^{1}_{e}(-,-). One may use this term ‘crystalline, Frobenius invariant’ because of the definition of He1H^{1}_{e}.

§ 9.6.1 

Assume C,L,X,L,ℓC,L,X,L,\ell are as in § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3. Let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L′)𝐲\mathfrak{hol}(X/L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}} be a holomorphoid of X/L′X/L^{\prime} and write 𝐲=(yw)v∈𝕍L′{\bf y}=(y_{w})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}. Assume w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset. Let KwK_{w} be the residue field of ywy_{w} and let Lw′⊂L¯^w′⊂KwL_{w}^{\prime}\subset\widehat{\overline{L}}_{w}^{\prime}\subset K_{w} be the algebraic closure of Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} in KwK_{w}. I want to construct a Galois cohomology class associated to X/Lw′X/L_{w}^{\prime} which lives in He1​(GLw′;Kw,ℤp​(1))H_{e}^{1}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}(1)). Let 𝔾^m/ℤp\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{m}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p} be the multiplicative formal group over ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}. Then one has
