Choose a OLw′{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}-minimal model for C/Lw′C/L_{w}^{\prime}. Let C^/OLw′\hat{C}/{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}} be the formal group obtained from C/OLw′C/{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}} (by formal completion along the identity). Then one has an isomorphism

C^≃𝔾^m\hat{C}\simeq\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{m}

of OLw′{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}-formal groups.

For each prime p<∞p<\infty, define p∗∈ℤpp^{*}\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{p} by setting

(9.6.1.2) p∗={p if  p≥3,4 if  p=2.p^{*}=\begin{cases}p&\text{ if } $p\geq 3$,\\ 4&\text{ if } $p=2$.\end{cases}

In particular, if w|pww|p_{w} is the rational prime lying under w∈𝕍L′n​o​nw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}^{non}, then pw∗p_{w}^{*} is defined by the above equation.

The quantity pw∗p_{w}^{*} is GLw′G_{L_{w}^{\prime}}-amphoric.

Proof.

This is proved in [Mochizuki, 2015] and also in [Hoshi, 2021, Proposition 3.6].

§ 9.6.2 

Now one uses § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3. § 9.7.1 

Let

(9.7.1.1) eB​K:Lw′​  ​He1​(GLw′,ℚp​(1))e_{BK}:L_{w}^{\prime}{\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 8.875pt\raise 4.72855pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-1.72855pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\simeq}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces}H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime}},{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}(1))

be the Bloch-Kato exponential isomorphism of topological groups (see [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018, 10.6.19]) in which cohomology on the right is viewed as a multiplicative group. Explicitly eB​Ke_{BK} is the homomorphism

x⟼epm⋅xpmm≫0.x\longmapsto\frac{e^{p^{m}\cdot x}}{p^{m}}\qquad m\gg 0.

Let logp\log_{p} denote the principal branch of the pp-adic logarithm (i.e. logp⁡(p)=0\log_{p}(p)=0).

Remark 9.7.1.2.
  1. (1)

    It is important to recall a basic fact about the pp-adic exponential function. Let me remind the reader that the power series giving the pp-adic exponential function ex=∑n=0∞xnn!e^{x}=\sum\limits_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^{n}}{n!} (here one can take x∈ℂpx\in{\mathbb{C}}_{p}, with the usual normalization |p|ℂp=1p\left|p\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}=\frac{1}{p}) has radius of convergence |x|ℂp<|p|ℂp1/(p−1)=(1p)1/(p−1)\left|x\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}<\left|p\right|^{1/(p-1)}_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}=\left(\frac{1}{p}\right)^{1/(p-1)} (see [Koblitz, 1984, Chapter IV, Section 1]). Hence for p=2p=2 the disk of convergence is |x|ℂ2<|2|ℂ2=12\left|x\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{2}}<\left|2\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{2}}=\frac{1}{2} while for pp odd, the disc of convergence strictly contains the open disk |x|ℂp<1p\left|x\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}<\frac{1}{p}. This should help clarify the difference in the formulae given below when w|2w|2.

  2. (2)

    Importantly, the pp-adic exponential does not converge on pp-adic units or even on 11-units but the series defining epm⋅ue^{p^{m}\cdot u} converges for any pp-adic unit uu for suitably large mm. This becomes important in calculating the inverse of the Bloch-Kato exponential.

∙\bullet

Proposition 9.7.2.3.

Let L,C,X,L′L,C,X,L^{\prime} be as in § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3. Let w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset (so pp is odd). Consider the set of prime w∈𝕍L′,pw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime},p}. One can obviously extend the above isomorphism eB​Ke_{BK} to the product topological groups ∏w∈𝕍L′Lw′\prod_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}L_{w}^{\prime} and a similar assertion for logB​K\log_{BK} and deduce the isomorphism

§ 9.7.4 

Recall from [Joshi, 2023a, § ], the definition of the Galois cohomology of an arithmeticoid. Then one can assemble these local classes {ξ(X/Lw′;Kw)}w∈𝕍L′\{\xi_{(X/L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w})}\}_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}} into a class

(9.7.4.1) 𝝃𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L′)𝐲=(ξ(X/Lw′;Kw))w∈𝕍L′∈He1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲,ℤ⁡(1))\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathfrak{hol}(X/L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}}}=(\xi_{(X/L_{w}^{\prime};K_{w})})_{w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}}\in H^{1}_{e}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{\bf y},{\mathbb{Z}}(1))

in the galois cohomology of the arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime})_{\bf y} (see [Joshi, 2023a, § ]). For notational simplicity, I will hence forth write 𝝃𝔥​𝔬​𝔩​(X/L′)𝐲\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathfrak{hol}(X/L^{\prime})_{{\bf y}}} as

𝝃𝐲.\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\bf y}}.

(9.7.4.2) ξw={{(1+pw∗)1/pwn}n≥0∈He1​(GLw′,ℤpw​(1))if w∈𝕍L′, and w∉𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s,{(1+pw∗⋅qw1/2​ℓ)1/pwn}n≥0∈He1​(GLw′,ℤpw​(1))if ​w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sqw∈E​x​tM​H​S1​(ℤ⁡(0),ℤ⁡(1))if ​w∈𝕍¯∩𝕍L′a​r​c.\xi_{w}=\begin{cases}\left\{(1+p_{w}^{*})^{1/p_{w}^{n}}\right\}_{n\geq 0}\in H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{w}}(1))&\text{if }w\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}},\text{ and }w\not\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss},\\ \left\{(1+p_{w}^{*}\cdot q^{1/2\ell}_{w})^{1/p_{w}^{n}}\right\}_{n\geq 0}\in H^{1}_{e}(G_{L_{w}^{\prime}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{p_{w}}(1))&\text{if }w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}\\ q_{w}\in Ext^{1}_{MHS}({\mathbb{Z}}(0),{\mathbb{Z}}(1))&\text{if }w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}\cap\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime}}^{arc}.\end{cases}

§ 9.7.5 Collation of Galois cohomology classes

One would like to collate and compare the cohomology classes 𝝃𝐲\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\bf y}} arising from different arithmeticoids 𝐲{\bf y} in the cohomology of one arithmeticoid. This is where our choice of the standard arithmeticoid § 4.4 comes in and the following assertion establishes this collation process.

§ 9.8 The definition of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} and Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}

My definition of the theta-values locus Θ~J​o​s​h​i{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}} is here § 6.2.1 and of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} is here § 9.8.

Let me make the following remarks which will help clarify the construction:

  1. (1)

    One important point to be noted is that Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} and Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} refer respectively to slightly different codomains 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} and 𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}. Mochizuki uses Anabelian Reconstruction Theory in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d], and this approach requires tracking a lot of additional data and this reflected in 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}. My approach is construction as opposed to reconstruction and requires less information be tracked and leads to a simpler codomain 𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}} (with a homomorphism 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢→𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}\to\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}) for defining Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}.

  2. (2)

    The substantively non-trivial portion of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] is the construction of the Theta-values set Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} in 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} (or 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}).

  3. (3)

    The bound asserted by [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] is natural modulo the existence of this set.

  4. (4)

    Both [Joshi, 2023b] and [Mochizuki, 2021c] require working with a certain number of copies of a fixed value group (explicitly |ℂp♭|⊂ℝ\left|{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}\right|\subset{\mathbb{R}}) for each prime pp.

  5. (5)

    As discussed in [Joshi, 2023b], in my theory one works with copies of the value group of the tilt |ℂp♭||{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}| (one can do this by [Scholze, 2012] or [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018]) and all the valuation calculations can be made in this chosen, fixed value group |ℂp♭|\left|{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}\right| for each prime pp. One may further assume that |ℂp♭|⊂ℝ\left|{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}\right|\subset{\mathbb{R}} if one needs to work with realified value groups (remember that [Fargues and Fontaine, 2018] works with valuations taking values in ℝ{\mathbb{R}}).

  6. (6)

    In [Mochizuki, 2021c], neither tilts nor algebraically closed complete valued fields are available, and value groups are tracked separately by means of perfect and realified Frobenioids of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} (for each prime pp). My discussion of perfect and realified Frobenioids is in § 10 especially § 10.4.

  7. (7)

    This provides the value group equal to the value group of ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} (which is equal to that of ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} as ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} is an immediate extension of ℚ¯p{\bar{{\mathbb{Q}}}}_{p} by [Poonen, 1993]) and ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} has value group equal to that of ℂp♭{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat} by [Scholze, 2012, Lemma 3.4].

  8. (8)

    The construction of Theta-locus provides the valuation data arising from distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures which are comparable in appropriate common value group at each prime.

  9. (9)

    Without the existence of distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022] and the construction of [Joshi, 2023b] this idea is difficult to understand and one can arrive at incorrect conclusion regarding [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

§ 9.8.1 

Now one can define Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\widetilde{\Theta}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}. The construction is similar to that of Θ~J​o​s​h​i\widetilde{\Theta}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}} (in fact the latter is modeled on the former). Theorem-Definition 9.8.1.1 is essentially [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11]. 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} and 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢ℚ\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}).

Proof.

The rest of the assertions are easily assembled from already established facts and properties.

Remark 9.8.1.2.

Despite the notation 𝝃𝐳M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}}^{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}} these crystalline Galois cohomology classes are not used by Mochizuki in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]. His method uses a multiplicative action of theta-values on log-shells which is described in detail in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Figure 3.1]. As is clarified in Remark 9.9.7, this multiplicative action emerges in the proof of Theorem 9.9.1 given below. However, one can obviously follow Mochizuki’s approach to constructing the theta-values locus Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈\widetilde{\Theta}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathscrbf{I}}}. ∙\bullet

Corollary 9.8.1.3.

The subset Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (resp. Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) is contained in a compact subset of 𝐈𝐉​𝐨​𝐬​𝐡​𝐢ℚ\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} (resp. 𝐈𝐌​𝐨​𝐜​𝐡​𝐢​𝐳​𝐮​𝐤​𝐢ℚ\mathscrbf{I}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}).

Proof.

Since Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (resp. Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) are the images of Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} (resp. Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}) under the (continuous) homomorphisms, it is enough to prove the assertion for the latter sets. This, in turn, is immediate from the fact that each of factors of the Galois cohomology of an arithmeticoid He1​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L′),ℤ⁡(1))H^{1}_{e}(\mathfrak{arith}(L^{\prime}),{\mathbb{Z}}(1)) is compact and the topology on 𝐈~J​o​s​h​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} (resp. 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}) is the product topology.

One sees immediately that:

The four suprema |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~|\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}\right|, |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈|\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right|, |Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~|\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}\right| and |Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈|\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right| are bounded.

Proof.

This is clear from Corollary 9.8.1.3.

Lemma 9.8.2.7.

Let EE be a pp-adic field and let |−|E\left|-\right|_{E} be a pp-adic absolute value on EE. Then for all x∈(p∗⋅OE)−{0}x\in(p^{*}\cdot{O}_{E})-\{0\} one has

|logE⁡(1+x)|E=|x|E.\left|\log_{E}(1+x)\right|_{E}=\left|x\right|_{E}.

Proof.

Let π∈OE\pi\in{O}_{E} be a uniformiser of OE{O}_{E}. By [Koblitz, 1984], logE⁡(1+x)\log_{E}(1+x) converges for |x|E<1\left|x\right|_{E}<1. As EE is a pp-adic field and |−|E\left|-\right|_{E} is a pp-adic absolute value on EE i.e. EE has a discrete value group, so |x|E≤|π|E\left|x\right|_{E}\leq\left|\pi\right|_{E} for all x∈𝔪Ex\in\mathfrak{m}_{E}. Thus this series converges for all xx such that |x|E≤|π|E\left|x\right|_{E}\leq\left|\pi\right|_{E} and hence the nt​hn^{th} term |xnn|E→0\left|\frac{x^{n}}{n}\right|_{E}\to 0 as n→∞n\to\infty. So one may approximate logE⁡(1+x)\log_{E}(1+x) by its partial sum

∑n=1N(−1)n−1⋅xnn=x+ higher order terms\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}\cdot x^{n}}{n}=x+\text{ higher order terms}

for some sufficiently large NN and estimate the absolute value of this partial sum. Hence, by the standard properties of pp-adic absolute values, it is enough to show that

|xnn|E<|x|En≥2.\left|\frac{x^{n}}{n}\right|_{E}<\left|x\right|_{E}\qquad n\geq 2.

This is true if |xn−1|<|n|E\left|x^{n-1}\right|<\left|n\right|_{E} for all n≥2n\geq 2 or equivalently

|x|E<|n|E1/(n−1).\left|x\right|_{E}<\left|n\right|_{E}^{1/(n-1)}.

So it is enough to verify that

|x|E<infn≥1{|n|E1/(n−1)}.\left|x\right|_{E}<\inf_{n\geq 1}\left\{\left|n\right|_{E}^{1/(n-1)}\right\}.

If p∤np\nmid n then |n|E=1\left|n\right|_{E}=1, and if p|np|n then write n=pk⋅rn=p^{k}\cdot r with k≥1k\geq 1, p∤rp\nmid r, so it is enough to check that

|x|E<infk≥1,r≥1{1,|pk|E1/(pk⋅r−1)}=infk≥1,r≥1{1,|p|Ek/(pk⋅r−1)}.\left|x\right|_{E}<\inf_{k\geq 1,r\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p^{k}\right|_{E}^{1/(p^{k}\cdot r-1)}\right\}=\inf_{k\geq 1,r\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p\right|_{E}^{k/(p^{k}\cdot r-1)}\right\}.

For any fixed 0<t<10<t<1 the continuous function of yy on the open interval (0,1)(0,1) given by f⁡(t)=tyf(t)=t^{y} is a decreasing function of yy. As kpk⋅r−1<kpk−1\frac{k}{p^{k}\cdot r-1}<\frac{k}{p^{k}-1} for r≥2r\geq 2, one may replace the rightmost infimum by

|x|E<infk≥1,r≥1{1,|pk|E1/(pk⋅r−1)}=infk≥1{1,|p|Ek/(pk−1)}.\left|x\right|_{E}<\inf_{k\geq 1,r\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p^{k}\right|_{E}^{1/(p^{k}\cdot r-1)}\right\}=\inf_{k\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p\right|_{E}^{k/(p^{k}-1)}\right\}.

Now for k≥1k\geq 1, k⟼k/(pk−1)k\longmapsto k/(p^{k}-1) is an exponentially decaying, decreasing function and hence

k/(pk−1)<{1/(p−1) if ​p≠2,1 if ​p=2,k/(p^{k}-1)<\begin{cases}1/(p-1)&\text{ if }p\neq 2,\\ 1&\text{ if }p=2,\end{cases}

equivalently (for any pp and each k≥2k\geq 2)

k/(pk−1)<1/(p−1).k/(p^{k}-1)<1/(p-1).

So one has

|x|E<infk≥1,r≥1{1,|pk|E1/(pk⋅r−1)}=infk≥1{1,|p|E1/(p−1)}=|p|E1/(p−1).\left|x\right|_{E}<\inf_{k\geq 1,r\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p^{k}\right|_{E}^{1/(p^{k}\cdot r-1)}\right\}=\inf_{k\geq 1}\left\{1,\left|p\right|_{E}^{1/(p-1)}\right\}=\left|p\right|_{E}^{1/(p-1)}.

Now by the hypothesis of the theorem x∈(p∗​OE)−{0}x\in(p^{*}{O}_{E})-\{0\}. Thus

|x|E≤|p∗|E<|p|E1/(p−1).\left|x\right|_{E}\leq\left|p^{*}\right|_{E}<\left|p\right|_{E}^{1/(p-1)}.

Hence under the hypothesis of the lemma, the asserted estimate holds. This proves the lemma.

§ 9.9 Proof of the fundamental estimate for |Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈|\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right| and |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈|\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right|.

Now one is ready to prove the fundamental estimate [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

Theorem 9.9.1.

For X,C,L,L′X,C,L,L^{\prime} satisfying § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3, and for an odd prime ℓ≫0\ell\gg 0 one has

|Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈|≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗,\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right|\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{{\ell^{*}}},

and also

|Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈|≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗.\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right|\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{{\ell^{*}}}.

Proof of Theorem 9.9.1.

The strategy of the proof is the same as the local strategy of [Joshi, 2023b]. One exhibits an element, namely 𝝃𝐳=𝝃𝐳ΘJ​o​s​h​i\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}}^{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}} (resp. 𝝃𝐳=𝝃𝐳ΘM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}}=\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}_{\Theta}}^{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}), of Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}, Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}, Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}, Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} for which the absolute value can be computed and one shows that |𝝃𝐳|\left|\boldsymbol{\xi}_{\mathbf{z}}\right| exceeds the number on the right of the stated inequality. Since |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈|\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right| (resp. |Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈|\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right|) on the left of the asserted inequality is a supremum, the inequality claimed in the theorem will follow if the absolute value of this chosen element bounds above the quantity on the right of the asserted inequality in the theorem.

Since Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈,Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~,Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈,Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}},{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}},{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}},{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} as defined in § 9.8.1, Theorem-Definition 9.8.1.1 are adelic, and |Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈|\left|{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right| and |Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈|\left|{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}\right| are defined multiplicatively, one may work with components Θ~𝐈J​o​s​h​i,w{\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi},w}, Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w{\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w} for each w∈𝕍¯w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}. So it is enough to estimate |Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w|\left|{\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w}\right| and then take product over all w∈𝕍¯w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}.

First I will work with the product versions Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} and Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} and then deduce the inequality for the tensor product versions Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} and Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} from this.

Note that these products are finite by Corollary 9.8.1.3. [As remarked earlier, by Lemma 9.8.2.7, |logp⁡(1+pw∗)|Lw′=|p∗|Lw′\left|\log_{p}(1+p_{w}^{*})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}=\left|p^{*}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}. So logB​K⁡(𝟏+𝐩∗)\log_{BK}({\bf 1+p^{*}}) contributes an element of unit norm in the product.]

So it suffices to establish the inequality (for w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​sw\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss})

|Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w|≥|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗.\left|{\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w}\right|\geq\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{{\ell^{*}}}.

For this purpose it will be convenient to work with the Bloch-Kato logarithms § 9.7.2 of the cohomological classes 𝝃𝐲\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\bf y}}. Then Equation 9.7.2.1 asserts that the codomain of Bloch-Kato logarithm logB​K\log_{BK} is, for each w∈𝕍L′,pw\in\mathbb{V}_{L^{\prime},p}, the field Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} considered as a ℚpw{\mathbb{Q}}_{p_{w}}-vector space. This means that in the product setting i.e. in 𝐈~J​o​s​h​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} and 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}, each class 𝝃𝐲¯j\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\underline{{\bf y}}}_{j}} contributes logB​K⁡(𝝃𝐲¯j)\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\underline{{\bf y}}}_{j}}) in Lw;𝐲j′L^{\prime}_{w;{\bf y}_{j}} to the corresponding factor of 𝐈~J​o​s​h​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}} (resp. 𝐈~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​iℚ\widetilde{\mathscrbf{I}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{{\mathbb{Q}}}).

Now let me say how one may deduce the inequality for Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} from Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} (resp. Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} from Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}). One may pass from the finite direct product ∏w|pLw′\prod_{w|p}L^{\prime}_{w} (equivalently from the finite direct sum) of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector spaces to the tensor product ⊗w|pLw′\otimes_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime} of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector spaces as follows. Consider the mapping

∏w|pLw′∋(aw)⟼⊗w|p(aw)∈⨂w|pLw′⟼|⊗w|paw|⊗w|pLw′∈ℝ,\prod_{w|p}L^{\prime}_{w}\ni(a_{w})\longmapsto\otimes_{w|p}(a_{w})\in\bigotimes_{w|p}L^{\prime}_{w}\longmapsto\left|\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{w|p}a_{w}\right|_{\otimes_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime}}\in{\mathbb{R}},

where first mapping is the natural homomorphism of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector spaces:

∏w|pL′w→⊗w|pL′w,\prod_{w|p}L^{\prime}_{w}\to\otimes_{w|p}L^{\prime}_{w},

and the second mapping is the tensor norm. In other words, one considers the image of the theta-values locii in the tensor product (via the first mapping) and then takes supremum over the tensor norms of all the images under the first homomorphism. This is where the cross-norm property § 7.6.2 of the tensor product norms comes in to play. This property says one has

|⊗w|paw|⊗w|pLw′=∏w|p|aw|Lw′.\left|\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{w|p}a_{w}\right|_{\otimes_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime}}=\prod_{w|p}\left|a_{w}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}.

Hence one may also work with suprema of absolute values of the images of the theta-locii in the tensor products i.e. one can work with Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}} instead of Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (resp. work with Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~,Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}},{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) and still arrive at the required estimates in the tensor product settings (i.e. for Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (resp. Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) of [Mochizuki, 2021c]. Notably, since the tensor product ⊗w|pLw′\otimes_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime} is constructed using the product ∏w|pLw′\prod_{w|p}L_{w}^{\prime} (more precisely the tensor product is the quotient of a suitable free ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-module on the set underlying this product), one can expect that the theta-values locus in the tensor product setting (i.e. Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈,Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}},{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) should provide tighter upper bounds than the theta-values locus in the product setting i.e. Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈~,Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈~{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}},{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\tilde{\mathscrbf{I}}}.

In any of these cases, each class 𝝃𝐲¯j\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\underline{{\bf y}}}_{j}} contributes logB​K⁡(𝝃𝐲¯j)\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{{\underline{{\bf y}}}_{j}}) in Lw;𝐲j′L^{\prime}_{w;{\bf y}_{j}} and by the definition of this class and, at each ww one has, by (9.7.2.2) one has:

(9.9.2) |logB​K⁡(𝝃w,j)|Lw′,j=|logLw′⁡(1+p∗⋅qw;j1/2​ℓ)p∗|Lw′,j for ​j=1,2,…,ℓ∗\left|\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{w,j})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\left|\frac{\log_{L_{w}^{\prime}}(1+p^{*}\cdot q_{w;j}^{1/2\ell})}{p^{*}}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}\qquad\text{ for }j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}

By Lemma 9.8.2.7 one has:

(9.9.3) |logB​K⁡(𝝃w,j)|Lw′,j=|logLw′⁡(1+p∗⋅qw;j1/2​ℓ)p∗|Lw′,j=|qw;j1/2​ℓ|Lw′,j for ​j=1,2,…,ℓ∗\left|\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{w,j})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\left|\frac{\log_{L_{w}^{\prime}}(1+p^{*}\cdot q_{w;j}^{1/2\ell})}{p^{*}}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\left|q_{w;j}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}\qquad\text{ for }j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}

Now by the valuation scaling property Theorem 4.2.2.1(4) one obtains

(9.9.4) |logB​K⁡(𝝃w,j)|Lw′,j=|qw;j1/2​ℓ|Lw′,j=|qw;11/2​ℓ|Lw′,1j2/ℓ∗2​ for ​j=1,2,…,ℓ∗\left|\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{w,j})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\left|q_{w;j}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\left|q_{w;1}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{j^{2}/{\ell^{*}}^{2}}_{L_{w}^{\prime},1}\text{ for }j=1,2,\ldots,{\ell^{*}}

Hence (writing qwq_{w} in place of qw;1q_{w;1})

(9.9.5) ∏j=1ℓ∗|logB​K⁡(𝝃w,j)|Lw′,j=∏j=1ℓ∗|qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′,j=∏j=1ℓ∗|qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′,1j2/ℓ∗2=|qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′,1∑j=1ℓ∗j2ℓ∗2.\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\left|\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{w,j})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{j^{2}/{\ell^{*}}^{2}}_{L_{w}^{\prime},1}=\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},1}^{\sum_{j=1}^{{\ell^{*}}}\frac{j^{2}}{{\ell^{*}}^{2}}}.

Hence one may pass to product over w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset and over all rational primes pp for which 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset:

(9.9.6) ∏p∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅∏j=1ℓ∗|logB​K⁡(𝝃w,j)|Lw′,j=∏p∏w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅|qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′,1∑j=1ℓ∗j2ℓ∗2.\prod_{p}\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\prod_{j=1}^{\ell^{*}}\left|\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\xi}_{w,j})\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},j}=\prod_{p}\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},1}^{\sum_{j=1}^{{\ell^{*}}}\frac{j^{2}}{{\ell^{*}}^{2}}}.

Now the proof can be completed by estimating, for each w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset, the factor |qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′,1∑j=1ℓ∗j2ℓ∗2\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime},1}^{\sum_{j=1}^{{\ell^{*}}}\frac{j^{2}}{{\ell^{*}}^{2}}} contributed by ww and this estimate is provided by the proof of [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem 9.2.1]. This proves the theorem.

Remark 9.9.7.

It is precisely because of Lemma 9.8.2.7 and the property established by Equation 9.9.2 in the proof of Theorem 9.9.1 that one recovers Mochizuki’s multiplicative action of theta-values on log-shells depicted in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Figure 3.1], i.e. multiplication by theta-value on the log-shell, used in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Theorem 3.11] for defining Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} instead of constructing crystalline Galois cohomology classes as has been done here. ∙\bullet

§ 9.10 Relationship with Mochizuki’s log-volumes and hulls

Since Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} (resp. Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) are contained in adelic compact sets, one can compute volumes of the smallest compact subset containing these sets. So one needs to define a volume of sets of this type which arise in realizing this idea. This theory is detailed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 3.1, Proposition 3.9] and this theory is applied in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] and in [Mochizuki, 2021d] for estimating the volume Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}) of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}. More precisely, Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}) is the volume of the smallest compact set (of a suitable sort chosen below) containing Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}. In [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d] one works with

LogVol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈)=log⁡Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈)∈ℝ∪{±∞},{\rm LogVol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}})=\log{\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}})\in{\mathbb{R}}\cup\{\pm\infty\},

which is the natural logarithm of Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}).

The fundamental inequality of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] is an assertion about the log-volume LogVol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm LogVol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}) of Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}. Equivalently, it is an inequality about the volume Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}). As I have remarked in [Joshi, 2023c, § 1.12], the volume computation of [Mochizuki, 2021c] is quite similar to the sort of volume computations in classical Teichmuller Theory which, for instance, occur in [Mirzakhani, 2007].

§ 9.10.1 

As explained in § 1, my approach to establishing [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] i.e. establishing the fundamental estimate for LogVol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm LogVol}({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}^{\boldsymbol{\mathscrbf{I}}}}) is different from that of Mochizuki. Though at this point, using the results of the preceding sections along with the Rosetta Stone Fragments 8.3.5, 8.3.6, 8.5, 8.7.1, 8.11.3 and Theorem-Definition 9.8.1.1, it is possible to proceed exactly as Mochizuki does, to arrive at Mochizuki’s proof of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

However once the principles underlying [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] are understood, one can formulate approaches different from that of Mochizuki. I will take this approach to the proof rather than repeat Mochizuki’s approach.

§ 9.10.2 

Let me begin with the theory of volumes described in [Mochizuki, 2021c]. The basic properties are summarized in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Proposition 3.9] and also in [Mochizuki, 2015, Proposition 5.7].

Let L′L^{\prime} be a number field, and for w|pw|p in L′L^{\prime}, one has the pp-adic field Lw′L_{w}^{\prime}. Let OLw′⊂Lw′{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}\subset L_{w}^{\prime} be the ring of integers. Since Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} is a locally compact abelian group, there is a unique normalized translation invariant (real valued) Haar measure on Lw′L_{w}^{\prime} which I will denote by VolLw′{\rm Vol}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}.

If S⊂LwS\subset L_{w}, is a measurable subset, for some ww, I will write VolLw′​(S){\rm Vol}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}(S) for its normalized Haar measure. Here normalization means the following:

VolLw′​(OLw′)=1.{\rm Vol}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}({O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}})=1.

Let

(9.10.2.1) log:(0,∞)→ℝ\log:(0,\infty)\to{\mathbb{R}}

be the natural real-valued logarithm function and extend log\log by setting

log⁡(0)=−∞​ and ​log⁡(∞)=∞.\log(0)=-\infty\text{ and }\log(\infty)=\infty.

This extended logarithm function takes values in ℝ∪{±∞}{\mathbb{R}}\cup\{\pm\infty\}. By the log-volume S⊂Lw′S\subset L_{w}^{\prime}, I will mean

LogVolLw′​(S)=log⁡(VolLw′​(S))∈ℝ∪{±∞}.{{\rm LogVol}}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}({S})=\log({\rm Vol}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}(S))\in{\mathbb{R}}\cup\{\pm\infty\}.

In particular, this means that one has

LogVolLw′​(OLw′)=0.{{\rm LogVol}}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}({{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}})=0.

Let π∈OE\pi\in{O}_{E} be a uniformizer. Then by translation invariance of the Haar measure VolE{\rm Vol}_{E} (or otherwise) one has

Vol⁡(π​OLw′)=|π|Lw′{\rm Vol}(\pi{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}})=\left|\pi\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}

and so

LogVolLw′​(π​OLw′)=log⁡(|π|Lw′).{{\rm LogVol}}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}({\pi{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}})=\log(\left|\pi\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}).

The following lemma is now elementary.

Lemma 9.10.2.2.

Let EE be a pp-adic field with absolute value |−|E\left|-\right|_{E} and let S=α+λ​OES=\alpha+\lambda{O}_{E} be a non-empty open subset for some α∈E\alpha\in E and λ∈E∗\lambda\in E^{*}. Then

  1. (1)
    VolE​(S)=VolE​(α+λ⋅OE)=Vol⁡(λ​OE),{\rm Vol}_{E}(S)={\rm Vol}_{E}(\alpha+\lambda\cdot{O}_{E})={\rm Vol}(\lambda{O}_{E}),

    and hence

  2. (2)
    VolE​(α+λ⋅OE)=Vol⁡(λ​OE)=|λ|E,{\rm Vol}_{E}(\alpha+\lambda\cdot{O}_{E})={\rm Vol}(\lambda{O}_{E})=\left|\lambda\right|_{E},

    and also

  3. (3)
    Vol⁡(λ​OE)=sup{|s|E:s∈λ​OE}=|λ|E,{\rm Vol}(\lambda{O}_{E})=\sup\{\left|s\right|_{E}:s\in\lambda{O}_{E}\}=\left|\lambda\right|_{E},

    and, in particular,

  4. (4)

    for any s∈λ⋅OEs\in\lambda\cdot{O}_{E} (note that s∈Ss\in S if and only if α=0\alpha=0) one has the tautology

    |λ|E=VolE​(S)≥|s|E.\left|\lambda\right|_{E}={\rm Vol}_{E}(S)\geq\left|s\right|_{E}.

Proof.

The first equality is the translation invariance of Vol{\rm Vol} and the second equality is clear from the definition of VolE{\rm Vol}_{E}. The remaining assertions are clear.

§ 9.10.3 Weighted volumes

These considerations can be extended as follows. Let E1,…,EnE_{1},\ldots,E_{n} be finite extensions of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. The theory of volumes and log-volumes on E1,…,EnE_{1},\ldots,E_{n} extends to a theory of weighted volumes on the tensor product E=E1⊗ℚpE2⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEnE=E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}. Let Γ={γ1,γ2,…,γn}⊂(0,1]⊂ℝ\Gamma=\{\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2},\ldots,\gamma_{n}\}\subset(0,1]\subset{\mathbb{R}} be a set of weights. Then the Γ\Gamma-weighted volume VolΓE1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEn{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma}_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}} is a function on certain measuable subsets of the ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector space EE. This is defined as follows.

Recall from [Schneider, 2002], that E1⊗ℚpE2E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2} is equipped with topology which has a fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero consisting of sets of the form V1⊗V2⊗⋯⊗VnV_{1}\otimes V_{2}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{n} where Vi⊂EiV_{i}\subset E_{i} is a ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}-lattice in each EiE_{i}.

So it suffices to define

(9.10.3.1) VolE1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEn(V1⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤpVn)=VolE1γ1(V1)⋯VolEnγn(Vn).{\rm Vol}_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}}(V_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{n})={\rm Vol}^{\gamma_{1}}_{E_{1}}(V_{1})\cdots{\rm Vol}_{E_{n}}^{\gamma_{n}}(V_{n}).

This leads to the following version of Lemma 9.10.2.2:

Lemma 9.10.3.2.

Let, for i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n, Vi=αi+λi​OEi⊂OEiV_{i}=\alpha_{i}+\lambda_{i}{O}_{E_{i}}\subset{O}_{E_{i}} with αi∈Ei\alpha_{i}\in E_{i} and λi∈Ei∗\lambda_{i}\in E_{i}^{*}. Then

  1. (1)
    VolE1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEnΓ(V1⊗ℤpV2⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤpVn)=∏i=1nVolEiγi(Vi).{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma}_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}}(V_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{2}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{n})=\prod_{i=1}^{n}{\rm Vol}^{\gamma_{i}}_{E_{i}}(V_{i}).
  2. (2)

    Hence

    VolE1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEnΓ(V1⊗ℤpV2⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤpVn)=∏i=1nVolEiΓ(Vi)=∏i=1n|λi|Eiγi,{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma}_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}}(V_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{2}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{n})=\prod_{i=1}^{n}{\rm Vol}_{E_{i}}^{\Gamma}(V_{i})=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left|\lambda_{i}\right|^{\gamma_{i}}_{E_{i}},
  3. (3)

    and hence if si∈λi​OEi∩Ei∗s_{i}\in\lambda_{i}{O}_{E_{i}}\cap E_{i}^{*} then

    VolE1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEnΓ(V1⊗ℤpV2⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤpVn)=∏i=1nVolEiγi(Vi)≥∏i=1n|si|γi.{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma}_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}}(V_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{2}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}V_{n})=\prod_{i=1}^{n}{\rm Vol}_{E_{i}}^{\gamma_{i}}(V_{i})\geq\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left|s_{i}\right|^{\gamma_{i}}.

§ 9.10.4 

The sets of interest to us, arising in Theorem 7.7.3.1, contain tensor products of sets of the form

∏w∈𝕍¯(λw⋅OLw′)\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}}(\lambda_{w}\cdot{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}})

for λw∈Lw′⁣∗\lambda_{w}\in L_{w}^{\prime*} satisfying the condition: for all w∉∪p𝕍¯o​d​d,s​spw\notin\cup_{p}\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}, λw∈OLw′∗\lambda_{w}\in{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}^{*}.

For tensor products sets, one may define weighted adelic volumes using the preceding formalism:

(9.10.4.1) Vol⁡(∏w∈𝕍¯(λw⋅OLw′))=∏w∈𝕍¯VolLw′​(λw⋅OLw′){\rm Vol}\left(\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}}(\lambda_{w}\cdot{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}})\right)=\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}}{\rm Vol}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}(\lambda_{w}\cdot{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}})

with some choice of weights. The condition that λw∈OLw′∗\lambda_{w}\in{O}_{L_{w}^{\prime}}^{*} for all but finitely many ww ensures that this volume is finite. Hence the sets of interest to us have a finite volume. Notably, for sets of this type, the volume is related to absolute values through the above elementary lemma.

§ 9.10.5 

Fix a prime pp such that 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset. Let {w1,…,wm}=𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s\{w_{1},\ldots,w_{m}\}=\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p} be all the distinct primes of L′L^{\prime} lying over pp and also contained in 𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}. Take

(9.10.5.1) Γp={1/[Lwi′:Lmod,v]:wi∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s}\Gamma_{p}=\{1/[L^{\prime}_{w_{i}}:{L_{\rm mod}}_{,v}]:w_{i}\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\}

as the set of weights. This sets of weights is determined by Proposition 9.4.2.4 and coincides with the choice of weights in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.1.1]. These are the weights and sets of interest to us here, and in [Mochizuki, 2021c] and [Mochizuki, 2021d], are the tensor product subsets which arise in the proof of Theorem 7.7.3.1.

This allows us to compute VolE{\rm Vol}_{E} for suitable subsets using absolute values and hence the two calculations will yield the same lower estimates.

§ 9.10.6 

In particular, the notion of weighted volumes and log-weighted-volumes extends verbatim to the ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} vector spaces obtained from the pp-component of the log-shells IM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,pℚp{I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}_{Mochizuki,p}, and IM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,pℚp𝕊j+1{}^{\mathbb{S}_{j+1}}{I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}_{Mochizuki,p}. In particular, for any measurable set S⊂IM​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,pℚp𝕊j+1S\subset{}^{\mathbb{S}_{j+1}}{I}^{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}_{Mochizuki,p}, one can talk of its volume Vol⁡(S){\rm Vol}(S).

§ 9.10.7 

Let

S⊂E1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEn=⨁αE′α.S\subset E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n}=\bigoplus_{\alpha}E^{\prime}_{\alpha}.

Then the hull of SS, denoted here by hull​(S)\text{hull}(S), is the smallest subset hull(S)⊂E1⊗ℚp⋯⊗ℚpEnhull(S)\subset E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{n} of the tensor product such that hull​(S)⊃S\text{hull}(S)\supset S and whose image in the direct sum decomposition on the right is of the form

⨁αλα​OEα′\bigoplus_{\alpha}\lambda_{\alpha}{O}_{E_{\alpha}^{\prime}}

where 0≠λα∈OEα′0\neq\lambda_{\alpha}\in{O}_{E_{\alpha}^{\prime}}.

Properties of hulls are established in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5(ii)].

The following lemma is now clear:

Lemma 9.10.7.1.

Let S′⊃S=(τ1OE1)⊗ℤp(τ2OE2)⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤp(τnOEn)S^{\prime}\supset S=(\tau_{1}{O}_{E_{1}})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}(\tau_{2}{O}_{E_{2}})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}(\tau_{n}{O}_{E_{n}}) with τi∈OEi\tau_{i}\in{O}_{E_{i}} for i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n and suppose Γp\Gamma_{p} are chosen as above and suppose that one has an element s1⊗s2⊗⋯⊗sn∈Ss_{1}\otimes s_{2}\otimes\cdots\otimes s_{n}\in S with si∈τi​OEis_{i}\in\tau_{i}{O}_{E_{i}} for i=1,…,ni=1,\ldots,n. Then

VolΓ​(h​u​l​l​(S′))≥VolΓp​(h​u​l​l​(S))≥VolΓp​(S)≥∏i=1n|si|Eiγi≥∏i=1n|si|Ei.{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma}(hull(S^{\prime}))\geq{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma_{p}}(hull(S))\geq{\rm Vol}^{\Gamma_{p}}(S)\geq\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left|s_{i}\right|^{\gamma_{i}}_{E_{i}}\geq\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left|s_{i}\right|_{E_{i}}.

Proof.

The first inequality is immediate from the properties of the hull in [Mochizuki, 2021c, § 3]. So the only point which needs to be checked is that 0<γi≤10<\gamma_{i}\leq 1, so the last inequality follows from the fact that all the τi\tau_{i}, and hence all the sis_{i} have absolute values at most one.

§ 9.10.8 Mochizuki’s Hulls and Convex closures

In this subsection I want to provide the following proposition which clarifies my usage of convex closures and Mochizuki’s holomorphic hulls detailed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5]. The notion of convex closure can be made in any Banach space [Schneider, 2002]. Mochizuki’s notion of holomorphic hull is a bit more specific. To establish the relationship assume, for notational simplicity, that E1,E2E_{1},E_{2} are two pp-adic fields considered as finite dimensional vector spaces over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}.

I work with the tensor product norm |−|E1⊗ℚpE2\left|-\right|_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}} and the normed ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}-vector space

(E1⊗ℚpE2,|−|E1⊗ℚpE2)(E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2},\left|-\right|_{E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}})

equipped with this tensor norm.

On the other hand Mochizuki’s approach to holomorphic hulls detailed in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5] is based on the following decomposing the tensor product vector space E1⊗ℚpE2E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}:

f:E1⊗ℚpE2  ⨁αFαf:E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}{\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 8.875pt\raise 4.72855pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-1.72855pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\simeq}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces}\bigoplus_{\alpha}F_{\alpha}

into a direct sum of pp-adic fields Fα⊃ℚpF_{\alpha}\supset{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} (obviously the set {α}\{\alpha\} is also finite) and work, according to [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5], relative to this decomposition. Since E1⊗ℚpE2E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2} is finite dimensional over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}, ff is an isomorphism of finite dimensional Banach spaces over ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}.

Proposition 9.10.8.1.

In the notation of this paragraph, suppose U⊂E1⊗ℚpE2U\subset E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2} is a relatively compact subset. Let H=H⁡(U)=h​u​l​l​(U)H=H(U)=hull(U) be the hull of UU as defined by [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5, Page 543]. Then

  1. (1)

    HH is a convex subset of ⊕αFα\oplus_{\alpha}F_{\alpha} containing f⁡(U)f(U) and by [Mochizuki, 2021c, Properties P1, P2, P3, Page 534] it is the minimal convex subset containing f⁡(U)f(U) with this property.

  2. (2)

    If V⊂E1⊗ℚpE2V\subset E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2} is a convex subset of this normed vector space then its image under ff is also convex.

  3. (3)

    In particular, if PP is a tensor product region of P⊆E1⊗ℚpE2P\subseteq E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2} in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.1.1], then H(P)⊆⊕αFαH(P)\subseteq\oplus_{\alpha}F_{\alpha} is the image of the convex closure of P⊆E1⊗ℚpE2P\subseteq E_{1}\otimes_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}E_{2}.

Proof.

By the definition of the hull given in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5] the hull is an ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}-module. By the definition of convex subsets [Schneider, 2002, Chap I, § 2], the hull is a convex subset as it is an ℤp{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}-module. By [Mochizuki, 2021c, Remark 3.9.5, Properties P1, P2, P3] it is the smallest subset with the said properties. This proves (1). The assertion (2) is clear from the definitions [Schneider, 2002]. The last assertion is a consequence of the fact that holomorphic hull is the convex closure of f⁡(P)f(P).

Remark 9.10.8.2.

Because of Proposition 9.10.8.1, one can work with hulls and convex closures on an equal footing and this allows me to translate my results to Mochizuki’s context. ∙\bullet

§ 9.11 Proof of the fundamental estimate for Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}) and Vol⁡(Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈){\rm Vol}({{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}})

Now one is ready to prove the fundamental estimate [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12].

Theorem 9.11.1.

For X,C,L,L′X,C,L,L^{\prime} satisfying § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3, and for an odd prime ℓ≫0\ell\gg 0 one has

Vol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈)≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗,{\rm Vol}({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}})\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{{\ell^{*}}},

and also

Vol⁡(Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈)≥∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗.{\rm Vol}({{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}})\geq\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{{\ell^{*}}}.

Proof.

By Proposition 9.10.8.1, one can work with Mochizuki’s holomorphic hulls or convex closures (in Banach spaces). It will be enough to prove this for one of the two Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈,Θ~J​o​s​h​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}},{{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Joshi}}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}. I will prove the assertion for Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}}. The proof of Theorem 9.9.1 will serve as a template for this assertion. By the construction of these sets, Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} contains the classes 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}} given by Theorem-Definition 9.8.1.1 obtained from each choice of Tate parameters obtained using the standard point of the Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} and hence it contains a subset of the type considered in Lemma 9.10.7.1

∏w∈𝕍¯o​d​d,s​s(τ1OLw,1′)⊗ℤp(τ2OLw,2′)⊗ℤp⋯⊗ℤp(τℓ∗OLw,ℓ∗′),\prod_{w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}}(\tau_{1}{O}_{L^{\prime}_{w,1}})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}(\tau_{2}{O}_{L^{\prime}_{w,2}})\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}\cdots\otimes_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}}(\tau_{\ell^{*}}{O}_{L^{\prime}_{w,{\ell^{*}}}}),

with τj=logB​K⁡(𝚵0,𝐳j,w)\tau_{j}=\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{0,\mathbf{z}_{j},w}) (for suitable jj). So the volume of this set can be bounded by Lemma 9.10.7.1.

Since Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈{{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}} defined in § 9.8.1 is adelic, and weighted volumes are defined multiplicatively, one may work with components Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w{\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w} for each w∈𝕍¯w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}. So it is enough to estimate Vol⁡(Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w){\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w}) and then take product over all w∈𝕍¯w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}. Note that the product is finite by Corollary 9.8.1.3. So it suffices to establish the inequality Vol⁡(Θ~𝐈M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,w)≥|qw1/2​ℓ|ℓ∗{\rm Vol}({\widetilde{\Theta}^{\mathscrbf{I}}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},w})\geq\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|^{\ell^{*}}. This in turn is clear from the construction of these sets: they contain the classes 𝚵𝐳\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{\mathbf{z}} given by Theorem-Definition 9.8.1.1 obtained from each choice of Tate parameters obtained using the standard point of the Σ~L′\widetilde{\Sigma}_{L^{\prime}} and so contain a subset of the type Lemma 9.10.7.1 with τj=logB​K⁡(𝚵0,𝐳j,w)\tau_{j}=\log_{BK}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{0,\mathbf{z}_{j},w}) (for suitable jj). Using this and the relationship between weighted volumes absolute values established earlier and arguing as in the proof of Theorem 9.9.1, one obtains the assertion.

§ 9.11.1 Proof of Mochizuki’s Corollary 3.12

Mochizuki’s notational conventions [Mochizuki, 2021c, Page 420 and Page 608] sign conventions are a bit awkward to work with. The notation convention of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Page 420 and Page 608] is designed so that the ration of the LHS and RHS in [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12] is positive while both the LHS and RHS are negative. I will define

−|LogVol(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈)|=∑p−|LogVol(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,p)|=−∑p|LogVol(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,p)|.-\left|{\rm LogVol}({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}})\right|=\sum_{p}-\left|{\rm LogVol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},p})\right|=-\sum_{p}\left|{\rm LogVol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},p})\right|.

This is perfectly reasonable as the LogVol⁡(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i,p)≤0{\rm LogVol}({\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki},p})\leq 0 and this notation convention is compatible with the following standard properties of real numbers and logarithms: if 0<x≤10<x\leq 1 is a real number then

log⁡(x)≤0​ and so ​|log⁡(x)|=−log⁡(x)≥0​ and hence −|log⁡(x)|=log⁡(x)≤0.\log(x)\leq 0\text{ and so }\left|\log(x)\right|=-\log(x)\geq 0\text{ and hence }-\left|\log(x)\right|=\log(x)\leq 0.

Moreover if 0<x,y≤10<x,y\leq 1 are real numbers then

−|log⁡(x⋅y)|\displaystyle-\left|\log(x\cdot y)\right| =log⁡(x⋅y)\displaystyle=\log(x\cdot y)
=−|log⁡(x)|+(−|log⁡(y)|)\displaystyle=-\left|\log(x)\right|+(-\left|\log(y)\right|)
=−(|log⁡(x)|+|log⁡(y)|).\displaystyle=-(\left|\log(x)\right|+\left|\log(y)\right|).

To provide a translation of Theorem 9.11.1 into [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12], one must work with Mochizuki’s notational convention and the above observation regarding logarithms of real numbers. From Theorem 9.11.1 one obtains, using Mochizuki’s notational conventions [Mochizuki, 2021c, Page 420 and Page 608], the assertion known as [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]:

Corollary 9.11.1.1.

With notations and assumptions of Theorem 9.11.1, and in Mochizuki’s notational conventions [Mochizuki, 2021c, Page 420 and Page 608], one has

−1ℓ∗|LogVol(Θ~M​o​c​h​i​z​u​k​i𝐈)|≥−∑p,w∈𝕍¯po​d​d,s​s≠∅log|qw1/2​ℓ|Lw′.-\frac{1}{{\ell^{*}}}\left|{\rm LogVol}({{\widetilde{\Theta}}_{\scriptscriptstyle{Mochizuki}}}^{\mathscrbf{I}})\right|\geq-\sum_{p,w\in\underline{\mathbb{V}}^{odd,ss}_{p}\neq\emptyset}\log\left|q_{w}^{1/2\ell}\right|_{L_{w}^{\prime}}.

10 Appendix: Frobenioids and Hodge-Theaters à la Mochizuki via [Joshi, 2021a]

[Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] uses Mochizuki’s notion of Frobenioids and Hodge-Theaters. Let me explicate how these objects of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] arise from the perspective of [Joshi, 2021a]. I will not use the broad definition of Frobenioids given in [Mochizuki, 2008] but use [Mochizuki, 2008, Example 6.1 and Example 6.3] which are more than adequate for my discussion and for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

§ 10.1 Frobenioid of an archimedean valued field

The simplest example of a Frobenioid is the Frobenioid of an archimedean valued field. Let me recall it here.

Let KK be a field equipped with an archimedean absolute value |−|K\left|-\right|_{K}. I will assume that KK contains −1\sqrt{-1} (this is also the assumption throughout most of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c, Mochizuki, 2021d]) and hence by Ostrowski’s Theorem, K≃ℂK\simeq{\mathbb{C}} as valued fields, where ℂ{\mathbb{C}} is equipped with the standard complex absolute value |−|ℂ\left|-\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}}.

Let

(10.1.1) Φ⁡(K)=ℝ≥0,\Phi(K)={\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0},

where ℝ≥0{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} is the additive monoid of non-negative real numbers. Here and in what follows, let Φ​(K)g​p\Phi(K)^{gp} be the group associated to the monoid Φ⁡(K)\Phi(K). Then as Φ⁡(K)=ℝ≥0\Phi(K)={\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}, so one has Φ​(K)g​p=ℝ\Phi(K)^{gp}={\mathbb{R}}. Let

(10.1.2) K∗→Φ​(K)g​p=ℝ,K^{*}\to\Phi(K)^{gp}={\mathbb{R}},

be a homomorphism of groups.

Note that if (K,|−|K)=(ℂ,|−|ℂp)(K,\left|-\right|_{K})=({\mathbb{C}},\left|-\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}) then one has the familiar homomorphism of monoids

(10.1.3) ℂ∗⟼ℝ​ given by ​z⟼log⁡(|z|ℂ),{\mathbb{C}}^{*}\longmapsto{\mathbb{R}}\text{ given by }z\longmapsto\log(\left|z\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}}),

where log:ℝ>0→ℝ\log:{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\to{\mathbb{R}} is the natural logarithm of a positive real number. This will be referred to as the archimedean (arithmetic) degree homomorphism.

The Frobenioid associated to the archimedean valued field (K,|−|K)(K,\left|-\right|_{K}) (see [Mochizuki, 2008, Example 6.3]) is the triple

(10.1.4) 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(K,|−|K)=(Φ(K)=ℝ≥0,K∗→Φ(K)g​p=ℝ).\mathfrak{Frob}(K,\left|-\right|_{K})=(\Phi(K)={\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0},K^{*}\to\Phi(K)^{gp}={\mathbb{R}}).

§ 10.2 Frobenioid of a non-archimedean valued field

Let me now describe Frobenioid associated to a non-archimedean valued field as it will be used in what follows. Let KK be a field equipped with a non-archimedean absolute value |−|K\left|-\right|_{K}. Typically KK will be either perfectoid with tilt ℂp♭{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat} or a discretely valued for this discussion.

To fix the notation and sign conventions, for K=ℂpK={\mathbb{C}}_{p}, I will require that

(10.2.1) |p|ℂp=p−1.\left|p\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}=p^{-1}.

Let OK⊂K{O}_{K}\subset K be its ring of integers, let OK⊳=OK−{0}{O}^{\triangleright}_{K}={O}_{K}-\{0\} be considered as a multiplicative monoid and let OK∗{O}_{K}^{*} be the group of units of OK{O}_{K}. Let |K∗|K={|x|K:x∈K∗}\left|K^{*}\right|_{K}=\{\left|x\right|_{K}:x\in K^{*}\} and similarly define |OK|K\left|{O}_{K}\right|_{K}. Let

(10.2.2) Φ⁡(K)=OK⊳/OK∗\Phi(K)={O}^{\triangleright}_{K}/{O}_{K}^{*}

be the quotient of the multiplicative monoid OK⊳{O}^{\triangleright}_{K} by its submonoid of units OK∗{O}_{K}^{*}, this is equipped with the canonical isomorphism of monoids

(10.2.3) Φ⁡(K)​  ​|OK⊳|K.\Phi(K){\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 5.1701pt\raise 6.5pt\hbox{{}\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-1.75pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\left|\cdot\right|_{K}}$}}}\kern 3.0pt}}}}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 27.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces}\left|{O}^{\triangleright}_{K}\right|_{K}.

Let Φ​(K)g​p\Phi(K)^{gp} be the group associated with the monoid Φ⁡(K)\Phi(K), one has a homomorphism of monoids

(10.2.4) Φ⁡(K)→|OK⊳|K→|K∗|K.\Phi(K)\to\left|{O}^{\triangleright}_{K}\right|_{K}\to\left|K^{*}\right|_{K}.

which factors as

(10.2.5) Φ⁡(K)→Φ​(K)g​p→|K∗|.\Phi(K)\to\Phi(K)^{gp}\to\left|K^{*}\right|.

Then according to [Mochizuki, 2008], the data

(10.2.6) 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(K,|−|K)=(Φ(K),K∗→Φ(K)g​p),\mathfrak{Frob}(K,\left|-\right|_{K})=(\Phi(K),K^{*}\to\Phi(K)^{gp}),

consisting of the monoid Φ⁡(K)\Phi(K) and the natural homomorphism of K∗→Φ​(K)g​pK^{*}\to\Phi(K)^{gp} given by mapping

(10.2.7) x⟼xmodOK∗x\longmapsto x\bmod{{O}_{K}^{*}}

is the Frobenioid associated to the non-archimedean valued field (K,|−|K)(K,\left|-\right|_{K}).

For Diophantine applications, one needs to work with the notion of (local) arithmetic degrees. This is done by means of the natural homomorphism

(10.2.8) Φ⁡(K)→ℝ\Phi(K)\to{\mathbb{R}}

given by

(10.2.9) x⟼log⁡(|x|K)∈ℝ,x\longmapsto\log(\left|x\right|_{K})\in{\mathbb{R}},

which will be called the (local) arithmetic degree. Since ℝ{\mathbb{R}} is a group, by the universal property of Φ​(K)g​p\Phi(K)^{gp}, the arithmetic degree factors as a homomorphism

(10.2.10) Φ⁡(K)→Φ​(K)g​p→ℝ,\Phi(K)\to\Phi(K)^{gp}\to{\mathbb{R}},

and so composing with K∗→Φ​(K)g​pK^{*}\to\Phi(K)^{gp} one gets the arithmetic degree homomorphism

(10.2.11) degK:K∗→ℝ{\rm deg}_{K}:K^{*}\to{\mathbb{R}}

given by x⟼log⁡(|x|K)x\longmapsto\log(\left|x\right|_{K}).

If K=ℚpK={\mathbb{Q}}_{p} with the standard valuation vℚpv_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}} on ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}, then

(10.2.12) Φ⁡(ℚp)=ℤp⊳/ℤp∗≃ℤ≥0​ and ​Φ​(ℚp)g​p=ℤ\Phi({\mathbb{Q}}_{p})={\mathbb{Z}}_{p}^{\triangleright}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}^{*}\simeq{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}\text{ and }\Phi({\mathbb{Q}}_{p})^{gp}={\mathbb{Z}}

and the arithmetic degree homomorphism is a homomorphism

(10.2.13)

which on p∈ℚp∗p\in{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}^{*} takes the value

(10.2.14) degℚp​(p)=log⁡(|p|ℚp).{\rm deg}_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}(p)=\log(\left|p\right|_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}).

§ 10.3 Induced Frobenioid structures

In the context of Diophantine applications of the Arithmetic Teichmuller Theory of [Joshi, 2021a, Joshi, 2022, Joshi, 2023a] and the theory of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], it is important to recognize that the Frobenioid of a pp-adic field EE

(10.3.1) (𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|E),degE)(\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{E}),{\rm deg}_{E})

depends on the absolute value |−|E\left|-\right|_{E}. This is best understood using the notion of induced Frobenioid structures. Let me discuss this, as this is not discussed in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c].

Suppose E→KE\to K is a homomorphism of valued fields, then one has Frobenioid associated to valued field 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|E)\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{E}) and as E↪KE\hookrightarrow K is a valued subfield, one can also consider EE as a subfield of KK with induced valuation, and so, one has a sub-Frobenioid 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|K)\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{K}) of the Frobenioid 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(K,|−|K)\mathfrak{Frob}(K,\left|-\right|_{K}) of KK obtained by considering the valuation induced on EE from KK. I will write this as

(10.3.2) 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|K)=(Φ(E),E∗→Φ(E)g​p)K\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{K})=(\Phi(E),E^{*}\to\Phi(E)^{gp})_{K}

and which I will call the Frobenioid structure on EE induced by KK.

Mochizuki does not work with induced structures in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], as Mochizuki’s theory, especially [Mochizuki, 2021c], does not use valued fields as such, and works with the abstract notion of Frobenioids. So my approach is slightly different from that taken in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] and will be used in what follows.

Typical example of this situation is the following: let EE be a pp-adic field and E↪KE\hookrightarrow K is an embedding of EE into an untilt KK of ℂp♭{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}. Since EE is a discretely valued field (E,|−|E)≃(E,|−|K)(E,\left|-\right|_{E})\simeq(E,\left|-\right|_{K}) is an isomorphism of discretely valued fields and hence the two Frobenioids 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|E)\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{E}) and 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|K)\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{K}) are abstractly isomorphic, but one wants to compare arithmetic degrees of the data (𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|E),degE)(\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{E}),{\rm deg}_{E}) and (𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(E,|−|K),degK|E)(\mathfrak{Frob}(E,\left|-\right|_{K}),{\rm deg}_{K}\big|_{E}).

Proposition 10.3.3.

Let E/ℚpE/{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} be a finite extension of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p} contained in ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p}. Let KK be an untilt of ℂp♭{\mathbb{C}}_{p}^{\flat}. Let ι:E↪K\iota:E\hookrightarrow K be an isometric embedding of EE into KK providing on EE a valuation given on ι⁡(E)\iota(E) by the restriction of the valuation of KK. Then one has

  1. (1)

    The two Frobenioid structures on EE induced by E↪ℂpE\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}_{p} and ι:E↪K\iota:E\hookrightarrow K are abstractly isomorphic.

  2. (2)

    In general, there may not exist any isomorphism of the two Frobenioid structures on EE provided by ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} and KK which is compatible with identity homomorphism on ℝ{\mathbb{R}} in the arithmetic degree homomorphisms (x∈E↪ℂp)⟼log⁡(|x|ℂp)∈ℝ(x\in E\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}_{p})\longmapsto\log(\left|x\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}})\in{\mathbb{R}} (resp. (x∈E↪K)⟼log⁡(|x|K)∈ℝ(x\in E\hookrightarrow K)\longmapsto\log(\left|x\right|_{K})\in{\mathbb{R}}).

Proof.

The fields EE and ι⁡(E)\iota(E) are isomorphic as valued fields, as both are discretely valued and one has an isomorphism given by the homomorphism ι|E:E→ι⁡(E)\iota|_{E}:E\to\iota(E). So the Frobenioids of E↪ℂpE\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}_{p} and E↪KE\hookrightarrow K are abstractly isomorphic. This proves the first assertion.

On the other hand, under the (local) arithmetic degree homomorphism of E↪ℂpE\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}_{p}, p⟼log⁡(|p|ℂp)∈ℝp\longmapsto\log(\left|p\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}})\in{\mathbb{R}} and ι⁡(E)↪K\iota(E)\hookrightarrow K, one has p⟼log⁡(|p|K)∈ℝp\longmapsto\log(\left|p\right|_{K})\in{\mathbb{R}} and vK​(p)v_{K}(p) which may not be equal to vℂp​(p)v_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}(p) and hence there may not exist any isomorphism between the Frobenioids of E↪ℂpE\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{C}}_{p} and ι⁡(E)↪K\iota(E)\hookrightarrow K which is compatible with the respective (local) arithmetic degrees and which is identity on ℝ{\mathbb{R}} i.e. there may not exist any commutative diagram of groups:

(10.3.4)

if the valuation of pp in ℂp{\mathbb{C}}_{p} and valuation of pp in KK do not coincide (and in general it is possible to find untilts KK such that this happens) i.e. log⁡(|x|ℂp)≠log⁡(|ι⁡(x)|K)\log(\left|x\right|_{{\mathbb{C}}_{p}})\neq\log(\left|\iota(x)\right|_{K}) in ℝ{\mathbb{R}} in general.

§ 10.4 Perfect Frobenioids and Perfectoids

An important point for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] is this: one wants to work with induced Frobenioids in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c] because one wants to allow valuations to be scaled by rationals (say |−|ℚp⟼|−|ℚp1/j2\left|-\right|_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}\longmapsto\left|-\right|_{{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}^{1/j^{2}}) (to be precise one wants a non-trivial scaling operation whose effect at the level of discretely valued pp-adic fields is this type of scaling). But such a scaling is not possible with Frobenioids of pp-adic fields, so Mochizuki remedies this with the introduction of perfect and realified Frobenioids where the value group is allowed to be ℚ{\mathbb{Q}} (or ℝ{\mathbb{R}}). This adds an additional notational and conceptual burden to his proof. Working with perfectoid fields allows one to overcome this difficulty quite naturally.

§ 10.4.1 

My approach to Mochizuki’s perfect and realified Frobenioids is summarized by the following proposition.

Proposition 10.4.1.1.

Let 𝔥​𝔬​𝔩X/E​(F)y\mathfrak{hol}_{X/E}(F)_{y} be an arithmetic holomorphic structure with y=(K,ιK:K♭≃F)y=(K,\iota_{K}:K^{\flat}\simeq F). Then

  1. (1)

    𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(K)\mathfrak{Frob}(K) is a perfect Frobenioid in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2008, Definition 1.1].

  2. (2)

    Suppose additionally that the value group of KK is equal to ℝ{\mathbb{R}} (equivalently FF has value group equal to ℝ{\mathbb{R}}), then 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(K)\mathfrak{Frob}(K) is a realified Frobenioid.

  3. (3)

    If EE is a pp-adic field and ι:E↪K\iota:E\hookrightarrow K is an embedding. The inclusion of Frobenioids 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(E)↪𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(K)\mathfrak{Frob}(E)\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{Frob}(K) provides a natural perfection, 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(K)\mathfrak{Frob}(K), of 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(E)\mathfrak{Frob}(E) and if KK has value group ℝ{\mathbb{R}}, then 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(K)\mathfrak{Frob}(K) is even a realification of 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(E)\mathfrak{Frob}(E) in the sense of [Mochizuki, 2008, Definition 1.1].

Proof.

The proofs are clear from the definitions [Mochizuki, 2008, Definition 1.1].

Remark 10.4.1.2.

Hence one could say that the above result demonstrates that there are many topologically inequivalent arithmetic models for the perfection of 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(E)\mathfrak{Frob}(E). This point is central even for [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c], as one wants a non-trivial variation of arithmetic-geometric data for the very statement of [Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12]. ∙\bullet

§ 10.5 Frobenioid of a number field

Let LL be a number field i.e. a finite extension of ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}, assume that LL has no real embeddings for simplicity (this will always be the case in [Mochizuki, 2021a, Mochizuki, 2021b, Mochizuki, 2021c]–for any choice of “initial Theta data”). Then for every prime vv of LL, archimedean or non-archimedean, one can associate to the completion LvL_{v}, a (local) Frobenioid for the local Field LvL_{v} (defined as above). Following Mochizuki, [Mochizuki, 2008, Example 6.3],

If vv is a complex archimedean prime of LL then let v¯\bar{v} be its complex conjugate.

As discussued in [Joshi, 2023a, § ], the Frobenioid 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(L)=(L∗,Φ(L),L∗→Φ(L)g​p)\mathfrak{Frob}(L)=(L^{*},\Phi(L),L^{*}\to\Phi(L)^{gp}) of the chosen number field LL is defined as follows. It consists of the data of the group L∗L^{*} and the monoid

(10.5.1) Φ⁡(L)=⨁vΦ⁡(Lv),\Phi(L)=\bigoplus\limits_{v}\Phi(L_{v}),

where the sum is over all primes vv (archimedean and non-archimdean) of LL. This comes equipped with the homomorphism

(10.5.2) L∗→Φ​(L)g​p=⨁vΦ​(Lv)g​pL^{*}\to\Phi(L)^{gp}=\bigoplus\limits_{v}\Phi(L_{v})^{gp}

given in the obvious way, and also a global arithmetic degree homomorphism

(10.5.3) Φ⁡(L)→ℝ\Phi(L)\to{\mathbb{R}}

given

(10.5.4) (xv)⟼∑vlog⁡(|xv|Lv)(x_{v})\longmapsto\sum_{v}\log(\left|x_{v}\right|_{L_{v}})

i.e. by the sum of local arithmetic degrees, which factors through Φ​(L)g​p\Phi(L)^{gp} as ℝ{\mathbb{R}} is a group and notably for any x∈L∗x\in L^{*}, one has the (logarithmic form of the) product formula (2.1.1):

(10.5.5) ∑vlog⁡(|x|Lv)=0.\sum_{v}\log(\left|x\right|_{L_{v}})=0.
Remark 10.5.6.

As established in [Joshi, 2023a, § ], each arithmeticoid 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{\bf y} provides a natural Frobenioid 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟​(𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L))\mathfrak{Frob}(\mathfrak{arith}(L)) and the product formula provides an hyperplane H𝐲H_{{\bf y}} (Theorem 4.6.1) and in fact one has a period mapping in 𝐲⟼H𝐲{\bf y}\longmapsto H_{{\bf y}} constructed by [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem ]. ∙\bullet

Let EE be a field and let X/EX/E be a geometrically connected, smooth, projective variety over EE. Let

(10.6.1) Φ⁡(X)=D​i​v+​(X)\Phi(X)=Div_{+}(X)

be the monoid of effective divisors on XX. Let E⁡(X)E(X) be the field of meromorphic functions on X/EX/E. Then one has a Frobenioid associated to X/EX/E given by the triple

(10.6.2) (Φ(X/E),E(X)∗→Φ(X/E)g​p)(\Phi(X/E),E(X)^{*}\to\Phi(X/E)^{gp})

where E​(X)∗→Φ​(X/E)g​pE(X)^{*}\to\Phi(X/E)^{gp} is the natural homomorphism given by

§ 10.7 A Frobenioid associated to a rigid analytic curve

I want to now describe a Frobenioid associated to the analytic space arising from a geometrically connected smooth quasi-projective curve over a pp-adic field. This will lead (in § 10.9) to the construction of Mochizuki’s tempered Frobenioid over an hyperbolic curve, which may be intuitively understood as the data of divisors descended (by Galois descent) from the universal cover of each tempered coverings of a fixed hyperbolic curve. So this construction is a little more elaborate than the ones described above but the key ideas are the same as above.

§ 10.7.1 

Let Z/EZ/E be a connected analytic space arising from the analytification of a geometrically connected, smooth quasi-projective variety of dimension one over a pp-adic field EE. I want to describe the construction of the tempered fundamental group given in [André, 2003a] as this will be used in the construction of Mochizuki’s Frobenioid associated to a hyperbolic curve over EE.

Let {(Zi,zi):i∈I}\left\{(Z_{i},z_{i}):i\in I\right\} be a countable, cofinal system of finite Galois coverings of (Z,zK)(Z,z_{K}) (with given geometric base-points dominating the geometric base-point zK:M⁡(K)→Zz_{K}:{M}(K)\to Z.

Let Zi∞/ZiZ_{i}^{\infty}/Z_{i} be the topological universal covering of ZiZ_{i} [Berkovich, 1990]. Let Zi∞,r​i​gZ_{i}^{\infty,rig} be the associated (classical) rigid analytic space (see [Berkovich, 1990]). Then one can describe tempered fundamental group ΠZ/Et​e​m​p\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{Z/E} explicitly as follows:

(10.7.2.1) ΠZ/Et​e​m​p=π1t​e​m​p​(Z,zK)=lim←i∈I⁡Gal⁡(Zi∞/Z).\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{Z/E}=\pi_{1}^{temp}(Z,z_{K})=\varprojlim_{i\in I}{\rm Gal}(Z_{i}^{\infty}/Z).

Then one has the following data

(10.7.2.2) Φt​e​m​p​(Z/E)=Div+~​(Z/E)=lim←i∈I⁡D​i​v+​(Zi∞,r​i​g)Gal⁡(Zi∞/Z),\Phi_{temp}(Z/E)=\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Z/E)=\varprojlim_{i\in I}Div_{+}(Z_{i}^{\infty,rig})^{{\rm Gal}(Z_{i}^{\infty}/Z)},

where Div+~​(Zi∞,r​i​g)\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Z_{i}^{\infty,rig}) is the group of effective divisors of the (classical) rigid analytic space Zi∞,r​i​gZ_{i}^{\infty,rig}; and let

(10.7.2.3) PDiv~​(Z/E)=lim←i∈I⁡P​D​i​v​(Zi∞,r​i​g)Gal⁡(Zi∞,r​i​g/Z),\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Z/E)=\varprojlim_{i\in I}PDiv(Z_{i}^{\infty,rig})^{{\rm Gal}(Z_{i}^{\infty,rig}/Z)},

where P​D​i​v​(Zi∞)PDiv(Z_{i}^{\infty}) is the group of principal divisors on Zi∞,r​i​gZ_{i}^{\infty,rig} i.e. the group of divisors of non-zero meromorphic functions on Zi∞,r​i​gZ_{i}^{\infty,rig}. One has a natural homomorphism

Mochizuki’s Tempered Frobenioid of Z/EZ/E is the data

(10.7.3.1) 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟(Z/E)=(Φt​e​m​p(Z/E),PDiv~(Z/E)→Φt​e​m​p(Z/E)g​p).\mathfrak{Frob}(Z/E)=\left(\Phi_{temp}(Z/E),\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Z/E)\to\Phi_{temp}(Z/E)^{gp}\right).

§ 10.8 The instructive example of Tate elliptic curves

Let KK be an algebraically closed perfectoid field with an isometric embedding of ℚp{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}. It is instructive to understand this for the concrete case of a (projective) Tate elliptic curve C/KC/K. Here by [André, 2003a], the (topological) universal cover of C/EC/E is 𝔾m→C\mathbb{G}_{m}\to C. Write ℤ^=lim←n⁡ℤn​ℤ\hat{{\mathbb{Z}}}=\varprojlim_{n}\frac{{\mathbb{Z}}}{n{\mathbb{Z}}}. Then one has

(10.8.1) ΠC/Et​e​m​p=ℤ^×ℤ.\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{C/E}=\hat{{\mathbb{Z}}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}.

So for every integer n≥1n\geq 1 one has a Galois étale cover Cn→CC_{n}\to C with Galois group ℤ/n​ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}} and Cn/KC_{n}/K is again a Tate elliptic curve. So its universal covering is (again) 𝔾m→Cn\mathbb{G}_{m}\to C_{n} and the tempered covering 𝔾m→Cn→C\mathbb{G}_{m}\to C_{n}\to C has Galois group

(10.8.2) Gn=ℤ/n​ℤ×ℤG_{n}={\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}

and one has

(10.8.3) ΠC/ℂpt​e​m​p=lim←n⁡Gn=lim←n⁡((ℤ/n​ℤ)×ℤ)=ℤ^×ℤ.\Pi^{\scriptscriptstyle temp}_{C/{\mathbb{C}}_{p}}=\varprojlim_{n}G_{n}=\varprojlim_{n}(({\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}})\times{\mathbb{Z}})=\hat{{\mathbb{Z}}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}.

Let 𝔾ma​n\mathbb{G}_{m}^{an} be the analytic space over KK associated to the affine variety 𝔾m/K\mathbb{G}_{m}/K where 𝔾m/ℂp\mathbb{G}_{m}/{\mathbb{C}}_{p} is the multiplicative group. By [Berkovich, 1990], the topological universal cover of CnC_{n} is

(10.8.4) 𝔾ma​n=Cn∞→Cn\mathbb{G}_{m}^{an}=C_{n}^{\infty}\to C_{n}

given by the Berkovich’s version of the Tate construction ([Berkovich, 1990]). Then the rigid analytic space associated to 𝔾ma​n\mathbb{G}_{m}^{an} is 𝔾ma​n,r​i​g=𝔾mr​i​g\mathbb{G}_{m}^{an,rig}=\mathbb{G}_{m}^{rig}. The rigid analytic function picture for Tate elliptic curves is discussed extensively in [Roquette, 1970].

Let K⁡(Cn∞,r​i​g)K(C_{n}^{\infty,rig}) be the function field of Cn∞,r​i​gC_{n}^{\infty,rig} (over KK). Then Mochizuki’s tempered Frobenioid which I describe below in § 10.9 can be described in terms of the divisors on the rigid analytic spaces {Cn∞,r​i​g}\{C^{\infty,rig}_{n}\} and of functions

(10.8.5) lim←n⁡K​(Cn∞,r​i​g)Gn,\varprojlim_{n}K(C_{n}^{\infty,rig})^{G_{n}},

and one can think of K​(Cn∞,r​i​g)GnK(C_{n}^{\infty,rig})^{G_{n}} as analytic functions on Cn∞,r​i​gC_{n}^{\infty,rig} with descent data with respect to the action of GnG_{n}.

§ 10.9 Mochizuki’s construction of tempered Frobenioids

Now let X/EX/E be a geometrically connected, smooth, hyperbolic curve over a pp-adic field EE. Let KK be an algebraically closed perfectoid field equipped with an isometric embedding of EE. Let XEa​nX^{an}_{E} (resp. XKa​nX^{an}_{K}) be the associated Berkovich spaces over EE and KK respectively).

§ 10.9.1 

Let me remark that by [André, 2003a, III, 1.4.10 and Remark after Definition 2.1.1] any tempered covering of Y→XKa​nY\to X^{an}_{K} is definable over a finite extension E′E^{\prime} (i.e. of the form Y=YE′Y=Y_{E^{\prime}}) of EE contained in KK and by base extension any tempered covering of YE′→XEa​nY_{E^{\prime}}\to X^{an}_{E} provides a tempered covering of XKa​nX^{an}_{K} . Hence in what follows, one can work with tempered coverings of XKa​nX^{an}_{K}.

Then for each tempered covering YE′→XEa​nY_{E^{\prime}}\to X^{an}_{E} one has the triple

(10.9.1.1) (Φt​e​m​p(Y/E′)=Div+~(Y/E′),PDiv~(YE′)⟶Φt​e​m​p(Y/E′)g​p)(\Phi_{temp}(Y/E^{\prime})=\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Y/E^{\prime}),\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Y_{E^{\prime}})\longrightarrow\Phi_{temp}(Y/E^{\prime})^{gp})

defined in § 10.7.

§ 10.9.2 

Mochizuki defines the tempered Frobenioid of X/EX/E as a category whose objects are Frobenioids of tempered coverings of X/EX/E defined in § 10.7 and with obvious morphisms between ordinary Frobenioids arising from morphisms between the curves. Mochizuki’s tempered Frobenioid is the category whose objects are (Mochizuki considers the case K=E¯^≃ℂpK=\widehat{\overline{E}}\simeq{\mathbb{C}}_{p})

(10.9.2.1) 𝔉𝔯𝔬𝔟t​e​m​p(X/E;K)={(Φt​e​m​p(Y/E′)=Div+~(YE′),PDiv~(YE′)⟶Φt​e​m​p(Z/E)g​p): where YE′→Xa​nK is a temp. covering defined over E′⊂K}\mathfrak{Frob}_{temp}(X/E;K)=\left\{(\Phi_{temp}(Y/E^{\prime})=\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Y_{E^{\prime}}),\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Y_{E^{\prime}})\longrightarrow\Phi_{temp}(Z/E)^{gp}):\text{ where }\right.\\ \qquad\left.\vphantom{\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Y_{E^{\prime}})}Y_{E^{\prime}}\to X^{an}_{K}\text{ is a temp. covering defined over }E^{\prime}\subset K\right\}

(with obvious morphisms between objects). This is equipped with a functor

(10.9.2.2) 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟t​e​m​p​(X/E,K)→Temp⁡(X/E,K)\mathfrak{Frob}_{temp}(X/E;K)\to{\rm Temp}(X/E;K)

from 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟t​e​m​p​(X/E,K)\mathfrak{Frob}_{temp}(X/E;K) to the category of tempered coverings of X/EX/E defined over finite extensions of EE contained in KK. This is given by the rule

(10.9.2.3) (Div+~(YE),Div+~(YE)g​p⟵PDiv~(YE′))⟼YE′(\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Y_{E}),\widetilde{{\rm Div_{+}}}(Y_{E})^{gp}\longleftarrow\widetilde{{\rm PDiv}}(Y_{E^{\prime}}))\longmapsto Y_{E^{\prime}}

in which one forgets the divisors but remembers the tempered covering YE′Y_{E^{\prime}} of XEa​nX^{an}_{E}. Two remarks must be made here:

Remark 10.9.2.4.

Note that for the construction of this Frobenioid one can work with the category of tempered coverings of XKa​nX^{an}_{K} because by [André, 2003a, Proof of Proposition 5.1.1] every tempered covering of XKa​nX^{an}_{K} is defined over a finite extension E′E^{\prime} of EE contained in KK. ∙\bullet

Remark 10.9.2.5.

In Mochizuki’s terminology , 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟t​e​m​p​(X/E,K)\mathfrak{Frob}_{temp}(X/E;K) is a Frobenioid over the base category of tempered coverings of XEa​nX^{an}_{E} and is the Frobenioid of [Mochizuki, 2021a, Example 3.2] (I do not use Mochizuki’s notation here). Mochizuki’s definition of this Frobenioid in [Mochizuki, 2009] does not use Berkovich’s topological universal coverings of XKa​nX^{an}_{K} and instead works with “combinatorial universal coverings” defined using formal schemes associated to the tempered coverings of the analytic space XEa​nX^{an}_{E}. But by [Berkovich, 1990], one can pass from analytic spaces to formal schemes to go back and forth between my view point and Mochizuki’s. ∙\bullet

§ 10.10 Prime-strips from Frobenioids and gluing Frobenioids by prime-strips

The following theorem is now a consequence of various results proved earlier.

Theorem 10.10.1.

Let X/LX/L be as in § 2.4. Let 𝔞​𝔯​𝔦​𝔱​𝔥​(L)𝐲\mathfrak{arith}(L)_{\bf y} be an arithmeticoid given by 𝐲=(yv)v∈𝕍L∈𝐘𝐋{\bf y}=(y_{v})_{v\in\mathbb{V}_{L}}\in\mathscrbf{Y}_{L}. Then 𝔉​𝔯​𝔬​𝔟t​e​m​p​(X/Lv,Kv)\mathfrak{Frob}_{temp}(X/L_{v};K_{v}) determines each of the prime-strips F?{F}^{?} in the Section 8.5.
